lessons.title: Prefixes 小- and 第-
lessons.summary: 小- makes a friendly or young form of a name or noun; 第- makes an ordinal number.
body: A prefix attaches to the front of a word. 小 (xiǎo) before a surname or a noun makes a friendly, often younger form: 小王, 小朋友, 小学生. 第 (dì) before a number makes an ordinal: 第一 (first), 第二 (second).
The contrast example uses the suffix 们, which attaches to the back of a word (同学们). Prefixes go in front, suffixes go behind; used as prefixes, they are bound to the word they attach to.

examples.reading: tā shì xiǎoxuéshēng.
examples.translation: He is a primary-school pupil.

examples.reading: Xiǎo Wáng shì wǒ de tóngxué.
examples.translation: Xiao Wang is my classmate.

examples.translation: This is my first book.

examples.translation: The children are singing.

examples.reading: tóngxuémen hǎo!
examples.translation: Hello, classmates!

lessons.title: Suffixes -们 and -边
lessons.summary: -们 makes a plural for people; -边 turns a position word into a place word.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 里 / 外 / 前 / 后 + 边
body: A suffix attaches to the back of a word. 们 (men) makes pronouns and person-nouns plural: 我们, 你们, 他们, 同学们, 老师们. It is not used after a number (say 三个学生, not 三个学生们).
边 (bian) attaches to a position word to make a place word: 上边, 下边, 里边, 外边, 前边, 后边. The contrast example uses the prefix 小-, which goes in front (小学生); suffixes go behind.

examples.reading: lǎoshīmen hǎo!
examples.translation: Hello, teachers!

examples.reading: háizimen xǐhuan gǒu.
examples.translation: The children like dogs.

examples.reading: shū zài zhuōzi shàngbian.
examples.translation: The book is on top of the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào wàibian yǒu yí ge shāngdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a shop outside the school.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei shì xiǎoxuéshēng.
examples.translation: My younger sister is a primary-school pupil.

lessons.title: Position nouns: 上 下 里 外 前 后
lessons.summary: Attach a position word to a noun to say where something is.
pattern: noun + 上 / 下 / 里 / 外 / 前 / 后
body: 上 (shàng, on), 下 (xià, under), 里 (lǐ, in), 外 (wài, outside), 前 (qián, front) and 后 (hòu, back) attach to a noun to make a place phrase: 桌子上, 椅子下, 家里, 学校外边. 前边 and 后边 stand alone as place words. With 在 they say where someone or something is: 书在桌子上.
The contrast example uses 在, the word that introduces the place phrase. Without 在, 我学校 is not a sentence; 在 links the subject to the place (我在学校).

examples.reading: shū zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.translation: The book is on the table.

examples.reading: māo zài yǐzi xià.
examples.translation: The cat is under the chair.

examples.reading: māma zài jiā li.
examples.translation: Mum is at home.

examples.reading: xuéxiào wàibian hěn lěng.
examples.translation: It is cold outside the school.

examples.reading: qiánbian yǒu yí ge shūdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a bookshop in front.

examples.reading: wǒ zài xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I am at school.

lessons.title: Modal verbs: 会 能 想 要 可以
lessons.summary: Put a modal before the verb to say ability, wish, need or permission.
pattern: subject + 会 / 能 / 想 / 要 / 可以 + verb
body: 会 (huì) is a learned skill (我会说汉语); 能 (néng) is ability or possibility (他能吃十个饺子); 想 (xiǎng) is a wish (我想去中国); 要 (yào) is a need or want, and can take a thing directly (我要一杯茶); 可以 (kěyǐ) is permission (你可以坐出租车).

To negate a modal, put 不 before it: 不想, 不会, 不能. The contrast example shows this. 没 cannot negate 会 (you cannot say 没会开车); at this level negate modals with 不. Above this level you will meet 没能, did not manage to. 没 negates 有 and past events.

examples.reading: wǒ huì shuō Hànyǔ.

examples.reading: wǒ yào yì bēi chá.
examples.translation: I would like a cup of tea.

examples.translation: I want to go to China.

examples.translation: You may take a taxi.

examples.translation: He can eat ten dumplings.

examples.translation: I cannot drive.

lessons.title: Separable verbs: 看病 睡觉 说话 上课 上班…
lessons.summary: These verbs already contain an object, so they cannot take another one.
pattern: verb + object inside one word: 睡 + 觉, 看 + 病, 上 + 班
body: 看病, 睡觉, 说话, 上课, 下课, 上班, 下班 and 生病 are verb-plus-object compounds: 睡 (sleep) + 觉, 看 (see) + 病 (illness), 上 (go to) + 班 (work). Because the object is already inside, they cannot take another object or a duration after the whole word.
Put a duration or 了 inside: 睡了八个小时 (not 睡觉了八个小时), 上了课, 看了病. To add an object, use the plain verb: 看医生, not 看病医生. The contrast example shows the plain verb 看 taking the object 医生.

examples.reading: bàba jīntiān shàngbān.
examples.translation: Dad is going to work today.

examples.reading: wǒ shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: I slept for eight hours.

examples.reading: tā shēngbìng le.
examples.translation: He has fallen ill.

examples.reading: wǒ qù kàn yīshēng.
examples.translation: I am going to see a doctor.

lessons.title: Question words: 什么 谁 哪 几 多少 怎么…
lessons.summary: Ask with a question word in the position of the answer; the word order does not change.
pattern: … + 什么 / 谁 / 哪 / 几 / 多少 / 怎么 / 哪儿 + …？
body: 什么 (what), 谁 (who), 哪 (which), 哪儿 / 哪里 (where), 哪些 (which ones), 几 (how many, small), 多少 (how many, any), 多 (how, before an adjective: 多大), 怎么 (how) and 怎么样 (how about) ask for a specific answer. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你叫什么名字？

几 is for small numbers and needs a measure word (几口人); 多少 is for any number (多少钱). The contrast example uses 吗, which makes a yes-no question instead; do not add 吗 to a question that already has a question word (you cannot say 你叫什么吗？).

examples.reading: nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
examples.translation: What is your name?

examples.reading: nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén?

examples.reading: zhè běn shū duōshao qián?
examples.translation: How much is this book?

examples.translation: Which country are you from?

examples.translation: Who is on the phone?

examples.translation: Where are you going?

lessons.title: Personal pronouns: 我 你 您 他 她 它 大家…
lessons.summary: Pronouns stand for people and things; 您 is polite, 它 is for things, 大家 addresses everyone.
pattern: 我 / 你 / 您 / 他 / 她 / 它 (+ 们)
body: 我 (I), 你 (you), 您 (you, polite), 他 (he), 她 (she), 它 (it) and their plurals with 们 (我们, 你们, 他们, 她们, 它们) stand for people and things. 您 shows respect (to a teacher or an older person). 它 is for things and animals. 大家 means everyone.

A singular pronoun cannot be summed up by 都: say 我们都去, not 我都去. The contrast example uses the suffix 们, which makes the plural (同学们); a number already gives the plural, so do not add 们 after it (三个学生, not 三个学生们).

examples.reading: wǒmen dōu shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: We are all students.

examples.reading: tāmen dōu hěn máng.
examples.translation: They are all busy.

examples.reading: lǎoshī, nín hǎo!
examples.translation: Hello, teacher!

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yì zhī māo, tā hěn piàoliang.
examples.translation: I have a cat; it is pretty.

examples.text: 我姐姐是医生，她在医院工作。

examples.translation: My older sister is a doctor; she works in a hospital.

lessons.title: Demonstratives: 这 那 这儿 这些 有的…
lessons.summary: Point near (这) or far (那); 这儿/那儿 are places, 这些/那些 plural, 有的/有些 mean some.
pattern: 这 / 那 (+ 个 / 些 / 儿 / 里)
body: 这 (zhè, this) points near, 那 (nà, that) points far. 这儿 / 这里 and 那儿 / 那里 are places; 这个 / 那个 and 这些 / 那些 point to one or several things; 有的 and 有些 mean some (有的学生). A measure word usually follows 这 / 那 before a noun: 这本书, 那个电影.
The contrast example uses the question word 哪 (which), which asks rather than points and also needs a measure word (哪本书). 这 / 那 point; 哪 asks.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ de shū.
examples.translation: This is my book.

examples.reading: nàxiē píngguǒ hěn piányi.
examples.translation: Those apples are cheap.

examples.reading: zhèr yǒu yí ge shūdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a bookshop here.

examples.reading: yǒude xuéshēng xǐhuan kàn shū.
examples.translation: Some students like reading.

examples.reading: nàge diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: That film is good.

examples.reading: nǐ yào mǎi nǎ běn shū?
examples.translation: Which book do you want to buy?

lessons.title: Numerals: 一 二/两 三…十 百 千 半 零
lessons.summary: Count with numerals; use 两 (not 二) before a measure word, and 半 for half.
body: 一, 二, 三, 四, 五, 六, 七, 八, 九, 十, 百, 千 and 零 are the numerals. Before a measure word, two is 两, not 二: 两个人, 两本书. 二 is used inside numbers: 十二, 二十. 半 (bàn) means half: 半个苹果, 两点半. 零 marks an empty digit.

The contrast example uses the prefix 第, which makes an ordinal (第一 = first), not a count. 一 reads yī alone, at the end of a number (十一) and in ordinals (第一 dì-yī, 第一本 dì-yī běn, 第一个 dì-yī ge); before another syllable in a count it changes: yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí ge), yì before other tones (一本 yì běn).

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu liǎng ge jiějie.
examples.translation: I have two older sisters.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei shí'èr suì.
examples.translation: My younger sister is twelve.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le bàn ge píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I ate half an apple.

examples.reading: zhège shǒujī yì qiān yuán.
examples.translation: This phone costs a thousand yuan.

examples.reading: wǒ yì tiān chī sān ge píngguǒ.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒ de dì-yī ge péngyou.
examples.translation: He is my first friend.

lessons.title: Measure words: 本 个 家 口 块 件 只 元 杯
lessons.summary: A number or 这/那 needs a measure word before the noun; each noun takes its own.
pattern: numeral / 这 / 那 + measure word + noun
body: Between a number (or 这, 那, 几) and a noun, Chinese needs a measure word: 本 for books (一本书), 个 the general one (一个人), 家 for shops and families (两家饭店), 口 for family members (三口人), 块 for money and pieces (二十块), 件 for clothes and matters (一件衣服), 只 for animals (一只猫), 元 for money (formal). 杯 is borrowed from 杯子 for cups of drink (一杯茶).
The contrast example shows 两 before a measure word: before a measure word, two is 两, not 二 (两本书, not 二本书).

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I'll buy a book.

examples.reading: tā jiā yǒu sān zhī māo.
examples.translation: His family has three cats.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu sān kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are three people in my family.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piàoliang.
examples.translation: This dress is very pretty.

examples.reading: wǒ hē le yì bēi chá.
examples.translation: I drank a cup of tea.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yí ge dìdi.
examples.translation: I have a younger brother.

examples.reading: zhèlǐ yǒu liǎng jiā fàndiàn.
examples.translation: There are two restaurants here.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi liǎng běn shū.
examples.translation: I'll buy two books.

lessons.title: Time measure words: 日 号 岁 点 分 年 天
lessons.summary: Count dates, ages, clock time and durations with time measure words.
pattern: numeral + 岁 / 点 / 分 / 年 / 天 / 号 / 日
body: 岁 (suì) counts age (五岁); 号 and 日 name the day of the month (三月五号 / 三月五日); 点 and 分 tell the clock (八点, 八点十分); 年 and 天 count duration (一年, 三天). After a number, 年 and 天 need no extra measure word, but 月 takes 个 (三个月).
The contrast example uses 半 (half): 八点半 is half past eight, 半小时 is half an hour. 半 is a numeral, not a measure word.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei wǔ suì.
examples.translation: My younger sister is five.

examples.reading: jīntiān sān yuè wǔ hào.
examples.translation: Today is the fifth of March.

examples.reading: xiànzài bā diǎn.
examples.translation: It is eight o'clock.

examples.reading: wǒ xué le yì nián Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: I studied Chinese for a year.

examples.reading: wǒ yì tiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: I work eight hours a day.

examples.reading: xiànzài bā diǎn bàn.
examples.translation: It is half past eight.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs: 非常 很 太 真 有点儿
lessons.summary: Put a degree adverb before an adjective; 太…了 exclamates, 有点儿 often signals a complaint.
pattern: subject + 非常 / 很 / 太 / 真 / 有点儿 + adjective
body: 非常 (fēicháng, very), 很 (hěn, very), 太 (tài, too), 真 (zhēn, really) and 有点儿 (yǒudiǎnr, a bit) go before an adjective: 非常热, 很好, 太贵了, 真好, 有点儿忙. 太 usually pairs with 了 to exclaim. 有点儿 often marks something unwanted.

The contrast example uses 一点儿, which measures a quantity of a thing (喝一点儿水) or follows a verb; it does not go before an adjective (you cannot say 一点儿忙). 有点儿 goes before an adjective; 一点儿 goes with a noun.

examples.reading: jīntiān fēicháng rè.
examples.translation: It is very hot today.

examples.reading: zhège diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: This film is good.

examples.reading: tài guì le!
examples.translation: Too expensive!

examples.reading: nǐ zhēn hǎo!
examples.translation: You are really kind!

examples.reading: wǒ yǒudiǎnr máng.
examples.translation: I am a bit busy.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng hē yìdiǎnr shuǐ.
examples.translation: I would like to drink a little water.

lessons.title: 都: all, both
lessons.summary: 都 sums up the plural subject or the object placed before it; it comes before the verb.
body: 都 (dōu, all, both) sums up what comes before it: a plural subject (我们都去) or an object moved to the front (这些书我都看了). It stands after the subject and before the verb, never at the end.
The contrast example uses 也 (also), which adds one more rather than summing up all. With a singular subject, 都 is wrong (他都很忙 is not said); 也 is fine (他也很忙). When both appear, 也 comes first: 我们也都去.

examples.reading: wǒmen dōu shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: We are all students.

examples.reading: tāmen dōu hěn máng.
examples.translation: They are all busy.

examples.reading: zhèxiē shū wǒ dōu kàn le.
examples.translation: I have read all these books.

examples.reading: dàjiā dōu bú rènshi tā.
examples.translation: Nobody knows him.

examples.reading: tā yě hěn máng.
examples.translation: He is busy too.

lessons.title: 在 and 正在: action in progress
lessons.summary: Put 在 or 正在 before the verb to say an action is happening now.
body: 在 (zài) and 正在 (zhèngzài) before a verb mark an action in progress: 我在吃饭, 妈妈正在做饭. 正在 stresses right now. This 在 is an adverb, different from the 在 that says where someone is (我在家).
The contrast example uses sentence-final 呢, which also marks an ongoing action (我吃饭呢) and can stand without 在. 了 marks a completed action, not an ongoing one.

examples.reading: wǒ zài chī fàn.
examples.translation: I am eating.

examples.reading: māma zhèngzài zuò fàn.
examples.translation: Mum is cooking.

examples.reading: tā zài kàn shū.
examples.translation: He is reading.

examples.reading: dìdi zhèngzài shuìjiào.
examples.translation: My younger brother is sleeping.

examples.reading: wǒ chī fàn ne.
examples.translation: I am eating.

lessons.title: 再: again, once more
lessons.summary: 再 before a verb says an action will happen again; it is for future repeats.
body: 再 (zài, again) before a verb says the action will repeat: 请再说一下, 我明天再来. It is used for future or intended repeats, not for a state that continues.

The contrast example uses 还 (still, more), which says a state continues or something is added. For still or in addition want, use 还, not 再: 我还想买一本书. 再 is for a future repeat of an action (再来, 再说一下). Do not confuse 再 with 在, which marks an action in progress.

examples.reading: qǐng zài shuō yíxià.
examples.translation: Please say it again.

examples.reading: wǒ míngtiān zài lái.
examples.translation: I will come again tomorrow.

examples.reading: nǐ zài chī yí ge bāozi ba.
examples.translation: Have another bun.

examples.reading: wǒmen zài kàn yí ge diànyǐng.
examples.translation: Let us watch another film.

examples.reading: wǒ hái xiǎng mǎi yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I still want to buy a book.

lessons.title: 还 and 也: also, still, more
lessons.summary: 也 adds (also); 还 adds more or says still; both come before the verb.
body: 也 (yě, also) adds one more of the same: 我也喜欢猫. 还 (hái, still, more) says a state continues or something is added: 他还有一个妹妹, 我还想喝茶. Both stand after the subject and before the verb.

The contrast example uses 都 (all), which sums up every member rather than adding one. When 也 and 都 appear together, 也 comes first: 我们也都想去. Do not put 也 or 还 after the verb or at the end of the sentence.

examples.reading: wǒ yě xǐhuan māo.
examples.translation: I like cats too.

examples.reading: tā hái yǒu yí ge mèimei.
examples.translation: He also has a younger sister.

examples.reading: wǒmen yě dōu xiǎng qù.
examples.translation: We all want to go too.

examples.text: 苹果很好吃，饺子也很好吃。
examples.reading: píngguǒ hěn hǎochī, jiǎozi yě hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: Apples are tasty, and dumplings are tasty too.

examples.reading: tóngxuémen dōu lái le.
examples.translation: The classmates have all come.

lessons.title: Negation: 不 没(有) 不要
lessons.summary: 不 negates verbs and adjectives; 没(有) negates 有 and past events; 不要 forbids.
body: 不 (bù) negates a verb or adjective (我不喝茶, 今天不冷); before a fourth tone it is said bú (不是 bú shì). 没 / 没有 (méi / méiyǒu) negates 有 (我没有手机) and says a past event did not happen (昨天我没去学校). 不要 (bú yào) forbids: 请不要说话.

For a past event use 没, not 不, and drop 了 (我没吃饭, not 没吃了饭). The contrast example uses sentence-final 了 with 不 to mark a change of plan: 我不去了 (I am not going anymore). Do not put 了 right after a verb negated with 没. (不 occasionally appears in a past context with a refusing meaning, but at this level always use 没 for the past.)

examples.reading: wǒ míngtiān bù hē chá.
examples.translation: I will not drink tea tomorrow.

examples.reading: zuótiān wǒ méi qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I did not go to school yesterday.

examples.reading: qǐng bú yào shuōhuà.
examples.translation: Please do not talk.

examples.reading: tā méiyǒu shǒujī.
examples.translation: He does not have a phone.

examples.reading: wǒ jīntiān bù xiǎng shàngbān.
examples.translation: I do not want to go to work today.

examples.reading: wǒ bú qù le.
examples.translation: I am not going anymore.

lessons.title: 在: introducing time and place
lessons.summary: 在 + place comes before the verb to say where an action happens; time words also come before the verb.
body: The preposition 在 (zài) introduces a place before the verb: 我在家吃饭, 他在学校学习. A time word also comes before the verb: 我上午在医院看病. The place and time go before the action, not after it.

The contrast example uses the adverb 正在, which marks an action in progress (姐姐正在看电视), not a place. 在 can also be the verb to be at (我在家); here it is a preposition introducing where the action happens.

examples.reading: wǒ zài jiā chī fàn.
examples.translation: I eat at home.

examples.reading: tā zài xuéxiào xuéxí.
examples.translation: He studies at school.

examples.reading: wǒmen zài fàndiàn chī wǎnfàn.
examples.translation: We have dinner at a restaurant.

examples.reading: wǒ shàngwǔ zài yīyuàn kànbìng.
examples.translation: I see a doctor at the hospital in the morning.

examples.reading: jiějie zhèngzài kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: My older sister is watching TV.

lessons.title: Prepositions 和 and 对: introducing a person
lessons.summary: 和 introduces a companion (with); 对 introduces the target of an attitude (toward).
body: The preposition 和 (hé, with) introduces a companion before the verb: 我和他一起去学校. 对 (duì, toward) introduces the target of an attitude: 妈妈对我很好. Both come before the verb or adjective.

The contrast example uses 和 as a conjunction joining two nouns (苹果和饺子). As a preposition 和 means with and is followed by a verb phrase (我和朋友去); as a conjunction it joins two things into one unit (我喜欢苹果和饺子).

examples.reading: wǒ hé tā yìqǐ qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I go to school with him.

examples.reading: māma duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: Mum is very kind to me.

examples.reading: wǒ hé jiějie zhù yí ge fángjiān.
examples.translation: I share a room with my older sister.

examples.reading: lǎoshī duì wǒmen hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: The teacher is very kind to us.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan píngguǒ hé jiǎozi.
examples.translation: I like apples and dumplings.

lessons.title: 和: joining words and phrases
lessons.summary: The conjunction 和 joins two nouns or phrases into one unit; it does not join sentences.
body: The conjunction 和 (hé, and) joins two nouns or phrases into one unit: 我和妹妹都喜欢猫, 我喜欢看书和写字. The joined unit acts as one subject or object.

The contrast example uses 和 as a preposition meaning with (我和朋友去电影院 = I go with friends). As a conjunction 和 joins two equal things; as a preposition it introduces a companion before a verb. 和 does not join two sentences (you cannot say 我去商店和我买书).

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei dōu xǐhuan māo.
examples.translation: My younger sister and I both like cats.

examples.text: 爸爸和妈妈都在公司工作。
examples.reading: bàba hé māma dōu zài gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Dad and Mum both work at a company.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū hé xiě zì.
examples.translation: I like reading and writing.

examples.text: 这本书和那本书都很好。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū hé nà běn shū dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: This book and that book are both good.

examples.reading: wǒ hé péngyou qù diànyǐngyuàn.
examples.translation: I go to the cinema with a friend.

lessons.title: 的: linking a modifier to a noun
lessons.summary: 的 links an owner, adjective or clause to the noun it modifies.
body: 的 (de) links a modifier to a noun: possession (我的书), an adjective (大的苹果), or a clause (他写的字). With close people and groups it is often left out: 我妈妈, 我们学校.

The contrast example uses 得, which links a verb to a complement describing how the action is done (他说得很好). 的 goes before a noun; 得 goes after a verb. Do not use 的 to introduce a complement (说得好, not 说的很好).

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ de shū.
examples.translation: This is my book.

examples.reading: lǎoshī de diànnǎo hěn xīn.
examples.translation: The teacher's computer is new.

examples.text: 我喜欢大的苹果，不喜欢小苹果。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan dà de píngguǒ, bù xǐhuan xiǎo píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I like big apples, not small ones.

examples.reading: zhè shì māma de diànhuà.
examples.translation: This is Mum's phone.

examples.reading: tā xiě de zì hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The characters he writes look nice.

examples.reading: tā shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He speaks well.

lessons.title: 了: a completed action
lessons.summary: 了 after a verb marks that the action happened or is complete.
body: 了 (le) right after a verb marks a completed action: 我买了一本书, 他吃了三个饺子. To say it did not happen, use 没 and drop 了: 我没买.

The contrast example uses 过, which marks experience rather than a specific completed event (我没去过中国 = I have never been to China). After 没 use 过 for never (没去过), not 了 (you cannot say 没去了中国). 了 is for a specific finished action; 过 is for life experience.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I bought a book.

examples.reading: tā chī le sān ge jiǎozi.
examples.translation: He ate three dumplings.

examples.reading: wǒmen kàn le yí ge diànyǐng.
examples.translation: We watched a film.

examples.reading: mèimei hē le yì bēi niúnǎi.
examples.translation: My younger sister drank a glass of milk.

examples.reading: wǒ méi qùguo Zhōngguó.
examples.translation: I have never been to China.

lessons.title: Particles 吗 and 吧: questions and suggestions
lessons.summary: 吗 makes a yes-no question; 吧 makes a suggestion or a guess.
body: 吗 (ma) turns a statement into a yes-no question without changing the word order: 你是学生吗？ 吧 (ba) makes a suggestion (我们回家吧！= let us go home) or a guess (你是老师吧？= you are a teacher, right?).

The contrast example uses 呢, which cannot make a yes-no question. 呢 asks what about someone or something after a noun (我很好，你呢？= I am fine, and you?). Use 吗 for a yes-no question, 吧 for a suggestion or guess, 呢 for a follow-up.

examples.reading: tā shì nǐ gēge ma?
examples.translation: Is he your older brother?

examples.reading: nǐ xǐhuan māo ma?
examples.translation: Do you like cats?

examples.reading: wǒmen huí jiā ba!
examples.translation: Let us go home!

examples.reading: nǐ shì lǎoshī ba?
examples.translation: You are a teacher, right?

examples.reading: wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?
examples.translation: I am fine, and you?

lessons.title: Particles 了 and 呢: change and ongoing
lessons.summary: Sentence-final 了 announces a new situation; 呢 marks an ongoing action or softens a question.
body: At the end of a sentence 了 (le) announces that the situation has changed or come about: 下雨了 (it has started raining), 他会开车了 (he can drive now). 呢 (ne) marks an ongoing action (我吃饭呢 = I am eating) or softens a question with a question word (你在做什么呢？).

The contrast example uses 吗, which asks a yes-no question (你是医生吗？). 吗 does not combine with a question word or with 呢 (you cannot say 你在做什么吗？). Sentence-final 了 states a change; 呢 marks ongoing or a follow-up; 吗 asks yes-no.

examples.reading: xià yǔ le.
examples.translation: It has started raining.

examples.reading: tā huì kāi chē le.
examples.translation: He can drive now.

examples.reading: tā dǎ diànhuà ne.
examples.translation: He is on the phone.

examples.reading: nǐ zài zuò shénme ne?
examples.translation: What are you doing?

examples.reading: mèimei shuìjiào ne.
examples.translation: My younger sister is sleeping.

examples.reading: nǐ shì yīshēng ma?
examples.translation: Are you a doctor?

lessons.title: 喂: hello on the phone
lessons.summary: 喂 is an interjection used to answer the phone or get someone's attention; it stands alone.
body: 喂 (wèi) is an interjection: it answers the phone or calls for attention (喂，你好！). It stands at the start, separated by a comma, and is not part of the sentence that follows. When answering the phone, many speakers say it with a rising tone, wéi; the dictionary lists wèi, and both are accepted.
The contrast example uses 请, which makes a polite request (请坐 = please sit). 喂 calls for attention; 请 asks someone politely to do something. Neither is a verb inside the sentence.

examples.reading: wèi, nǐ hǎo!
examples.translation: Hello! (on the phone)

examples.reading: wèi, qǐngwèn tā zài ma?
examples.translation: Hello, may I ask if he is in?

examples.reading: wèi, nǐ zhǎo shéi?
examples.translation: Hello, who are you looking for?

examples.reading: wèi, wǒmen míngtiān jiàn!
examples.translation: Hey, see you tomorrow!

examples.reading: qǐng zuò.
examples.translation: Please sit.

lessons.title: Basic phrase types: coordinate, modifier-head, verb-object, subject-predicate
lessons.summary: Phrases combine words: A和B, modifier+的+noun, verb+object, and subject+predicate.
body: Four basic phrase types: coordinate (我和妹妹, joined by 和), modifier-head (我的新书, a modifier before a noun), verb-object (看电影, a verb plus its object), and subject-predicate (他很好, a subject plus a predicate). Phrases combine into sentences.

The contrast example uses a preposition-object phrase (在家), which is an other type (next lesson): a preposition plus its object, used before a verb. The four basic types build the core of a sentence; preposition-object and place phrases modify it.

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: My younger sister and I go to school.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ de xīn shū.
examples.translation: This is my new book.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: I like watching films.

examples.reading: wǒ juéde tā hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: I think he is very good.

examples.reading: māma zài jiā kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Mum watches TV at home.

lessons.title: Other phrase types: numeral-measure, preposition-object, place
lessons.summary: A numeral-measure phrase counts; a preposition-object phrase and a place phrase modify the verb.
body: Three other phrase types: numeral-measure (三本书, a number plus a measure word), preposition-object (在学校, 对我, a preposition plus its object), and place (桌子上, 家里, a noun plus a position word). They usually modify the verb or count a noun.
The contrast example uses a modifier-head phrase (弟弟的杯子), a basic type: a modifier before a noun. A numeral-measure phrase counts a noun; a modifier-head phrase describes whose or which noun it is.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi sān běn shū.
examples.translation: I'll buy three books.

examples.reading: tā zài xuéxiào kàn shū.
examples.translation: He reads at school.

examples.reading: shǒujī zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.translation: The phone is on the table.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are five people in my family.

examples.reading: nà shì dìdi de bēizi.
examples.translation: That is my younger brother's cup.

lessons.title: The subject: who or what the sentence is about
lessons.summary: A noun, pronoun or noun phrase can be the subject, before the predicate.
body: The subject is who or what the sentence is about. A noun (爸爸), a pronoun (我) or a noun phrase (我的老师, 这个商店) can be the subject. It comes before the predicate.
The contrast example uses the adverb 都, which is not part of the subject: it comes after the subject and before the verb (我们都喜欢他). Do not put 都 before the subject.

examples.reading: wǒ shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: I am a student.

examples.reading: bàba xǐhuan hē chá.
examples.translation: Dad likes drinking tea.

examples.reading: wǒ de lǎoshī hěn máng.
examples.translation: My teacher is busy.

examples.reading: zhège shāngdiàn hěn dà.
examples.translation: This shop is big.

examples.reading: wǒmen dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.translation: We all like him.

lessons.title: The predicate: what the subject does or is
lessons.summary: A verb, adjective or numeral-measure phrase can be the predicate; a noun predicate needs 是.
body: The predicate says what the subject does or is. A verb or verb phrase (吃米饭, 学习汉语), an adjective or adjective phrase (很冷), or a numeral-measure phrase (三岁) can be the predicate without 是.
The contrast example uses 是 for a noun predicate (他是医生). A noun cannot be the predicate on its own (you cannot say 他医生); it needs 是. An adjective does not take 是 (you cannot say 我是忙).

examples.reading: wǒ chī mǐfàn.
examples.translation: I eat rice.

examples.reading: jīntiān hěn lěng.
examples.translation: It is cold today.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei sān suì.
examples.translation: My younger sister is three.

examples.reading: tā xuéxí Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: He studies Chinese.

examples.reading: tā shì yīshēng.
examples.translation: He is a doctor.

lessons.title: The object: what the action reaches
lessons.summary: A noun, pronoun or noun phrase can be the object, after the verb.
body: The object is what the action reaches. A noun (书), a pronoun (我) or a noun phrase (我的学校) can be the object. It comes after the verb: 看书, 认识我, 喜欢我的学校.
The contrast example uses a place phrase with 在, which comes before the verb, not as an object (弟弟在房间睡觉, not 弟弟睡觉在房间). Some verbs (睡觉, 上班) already contain their object and cannot take another.

examples.reading: wǒ kàn shū.
examples.translation: I read.

examples.reading: tā rènshi wǒ.
examples.translation: He knows me.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan wǒ de xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I like my school.

examples.reading: māma zuò wǎnfàn.
examples.translation: Mum makes dinner.

examples.reading: dìdi zài fángjiān shuìjiào.
examples.translation: My younger brother sleeps in the room.

lessons.title: The attributive: modifying a noun
lessons.summary: A noun word, adjective or numeral-measure phrase can modify a noun, often with 的.
body: The attributive modifies a noun: a noun word with 的 (我的书), an adjective (大苹果), or a numeral-measure phrase (两个姐姐). Some noun attributives drop 的 (汉语书, 我妈妈).
The contrast example uses 得, which introduces a complement after a verb (他汉语说得很好), not an attributive before a noun. 的 links a modifier to a noun; 得 links a verb to a complement.

examples.reading: nà shì māma de xīn yīfu.
examples.translation: Those are Mum's new clothes.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan dà píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I like big apples.

examples.reading: tā yǒu liǎng ge jiějie.
examples.translation: He has two older sisters.

examples.reading: zhè shì Hànyǔ shū.
examples.translation: This is a Chinese-language book.

examples.reading: tā Hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He speaks Chinese well.

lessons.title: The adverbial: modifying the verb
lessons.summary: An adverb, time word or place phrase can modify the verb, before it.
body: The adverbial modifies the verb or adjective: an adverb (很忙, 非常喜欢), a time word (明天去), or a place phrase (在家吃饭). It comes before the verb.

The contrast example uses 的, which links an attributive to a noun (姐姐的新手机), not an adverbial to a verb. An adverbial modifies the action; an attributive modifies a thing. Do not put the time or place after the verb.

examples.reading: wǒ hěn máng.
examples.translation: I am busy.

examples.reading: wǒ míngtiān qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I go to school tomorrow.

examples.reading: wǒmen zài jiā chī fàn.
examples.translation: We eat at home.

examples.reading: tā fēicháng xǐhuan māo.
examples.translation: He likes cats very much.

examples.reading: zhè shì jiějie de xīn shǒujī.
examples.translation: This is my older sister's new phone.

lessons.title: Action-measure complement: counting an action
lessons.summary: 一下 (and 一次) after a verb counts how many times the action happens.
body: An action-measure complement counts occurrences of an action: 看一下, 问了一下. 一下 means once, a short try; 了 goes between the verb and 一下 (我看了一下). 一次 also means one time.
The contrast example uses 一点儿, which measures a quantity of a thing (喝一点儿水), not occurrences of an action. 一下 counts the action; 一点儿 measures the thing.

examples.reading: wǒ kàn le yíxià.
examples.translation: I took a look.

examples.reading: nǐ lái kàn yíxià.
examples.translation: Come and take a look.

examples.reading: wǒ wèn le yíxià lǎoshī.
examples.translation: I asked the teacher.

examples.reading: wǒ qù le yí cì yīyuàn.
examples.translation: I went to the hospital once.

examples.reading: wǒ hē yìdiǎnr shuǐ.
examples.translation: I drink a little water.

lessons.title: Simple sentences: four predicate types
lessons.summary: A simple sentence has a verb, adjective, noun or no-subject predicate.
body: Four simple-sentence types by predicate: verb-predicate (他喜欢狗), adjective-predicate (今天天气很好), noun-predicate (今天星期三 — no 是 needed for dates and age), and non-subject-predicate (下雨了 — no subject).
The contrast example uses 是 for an identity sentence (我是学生). A noun-predicate sentence about date or age needs no 是; an identity or category sentence does need 是.

examples.reading: tā xǐhuan gǒu.
examples.translation: He likes dogs.

examples.reading: jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: The weather is fine today.

examples.reading: jīntiān xīngqīsān.
examples.translation: Today is Wednesday.

examples.reading: xià yǔ le.
examples.translation: It is raining.

examples.reading: wǒ shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: I am a student.

lessons.title: Declarative sentences: stating a fact
lessons.summary: A declarative states a fact with normal word order and ends in a period.
body: A declarative sentence states a fact: 我是学生, 他喜欢喝茶, 今天不冷. The word order is subject then predicate, and it ends in a period (。).

The contrast example uses 吗, which turns the same statement into a yes-no question (你会开车吗？) ending in a question mark. Adding 吗 changes a fact into a question; do not add it to a sentence you mean as a statement.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: My younger sister is a student.

examples.reading: tā xǐhuan hē chá.
examples.translation: He likes drinking tea.

examples.reading: jīntiān bù lěng.
examples.translation: It is not cold today.

examples.reading: wǒ méiyǒu dìdi.
examples.translation: I do not have a younger brother.

examples.reading: nǐ huì kāi chē ma?
examples.translation: Can you drive?

lessons.title: Question types: yes-no, wh-, affirmative-negative
lessons.summary: Ask with 吗 (yes-no), a question word (wh-), or verb-not-verb (affirmative-negative).
body: Three question types: yes-no with 吗 (你是老师吗？), wh- with a question word in the answer position (你喝什么？, 这是谁的书？), and affirmative-negative with verb-not-verb (你去不去学校？). The affirmative-negative form does not take 吗.

The contrast example uses 呢 for a follow-up question (我喜欢猫，你呢？= and you?). 呢 asks what about someone; it is not a yes-no, wh- or affirmative-negative question. Do not add 吗 to a wh- or affirmative-negative question.

examples.reading: nǐ shì lǎoshī ma?
examples.translation: Are you a teacher?

examples.reading: nǐ hē shénme?
examples.translation: What will you drink?

examples.reading: nǐ qù bu qù xuéxiào?
examples.translation: Are you going to school?

examples.reading: zhè shì shéi de shū?
examples.translation: Whose book is this?

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan māo, nǐ ne?
examples.translation: I like cats; what about you?

lessons.title: Imperative sentences: requests and commands
lessons.summary: 请 + verb makes a polite request; 不要 + verb forbids; the subject is often omitted.
body: An imperative gives a command or request. 请 (qǐng, please) makes it polite: 请大家坐, 请喝茶. 不要 (bú yào, do not) forbids: 不要说话, 不要看电视. The subject is usually left out.
The contrast example uses 吧, which softens a command into a suggestion (我们吃饭吧！= let us eat). 请 and 不要 address the listener directly; 吧 proposes doing something together.

examples.reading: qǐng dàjiā zuò.
examples.translation: Please sit down, everyone.

examples.reading: bú yào shuōhuà.
examples.translation: Do not talk.

examples.reading: qǐng hē chá.
examples.translation: Please have some tea.

examples.reading: bú yào kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Do not watch television.

examples.reading: wǒmen chī fàn ba!
examples.translation: Let's eat!

lessons.title: Exclamative sentences: strong feeling
lessons.summary: 太…了！, 真…！ and 好…！ express strong feeling and end in an exclamation mark.
body: An exclamative expresses strong feeling: 太 + adjective + 了 (太好了！, 太热了！), 真 + adjective (真漂亮！), or 好 + adjective (好大的苹果！). It ends in an exclamation mark (！).
The contrast example uses 很 in a plain statement (今天很热。), which just describes without strong feeling. 太 usually needs 了 to exclaim; a bare 太热 is incomplete. 很 states a degree; 太 and 真 exclaim.

examples.reading: tài hǎo le!
examples.translation: Great!

examples.reading: zhēn piàoliang!
examples.translation: How pretty!

examples.reading: tài rè le!
examples.translation: Too hot!

examples.reading: hǎo dà de píngguǒ!
examples.translation: What a big apple!

examples.reading: jīntiān hěn rè.
examples.translation: It is hot today.

lessons.title: 是: A is B (identity or category)
lessons.summary: 是 links two nouns to say A is B; its negative is 不是.
body: 是 (shì) links two nouns to say A is B, an identity or category: 我是学生, 他是医生, 这是我的书. To negate, put 不 before it: 不是 (bú shì).
The contrast example uses 很 with an adjective (今天很冷). An adjective is a predicate on its own and does not take 是 (you cannot say 我是忙); 是 is for linking nouns, 很 is for describing with an adjective.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒ de tóngxué.
examples.translation: He is my classmate.

examples.reading: wǒ shì Zhōngguórén.
examples.translation: I am Chinese.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ de shū.
examples.translation: This is my book.

examples.reading: tā bú shì lǎoshī.
examples.translation: She is not a teacher.

examples.reading: jīntiān hěn lěng.
examples.translation: It is cold today.

lessons.title: 有: possession
lessons.summary: 有 says someone has something; its negative is 没有, never 不有.
body: 有 (yǒu) says someone has something: 我有一个哥哥, 她有两只猫. Its negative is 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有.
The contrast example uses 是 for identity (他是学生 = he is a student). 有 says what someone has (我有书); 是 says what someone or something is (这是书). Do not use 是 for possession or 有 for identity.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge.
examples.translation: I have an older brother.

examples.reading: tā méiyǒu chē.
examples.translation: He does not have a car.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén.
examples.translation: There are five people in my family.

examples.reading: tā yǒu liǎng zhī māo.
examples.translation: She has two cats.

examples.reading: tā shì wǒ jiějie.
examples.translation: She is my older sister.

lessons.title: Existential sentences: what is at a place
lessons.summary: Place + 是 + noun identifies; place + 有 + numeral-measure + noun says what exists there.
body: An existential sentence introduces what is at a place. Place + 是 + noun identifies it (前边是一个书店); place + 有 + numeral-measure + noun says what exists there (桌子上有三本书).

The contrast example uses 在 with the thing first (书在桌子上), which says where the book is. An existential sentence puts the place first and introduces the thing; a 在 sentence puts the thing first and gives its place.

examples.reading: qiánbian shì yí ge shūdiàn.
examples.translation: In front is a bookshop.

examples.reading: qiánbian yǒu yí ge lǎoshī.
examples.translation: There is a teacher in front.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng yǒu sān běn shū.
examples.translation: There are three books on the table.

examples.reading: xuéxiào wàibian yǒu yí ge shāngdiàn.
examples.translation: There is a shop outside the school.

examples.reading: shū zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.translation: The book is on the table.

lessons.title: Serial-verb sentences: purpose or manner
lessons.summary: Two verbs share one subject: the second is the purpose of the first, or the first is the manner of the second.
body: In a serial-verb sentence two verbs share one subject and happen in order. The second action is the purpose of the first (我去商店买书 = I go to the shop to buy books); or the first is the manner of the second (他坐出租车去学校 = he goes to school by taxi).

The contrast example uses the preposition 和 (我和朋友去书店 = I go with a friend), which introduces a companion, not a second action. A serial-verb sentence has two actions by one subject; a 和 phrase has one action with a companion.

examples.reading: wǒ qù shāngdiàn mǎi shū.
examples.translation: I go to the shop to buy books.

examples.reading: tā zuò chūzūchē qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: He goes to school by taxi.

examples.reading: māma qù yīyuàn kànbìng.
examples.translation: Mum goes to the hospital to see a doctor.

examples.reading: tā kāi chē qù gōngsī.
examples.translation: He drives to the company.

examples.reading: wǒ hé péngyou qù shūdiàn.
examples.translation: I go to the bookshop with a friend.

lessons.title: Double-object sentences: verb + person + thing
lessons.summary: Some verbs take two objects: a person first, then a thing (给我一本书).
body: Some verbs take two objects: a person (the receiver) first, then a thing (what is given or asked). 给 (gěi, give): 我给你一本书. 问 (wèn, ask): 老师问我问题. The person comes before the thing.

The contrast example uses the preposition 对 (爸爸对我很好), which introduces the target of an attitude, not a transferred thing. A double-object verb transfers or asks something; 对 just points to whom an attitude is directed.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I'll give you a book.

examples.reading: wǒ wèn nǐ yí jiàn shì.
examples.translation: Let me ask you something.

examples.reading: bàba gěi wǒ qián.
examples.translation: Dad gives me money.

examples.reading: tā wèn wǒ jiào shénme míngzi.
examples.translation: He asks me what my name is.

examples.reading: bàba duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: Dad is very kind to me.

lessons.title: Coordinate clauses: …也…, …还…
lessons.summary: Two statements are joined by a comma with 也 or 还 in the second; no conjunction is needed.
body: A coordinate complex sentence joins two equal statements with a comma and 也 (also) or 还 (more) in the second: 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影; 他会说汉语，还会写汉字. No conjunction like and is needed.
The contrast example uses 和 to join two words inside one clause (我有哥哥和姐姐). 也 / 还 join two clauses; 和 joins words or phrases within one clause. Do not use 和 to join two sentences.

examples.text: 我喜欢看书，也喜欢看电影。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan kàn shū, yě xǐhuan kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: I like reading, and I also like watching films.

examples.text: 他会说汉语，还会写汉字。
examples.reading: tā huì shuō Hànyǔ, hái huì xiě Hànzì.
examples.translation: He can speak Chinese, and he can also write characters.

examples.reading: jīntiān hěn lěng, hái xià yǔ.
examples.translation: It is cold today, and it is also raining.

examples.reading: wǒ shì xuéshēng, tā yě shì xuéshēng.
examples.translation: I am a student, and he is a student too.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu gēge hé jiějie.
examples.translation: I have an older brother and an older sister.

lessons.title: Completed aspect: 了1
lessons.summary: 了1 right after the verb marks a completed action; negate with 没 and drop 了.
body: 了1 (le) right after the verb marks the action as completed: 我吃了两个苹果, 他写了一个字. It is about the action finishing, not about a change of situation.
The contrast example shows the negative: 我没吃饭. To say a completed action did not happen, use 没 and drop 了 (you cannot say 没吃了饭). 不 is for habits or the future, not for a past completed action.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I ate two apples.

examples.reading: tā xiě le yí ge zì.
examples.translation: He wrote a character.

examples.reading: wǒmen hē le yì bēi chá.
examples.translation: We drank a cup of tea.

examples.reading: mèimei chuān le yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
examples.translation: My younger sister put on new clothes.

examples.reading: wǒ méi chī fàn.
examples.translation: I have not eaten.

lessons.title: Change aspect: 了2
lessons.summary: Sentence-final 了2 marks a new situation or a change: it is so now.
body: 了2 (le) at the end of a sentence marks a new situation or change: 天冷了 (it has got cold), 我会说汉语了 (I can speak Chinese now), 他不去学校了 (he is not going to school anymore). It is about the situation now, not about one finished action.

The contrast example uses 了1 right after the verb (我买了一个苹果), which marks a completed action. 了1 follows the verb and marks completion; 了2 ends the sentence and marks change. Both can appear together, but they do different jobs.

examples.reading: tiān lěng le.
examples.translation: It has got cold.

examples.reading: wǒ huì shuō Hànyǔ le.
examples.translation: I can speak Chinese now.

examples.reading: tā bú qù xuéxiào le.
examples.translation: He is not going to school anymore.

examples.reading: xiànzài shí'èr diǎn le.
examples.translation: It's already twelve o'clock.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yí ge píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I bought an apple.

lessons.title: Progressive aspect: 在/正在…呢
lessons.summary: 在/正在 before the verb, or 呢 at the end, marks an action in progress.
body: The progressive marks an action in progress: 在 / 正在 before the verb (我在看书, 爸爸正在打电话), 呢 at the end (他吃饭呢), or both (妹妹在睡觉呢).

The contrast example uses 了1 (我吃了两个包子), which marks a completed action. The progressive says the action is happening now; 了 says it is finished. They mark different aspects and are not used for the same meaning.

examples.reading: wǒ zài kàn shū.
examples.translation: I am reading.

examples.reading: bàba zhèngzài dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: Dad is on the phone.

examples.reading: tā chī fàn ne.
examples.translation: He is eating.

examples.reading: mèimei zài shuìjiào ne.
examples.translation: My younger sister is sleeping.

examples.reading: wǒ chī le liǎng ge bāozi.
examples.translation: I ate two buns.

lessons.title: Number expressions: money and ordinals
lessons.summary: Money is number + 块 (spoken) or 元 (formal); ordinals are 第 + number.
body: Money: number + 块 (kuài, spoken) or 元 (yuán, formal): 二十块, 一千元. Ordinals: 第 + number: 第一 (first), 第二 (second). 第 makes an order, not a count.
The contrast example uses 两 before a measure word (我有两个哥哥). Before a measure word, two is 两, not 二; 第 + number is an ordinal, while a bare number counts.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū èrshí kuài.
examples.translation: This book is twenty kuai.

examples.reading: zhège shǒujī yì qiān yuán.
examples.translation: This phone is a thousand yuan.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ dì-yī tiān shàngbān.
examples.translation: This is my first day at work.

examples.reading: yì bēi chá shí yuán.
examples.translation: A cup of tea is ten yuan.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu liǎng ge gēge.
examples.translation: I have two older brothers.

lessons.title: Time expressions: dates, weekdays and clock time
lessons.summary: Dates run year-month-day, weekdays are 星期 + number, and clock time is number + 点 + 分.
body: Dates run from big to small: year + 月 + 日 / 号 (三月五号). Weekdays are 星期 + number (星期一 to 星期六, 星期日 / 星期天). Clock time is number + 点 + number + 分 (八点十分). 号 is spoken, 日 is written.
The contrast example uses 半 (half): 现在两点半 (it is half past two). 半 marks the half hour; 分 marks minutes. Both come after 点.

examples.reading: jīntiān xīngqī jǐ?
examples.translation: What day is it today?

examples.reading: xiànzài bā diǎn shí fēn.
examples.translation: It is ten past eight.

examples.reading: wǒ míngnián qù Zhōngguó.
examples.translation: I am going to China next year.

examples.reading: tā shàngwǔ shàngkè.
examples.translation: He has class in the morning.

examples.reading: xiànzài liǎng diǎn bàn.
examples.translation: It is half past two.

lessons.title: 后缀 -面: 上面 下面 前面 后面 里面 外面
lessons.summary: -面 attaches to position words to make a side or place word: 上面, 下面, 里面.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 前 / 后 / 里 / 外 + 面
body: 面 (miàn) is a suffix that makes a side or place word: 上面 (above), 下面 (below), 前面 (in front), 后面 (behind), 里面 (inside), 外面 (outside). After a noun it names a place: 桌子上面, 学校后面; with 在 it says where something is: 杯子在桌子上面. A 面 word can also stand alone: 外面很冷, 前面就是银行.
The contrast example uses 边: 小狗在门边. 边 makes place words the same way (门边, 桌子上边). 边 and 面 are different suffixes; learn each place word as a whole. A common mistake is 旁面: the word is 旁边, never 旁面.

examples.reading: bēizi zài zhuōzi shàngmian.
examples.translation: The cup is on the table.

examples.reading: māma zài chúfáng lǐmian.
examples.translation: Mum is in the kitchen.

examples.reading: xuéxiào hòumian yǒu yí ge gōngyuán.
examples.translation: There is a park behind the school.

examples.reading: xiǎo gǒu zài mén biān.
examples.translation: The puppy is by the door.

examples.reading: yǐzi xiàmian yǒu yì zhī xiǎo māo.
examples.translation: There is a kitten under the chair.

examples.reading: háizimen zài wàimian wánr.
examples.translation: The children are playing outside.

examples.reading: qiánmian jiù shì yínháng.
examples.translation: The bank is just ahead.

lessons.title: 左 and 右: 左边 右边
lessons.summary: 左 and 右 name sides; add 边 to make 左边 and 右边.
pattern: noun (+ 的) + 左边 / 右边
在 + noun + 左边 / 右边
body: 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) name sides. To name a place, add 边: 左边, 右边. After a noun, with or without 的, they make a place phrase: 学校的左边, 超市右边, 我左边. 左边 and 右边 can also stand alone: 右边的那个人. After 往 the bare 左 or 右 is enough: 往左走, 往右看.

The contrast example uses 往: 我们往右转. 往 introduces a direction you move toward, while 左边 / 右边 name a place (在桌子左边). A place word follows 在; a direction word follows 往. A common mistake is 桌子左 for a place: say 桌子左边.

examples.reading: yínháng zài xuéxiào de zuǒbian.
examples.translation: The bank is to the left of the school.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā zài chāoshì yòubian.
examples.translation: My home is to the right of the supermarket.

examples.reading: qǐng nǐ wǎng zuǒ zǒu.
examples.translation: Please go left.

examples.reading: wǒmen wǎng yòu zhuǎn.
examples.translation: We turn right.

examples.reading: tā zuò zài wǒ zuǒbian.
examples.translation: He sits on my left.

examples.text: 右边的那个人是我哥哥。
examples.reading: yòubian de nàge rén shì wǒ gēge.
examples.translation: The person on the right is my older brother.

lessons.title: Reduplicated verbs: 看看 问一问 看了看
lessons.summary: Repeat a verb to say an action is brief or casual: 看看, 试一试, 看了看.
pattern: V + V: 看看, 想想
V + 一 + V: 试一试; V + 了 + V: 看了看
body: Single-syllable verbs can be reduplicated to say do something a little or casually: 看看, 想想, 尝尝 (AA). A一A puts 一 in the middle: 试一试, 问一问. A了A puts 了 in the middle and tells a short past action: 看了看, 试了试. Two-syllable verbs repeat the whole word (ABAB): 介绍介绍, 学习学习; they never take 一 in the middle (介绍一介绍 is wrong). Verbs like 是, 有 and 在 do not reduplicate.
A了A is only for something that already happened, so it cannot be used in a request: 请你看一看, not 请你看了看.
The contrast example uses 一下 after the verb (请等一下). 一下 also makes an action brief, but the verb itself is not repeated: in 等一下 the verb is not repeated, although 等一等 is also possible.

examples.reading: qǐng nǐ kàn yi kàn.
examples.translation: Please take a look.

examples.reading: nǐ wèn yi wèn lǎoshī.
examples.translation: Ask the teacher.

examples.reading: tā kàn le kan biǎo.
examples.translation: He glanced at his watch.

examples.reading: qǐng děng yíxià.
examples.translation: Please wait a moment.

examples.reading: lái, chángchang wǒ zuò de cài.
examples.translation: Come and taste the dish I made.

examples.reading: nǐ gěi wǒmen jièshào jièshào ba.
examples.translation: Tell us a bit about it.

lessons.title: 可能: maybe, possibly
lessons.summary: Put 可能 before the verb to say something is possible.
body: 可能 (kěnéng) says something is possible: 明天可能下雨, 这件事可能很难. It usually goes after the subject, but it can also start the sentence (可能明天下雨). It can be a short answer on its own: 可能.
Watch the negation: 可能不来 means may not come, while 不可能 means impossible: 他不可能来, 这是不可能的. Do not shorten 不可能 to 不可.
The contrast example uses 会, which says a skill or a future fact rather than doubt: 他会开车. 可能 tells the listener the speaker is not sure.

examples.reading: zhè shì bù kěnéng de.
examples.translation: That is impossible.

examples.reading: míngtiān kěnéng xià yǔ.
examples.translation: It may rain tomorrow.

examples.reading: zhè kěnéng ma?
examples.translation: Is that possible?

examples.reading: tā huì kāi chē.
examples.translation: He can drive.

examples.reading: tā jīntiān kěnéng bù lái le.
examples.translation: He may not come today.

lessons.title: 离合词: 帮忙 游泳 跳舞 跑步
lessons.summary: These verbs contain their object; put 了, 个 or a duration between the two parts.
pattern: 帮 + 忙: 帮个忙, 请他帮忙
游 + 泳 / 跳 + 舞: 游了一个小时泳
跑 + 步: 跑了一会儿步
body: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞 and 跑步 are separable: 帮+忙, 游+泳, 跳+舞, 跑+步. Put 了, 个, a person or a duration between the parts: 帮我一个忙, 游了一个小时泳, 跳了一支舞, 跑了半个小时步. Used as one block they take no further object: 我请他帮忙.

The contrast example uses the plain verb 帮, which takes a person as its object: 妈妈常常帮我. 帮忙 already contains its object, so you say 帮我一个忙 or 帮我, never 帮忙我. The same goes for 游泳: 游泳 or 游了一会儿泳, not 游泳了一个小时.

examples.reading: wǒ qǐng tā bāngmáng.
examples.translation: I asked him for help.

examples.reading: tā yóu le yí ge xiǎoshí yǒng.
examples.translation: He swam for an hour.

examples.reading: tā tiào le yì zhī wǔ.
examples.translation: She did a dance.

examples.reading: māma chángcháng bāng wǒ.
examples.translation: Mum often helps me.

examples.reading: wǒ pǎo le bàn ge xiǎoshí bù.
examples.translation: I ran for half an hour.

examples.reading: nǐ néng bāng wǒ yí ge máng ma?
examples.translation: Can you do me a favour?

lessons.title: 为什么: why
lessons.summary: 为什么 asks for a reason; answer with 因为.
body: 为什么 (wèishénme, why) asks for a reason: 你为什么迟到了？ 他为什么不来？ It usually comes after the subject, but it can also start the question: 为什么他不来？ It can close a short question too: 这是为什么？ Do not add 吗: 你为什么不来吗？ is wrong.
The contrast example answers with 因为: 因为天气不好. 为什么 asks, 因为 answers; the answer is usually a reason clause, not a thing. Do not confuse 为什么 with 什么 (what) or 怎么样 (how is it).

examples.reading: nǐ wèishénme bù gāoxìng?
examples.translation: Why are you unhappy?

examples.reading: tā wèishénme bù lái?
examples.translation: Why is he not coming?

examples.reading: lǎoshī wèn wǒ wèishénme chídào.
examples.translation: The teacher asked me why I was late.

examples.reading: yīnwèi tiānqì bù hǎo.
examples.translation: Because the weather is bad.

examples.reading: zhè shì wèishénme?
examples.translation: Why is that?

lessons.title: 自己: self, by oneself
lessons.summary: A pronoun plus 自己 stresses that person: 我自己, 你自己.
body: 自己 (zìjǐ) follows a pronoun or a name to stress that person: 我自己, 你自己, 他自己 (I myself, by yourself). It can also be the object when it points back to the subject: 你要照顾好自己 (take care of yourself). With 的 it means one's own: 我自己的房间. A common saying: 自己的事情自己做.
The contrast example uses 一个人 (alone): 我一个人去医院 says nobody goes with me. 自己 says I do it myself rather than someone else doing it for me; the two often go together, but they are different words.

examples.reading: wǒ zìjǐ qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: I go to school by myself.

examples.reading: nǐ zìjǐ zuò fàn, hǎo ma?
examples.translation: Cook for yourself, OK?

examples.reading: tā zìjǐ xǐ yīfu.
examples.translation: He washes his clothes himself.

examples.reading: wǒ yí ge rén qù yīyuàn.
examples.translation: I am going to the hospital alone.

examples.reading: nǐ yào zhàogù hǎo zìjǐ.
examples.translation: You must take good care of yourself.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ de fángjiān.
examples.translation: This is my own room.

lessons.title: 这么 那么 这样 那样 每
lessons.summary: 这么/那么 show degree; 这样/那样 show manner; 每 means every.
pattern: 这么 / 那么 + adjective / verb
body: 这么 (zhème, so) and 那么 (nàme, so) go before an adjective, or a verb of feeling, to show degree: 这么大, 那么努力, 那么喜欢. 这样 (like this) and 那样 (like that) describe manner: 这样做, 别那样说. 每 (měi, every) goes with a measure word and often with 都: 每个学生都…, 每天.
The bare 这 and 那 cannot do these jobs: 这大 and 那说 are wrong; you need 这么 / 那样.
The contrast example uses 很, a plain degree adverb: 这家饭店很贵. 这么 and 那么 say so much, often with surprise or pointing at something; 很 just gives the degree without that reference.

examples.reading: zhège píngguǒ zhème dà a!
examples.translation: This apple is so big!

examples.text: 他学习那么努力，一定能考好。
examples.reading: tā xuéxí nàme nǔlì, yídìng néng kǎo hǎo.
examples.translation: He studies so hard that he is sure to do well in the exam.

examples.reading: wǒmen zhèyàng zuò ba.
examples.translation: Let us do it like this.

examples.reading: zhè jiā fàndiàn hěn guì.
examples.translation: This restaurant is very expensive.

examples.reading: měi ge xuéshēng dōu yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.translation: Every student has a book.

examples.reading: bié nàyàng shuō.
examples.translation: Do not say it like that.

lessons.title: Reduplicated adjectives: 大大的 高高兴兴
lessons.summary: Double an adjective for a vivid, warm tone: AA的 or AABB的.
pattern: AA + 的: 大大的, 红红的
AABB + 的: 干干净净的
AABB + 地 + verb: 高高兴兴地
body: Single-syllable adjectives can double to AA, usually with 的: 大大的, 红红的, 热热的. Two-syllable adjectives become AABB: 高高兴兴, 干干净净, 清清楚楚. A reduplicated adjective can be the predicate with 的 (房间干干净净的), go before a noun with 的 (一碗热热的面条) or before a verb with 地 (高高兴兴地回家).
Two-syllable adjectives are not doubled as ABAB: 干净干净 and 高兴高兴 are wrong as adjectives. A reduplicated adjective already carries degree, so do not add 很: 很漂亮 or 漂漂亮亮的, never 很漂漂亮亮 or 很大大的.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个书包很漂亮. 很 states a degree; reduplication paints a picture and sounds warmer or more casual.

examples.reading: tā de yǎnjing dàdà de.
examples.translation: Her eyes are big.

examples.reading: fángjiān gāngān jìngjìng de.
examples.translation: The room is spotless.

examples.text: 我们高高兴兴地回家了。
examples.reading: wǒmen gāogāo xìngxìng de huí jiā le.
examples.translation: We went home happily.

examples.reading: zhège shūbāo hěn piàoliang.
examples.translation: This schoolbag is very pretty.

examples.text: 他的字写得清清楚楚的。
examples.reading: tā de zì xiě de qīngqīng chǔchǔ de.
examples.translation: His handwriting is very clear.

examples.text: 我想吃一碗热热的面条。
examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng chī yì wǎn rèrè de miàntiáo.
examples.translation: I would like a bowl of nice hot noodles.

lessons.title: Numbers: 万 好多 多
lessons.summary: 万 is ten thousand; 好多 means a lot of; 多 after a round number means more than.
pattern: round number + 多 + measure / 岁
body: 万 (wàn) is ten thousand: 一万, 三万块钱; Chinese counts large numbers in 万, so 30,000 is 三万. 好多 (hǎoduō) means a lot of and goes before the noun: 好多人, 好多问题. 多 (duō) after a round number means a little more than: 四十多岁 (forty-odd), 一百多块.
多 cannot stand alone before a noun: say 很多人 or 好多人, not 多人. Also put 多 after the round number, not before it: 四十多岁, not 多四十岁.
The contrast example uses 几, which asks for a small number and needs a measure word: 你有几个朋友？ 几 asks how many; 多 after a number tells an approximate amount.

examples.text: 我们学校有一万个学生。
examples.reading: wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu yí wàn ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: Our school has ten thousand students.

examples.reading: gōngyuán li yǒu hǎoduō rén.
examples.translation: There are lots of people in the park.

examples.reading: wǒ bàba sìshí duō suì.
examples.translation: My dad is in his forties.

examples.reading: nǐ yǒu jǐ ge péngyou?
examples.translation: How many friends do you have?

examples.reading: zhè liàng chē sān wàn kuài qián.
examples.translation: This car costs thirty thousand kuai.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu hǎoduō wèntí xiǎng wèn nǐ.
examples.translation: I have a lot of questions to ask you.

lessons.title: Measure words: 条 位 间 名 包
lessons.summary: 条 for long things, 位 politely for people, 间 for rooms, 名 for roles, 包 for bags.
pattern: numeral + 条 / 位 / 间 / 名 / 包 + noun
body: 条 (tiáo) counts long, thin things: 一条鱼, 一条路, 一条裤子. 位 (wèi) counts people politely: 一位老师, 两位朋友. 间 (jiān) counts rooms: 一间教室, 三间卧室. 名 (míng) counts people in roles: 一名学生, 两名医生. 包 (bāo) is borrowed from the bag or packet: 一包饼干, 一包茶.

The contrast example uses 个, the general measure from Level 1: 我有一个书包. Use a specific measure when the noun calls for one, and learn the noun and its measure together: 一本书, 一件衣服, 一张纸 are not interchangeable.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le yì tiáo yú.
examples.translation: He bought a fish.

examples.reading: tā shì yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.translation: She is a teacher.

examples.reading: tā shì yì míng yīshēng.
examples.translation: He is a doctor.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yí ge shūbāo.
examples.translation: I have a schoolbag.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu sān jiān wòshì.
examples.translation: My home has three bedrooms.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yì bāo bǐnggān.
examples.translation: I bought a packet of biscuits.

lessons.title: 次: times, occasions
lessons.summary: 次 counts how many times: 一次, 两次, 三次.
body: 次 (cì) counts occasions: 一次 (once), 两次 (twice), 三次 (three times). Put the number and 次 after the verb: 打了两次电话, 一个月回一次家. With 过 it counts past experiences: 我去过一次北京. With a place or a thing as object, number + 次 can stand before or after it (去过一次北京, 去过北京一次); a pronoun object comes first (见过他两次).
次 does not count how long; use a duration such as 一个小时 for that. In a separable verb, 次 goes between the parts: 见过一次面.
The contrast example uses 一下: 我们休息一下吧. 一下 makes an action brief and is not counted; 次 counts the number of times.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo yí cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing once.

examples.reading: tā kàn le liǎng cì zhè bù diànyǐng.
examples.translation: He watched this film twice.

examples.reading: wǒmen jiàn guo yí cì miàn.
examples.translation: We have met once.

examples.reading: wǒmen xiūxi yíxià ba.
examples.translation: Let us take a short rest.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi tā dǎ le liǎng cì diànhuà.
examples.translation: I phoned him twice.

examples.reading: tā yí ge yuè huí yí cì jiā.
examples.translation: He goes home once a month.

lessons.title: 多 好 最: exclamation and superlative
lessons.summary: 多 and 好 exclaim before an adjective; 最 picks the highest degree.
body: 多 (duō) before an adjective makes an exclamation, usually with 啊: 多甜啊, 多美啊！ 好 (hǎo) in exclamations means so: 好冷啊, 这里的夏天好热啊！ 最 (zuì, most) makes the superlative: 最高, 最喜欢. Do not put 很 before 最, and do not use 第 for most: 第高 is wrong; 第 only counts order (第一).
The contrast example uses 很: 这个公园很大. 很 states a degree without exclaiming; 多 and 好 carry feeling, and 最 compares one thing with all others.

examples.reading: zhège xīguā duō tián a!
examples.translation: How sweet this watermelon is!

examples.reading: nǐ de fángjiān hǎo dà a!
examples.translation: Your room is so big!

examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de.
examples.translation: He is the tallest in our class.

examples.reading: zhège gōngyuán hěn dà.
examples.translation: This park is very big.

examples.reading: wǒ zuì xǐhuan chī jiǎozi.
examples.translation: I like dumplings best.

examples.reading: zhèlǐ de xiàtiān hǎo rè a!
examples.translation: Summer here is so hot!

lessons.title: 一起: together
lessons.summary: 一起 goes after the subject and before the verb to say people do something together.
pattern: A 和 B + 一起 + verb
body: 一起 (yìqǐ, together) stands after the subject and before the verb: 我们一起吃早饭. With two people, join them with 和: 我和爸爸一起看电视. It is an adverb, so it goes before the verb: 我们一起吃饭, not 我们吃饭一起.
The contrast example uses 和 alone: 我和妹妹一起回家. 和 joins two people into one subject; 一起 says they act together. In 我和妹妹一起回家 both are present, and the order of 我 and 妹妹 can be swapped.

examples.reading: wǒmen yìqǐ chī zǎofàn.
examples.translation: We eat breakfast together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé bàba yìqǐ kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Dad and I watch television together.

examples.reading: tóngxuémen yìqǐ qù túshūguǎn.
examples.translation: The classmates go to the library together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei yìqǐ huí jiā.
examples.translation: My sister and I go home together.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒmen yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.translation: Would you like to go with us?

lessons.title: Time adverbs: 还 已经 有时 快 快要 正
lessons.summary: 还 says still; 已经 says already; 有时 says sometimes; 快 / 快要 say soon; 正 says right now.
pattern: 有时(候) + clause; 快 / 快要 + … + 了
body: 还 (hái, still) says a situation continues: 他还在睡觉. 已经 (yǐjīng, already) usually has 了: 电影已经开始了. 有时 / 有时候 says occasionally and may stand before or after the subject: 我有时候去公园. 快 and 快要 say something is about to happen and need 了 at the end: 火车快开了, 快要考试了. 正 stresses the exact moment, often with 呢: 他们正吃饭呢.
正 and 快 do not mix with 了 the same way: 正…呢 is happening now, 快…了 has not happened yet, 已经…了 has already happened.
The contrast example uses 现在, a time noun: 她现在在开会. 现在 says when; 在 / 正在 / 正 are adverbs placed before the verb. Both 现在她在开会 and 她现在在开会 are possible orders.

examples.reading: tā hái zài shuìjiào.
examples.translation: He is still sleeping.

examples.reading: diànyǐng yǐjīng kāishǐ le.
examples.translation: The film has already started.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒushíhou qù gōngyuán.
examples.translation: I sometimes go to the park.

examples.reading: tā xiànzài zài kāihuì.
examples.translation: She is in a meeting now.

examples.reading: huǒchē kuài kāi le.
examples.translation: The train is about to leave.

examples.reading: tāmen zhèng chī fàn ne.
examples.translation: They are eating right now.

examples.reading: kuàiyào kǎoshì le.
examples.translation: The exam is coming up soon.

lessons.title: 常 and 经常: often
lessons.summary: 常常 and 经常 before the verb mean often; 常 is the short written form.
pattern: subject + 常常 / 经常 + verb
body: 常常 (chángcháng) and 经常 (jīngcháng) mean often and stand before the verb: 我经常去图书馆, 他常常迟到. 常 is a shorter form, used mostly before a one-syllable verb: 常去, 常来玩儿. They describe a habit, not a single occasion.
In the negative say 不常 or 不经常; 不常常 is wrong: 我不常看电视.
The contrast example uses 有时: 她有时不吃早饭. 经常 / 常常 mean often; 有时 means sometimes, so the frequency is lower, and unlike 常 it can also start the sentence (有时她不吃早饭).

examples.reading: wǒ jīngcháng qù túshūguǎn.
examples.translation: I often go to the library.

examples.reading: tā chángcháng chídào.
examples.translation: He is often late.

examples.reading: yéye cháng qù gōngyuán.
examples.translation: Grandfather often goes to the park.

examples.reading: tā yǒushí bù chī zǎofàn.
examples.translation: She sometimes skips breakfast.

examples.reading: wǒ bù cháng kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: I do not watch television much.

examples.reading: huānyíng nǐ cháng lái wánr.
examples.translation: You are welcome to drop by often.

lessons.title: 别: do not, don't
lessons.summary: 别 before a verb makes a negative command: 别说话.
body: 别 (bié) is the spoken negative command: 别开门, 别去那里, 别忘了带书. It tells someone not to do something now or later.
The first contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在这里抽烟. 别 and 不要 both make negative commands; 别 is shorter and more spoken, 不要 is fuller and common in notices and writing.
The second contrast example uses 没: 上周我没去游泳. 别 cannot negate the past or a fact; for something that did not happen use 没, so 昨天我没去, never 昨天我别去.

examples.reading: qǐng bié kāi mén.
examples.translation: Please do not open the door.

examples.reading: bié wàng le dài shū.
examples.translation: Do not forget to bring the book.

examples.reading: bié qù nàlǐ.
examples.translation: Do not go there.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.
examples.translation: Please do not smoke here.

examples.reading: shàng zhōu wǒ méi qù yóuyǒng.
examples.translation: I did not go swimming last week.

lessons.title: 再 and 就 linking actions
lessons.summary: 再 says then / next after something else; 就 says then / as early as.
body: 再 as a connective says then, after something else is done; it looks to the future: 我先喝水，再吃饭; 吃完饭再走吧. 就 links a condition or a first event to what follows at once: 他一来我就走; 你想去，我们就去. After a time word 就 says early or soon: 我五点就起床.
For a repeated action in the past use 又, not 再; for a future step use 再, not 又: 吃完饭再走, not 吃完饭又走.
The contrast example uses 才: 他十点才起床. 就 says early or quick; 才 says late or not until, so 五点就起床 and 十点才起床 point in opposite directions. After 一 the partner is always 就, never 才.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān hē shuǐ, zài chī fàn.
examples.translation: I will drink some water first, then eat.

examples.reading: tā yì lái wǒ jiù zǒu.
examples.translation: As soon as he comes, I will leave.

examples.reading: wǒ wǔ diǎn jiù qǐchuáng.
examples.translation: I get up as early as five.

examples.reading: tā shí diǎn cái qǐchuáng.
examples.translation: He does not get up until ten.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng qù, wǒmen jiù qù.
examples.translation: If you want to go, we will go.

examples.reading: chī wán fàn zài zǒu ba.
examples.translation: Eat before you go.

lessons.title: 都 就 还是: attitude words
lessons.summary: 都 stresses even; 就 stresses exactly or just; 还是 suggests or says still.
body: 都 adds emphasis, often with 了, meaning already or even: 他都十二岁了, 饭都凉了. 就 narrows or fixes: 我就想去公园 (that is all I want), 图书馆就在前面 (right there), 他就十块钱 (he has only ten kuai). 还是 suggests the better choice: 还是喝茶吧, 还是你先去吧.

The contrast example uses 也: 他也很想去. 也 adds one more person or thing. Do not confuse this with the 都 that means all: that 都 needs a plural subject (我们都去), while the emphatic 都……了 works with one person too (他都十二岁了).

examples.reading: tā dōu shí'èr suì le.
examples.translation: He is already twelve.

examples.reading: wǒ jiù xiǎng qù gōngyuán.
examples.translation: I just want to go to the park.

examples.reading: háishi hē chá ba.
examples.translation: Let us have tea instead.

examples.reading: tā yě hěn xiǎng qù.
examples.translation: He really wants to go too.

examples.reading: túshūguǎn jiù zài qiánmian.
examples.translation: The library is right ahead.

examples.reading: fàn dōu liáng le, kuài chī ba.
examples.translation: The food has gone cold; eat up.

lessons.title: 从: from (time and place)
lessons.summary: 从 marks the start of a time or place span; 到 marks the end.
body: 从 (cóng) marks a starting point in space or time: 我从中国来, 他刚从学校回来, 我们从八点开始上课. It is often paired with 到: 从家到学校很近; with a verb in between it marks a whole span: 他从早上工作到晚上.
Do not use 在 or 往 for a starting point: 我在中国来 and 他往学校回来 are wrong.
The contrast example uses 在: 我的手机在包里. 从 introduces where something starts or comes from; 在 says where it is.

examples.reading: wǒ cóng Zhōngguó lái.
examples.translation: I come from China.

examples.reading: tā cóng zǎoshang gōngzuò dào wǎnshang.
examples.translation: He works from morning till night.

examples.reading: cóng jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.translation: Home is very close to school.

examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī zài bāo li.
examples.translation: My phone is in my bag.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng bā diǎn kāishǐ shàngkè.
examples.translation: Our classes start at eight.

examples.reading: tā gāng cóng xuéxiào huílai.
examples.translation: He has just come back from school.

lessons.title: 往 and 从: direction and route
lessons.summary: 往 says toward; 从 says by way of / through.
body: 往 (wǎng) says toward a direction: 往前走, 往后看, 飞机往南飞. 从 (cóng) here says by way of or through: 我们从这条路走, 从公园里走过去. 往 is the direction you face or head; 从 is the route taken.
The contrast example uses 到: 我们到学校了. 往 points in a direction; 到 names the place you arrive at, so 到前走 is wrong.

examples.reading: qǐng wǎng qián zǒu.
examples.translation: Please walk straight ahead.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng zhè tiáo lù zǒu.
examples.translation: We take this road.

examples.reading: nǐ wǎng hòu kàn!
examples.translation: Look behind you!

examples.reading: wǒmen dào xuéxiào le.
examples.translation: We have arrived at school.

examples.text: 我们从公园里走过去吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen cóng gōngyuán li zǒu guòqu ba.
examples.translation: Let us walk through the park.

examples.reading: fēijī wǎng nán fēi.
examples.translation: The plane is flying south.

lessons.title: 给 比 跟: objects
lessons.summary: 给 introduces the receiver; 比 compares; 跟 introduces the person you act with.
pattern: 给 + person + verb: 给妈妈打电话
body: As a preposition, 给 (gěi) introduces the person who receives or benefits: 我给你介绍一下, 我给妈妈写了一封信. 比 (bǐ) introduces the thing compared: 我的书比你的多. 跟 (gēn) introduces the person you do something with or speak to: 请跟我来, 我想跟你说一件事. All three stand before the verb.

The contrast example uses 对: 他对中国文化很感兴趣. 对 says an attitude or interest is directed toward someone or something. 对 and 比 are not interchangeable, and in a 比 sentence the adjective takes no 很: 我的书比你的多, never 比你的很多.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi nǐ jièshào yíxià.
examples.translation: Let me introduce someone to you.

examples.reading: wǒ de shū bǐ nǐ de duō.
examples.translation: I have more books than you.

examples.reading: qǐng gēn wǒ lái.
examples.translation: Please come with me.

examples.text: 他对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.reading: tā duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.translation: He is very interested in Chinese culture.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi māma xiě le yì fēng xìn.
examples.translation: I wrote a letter to Mum.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ shuō yí jiàn shì.
examples.translation: I want to tell you something.

lessons.title: 因为: because
lessons.summary: As a preposition, 因为 + a noun phrase gives the cause: 因为这件事, 因为工作.
pattern: subject + 因为 + noun phrase + verb phrase
body: As a preposition, 因为 (yīnwèi) takes a noun phrase and gives the cause of what follows: 因为这件事，他很不高兴; 他因为工作没有时间休息; 他因为感冒没来上课. It can stand at the head of the sentence (with a comma) or after the subject.
With a noun phrase you do not need 所以. The usual mistake is to put 所以 here instead: 所以这件事 is wrong, because 所以 introduces a result, not a cause.
The contrast example uses the conjunction pair 因为……所以: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少. There 因为 introduces a whole clause and 所以 gives the result.

examples.text: 因为这件事，他很不高兴。
examples.reading: yīnwèi zhè jiàn shì, tā hěn bù gāoxìng.
examples.translation: Because of this matter he is very unhappy.

examples.text: 他因为工作没有时间休息。
examples.reading: tā yīnwèi gōngzuò méiyǒu shíjiān xiūxi.
examples.translation: Because of work he has no time to rest.

examples.reading: zhè dōu shì yīnwèi tiānqì.
examples.translation: It is all because of the weather.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang rén hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few people on the road.

examples.reading: tā yīnwèi gǎnmào méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: He missed class because of a cold.

lessons.title: 跟 joining words: A 跟 B
lessons.summary: 跟 connects two nouns as a compound subject or object, like 和.
body: 跟 (gēn) can join two nouns or pronouns like 和: 老师跟学生, 爸爸跟妈妈, 我跟他. It is more spoken; 和 is the general form. The two joined words can usually swap places. Do not use 跟 or 和 to join clauses; use a clause conjunction such as 但是.
Do not mix it up with the preposition 跟 (跟我来): as a conjunction, the two nouns form one subject and often take 都.
The contrast example uses 和: 我家有一只猫和一只狗. 和 is neutral and common in writing; like 跟 it joins nouns, not clauses.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le miànbāo gēn niúnǎi.
examples.translation: I bought bread and milk.

examples.reading: bàba gēn māma dōu shì yīshēng.
examples.translation: Both Dad and Mum are doctors.

examples.text: 哥哥跟弟弟都喜欢踢足球。
examples.reading: gēge gēn dìdi dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.translation: Both the older and the younger brother like playing football.

examples.text: 我家有一只猫和一只狗。
examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī māo hé yì zhī gǒu.
examples.translation: We have a cat and a dog at home.

examples.reading: wǒ gēn tā shì hǎo péngyou.
examples.translation: He and I are good friends.

lessons.title: Clause conjunctions: 但是 那 虽然 还是
lessons.summary: These conjunctions link clauses: 但(是) turns, 那 follows on, 虽然 concedes, 还是 offers a choice, 因为 / 所以 give cause and result.
pattern: 那 + clause; 虽然 ……，(但是 / 还是) ……
A 还是 B (choice); 因为 ……，所以 ……
body: 但 and 但是 turn to a contrasting second clause: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了; 他很想去，但没有时间. 那 carries on from what the other person said: 那你就别去了. 虽然 concedes a fact: 虽然很累，他还是很高兴. 因为 gives a reason and 所以 the result: 因为太晚了，所以我打车回家.
As a conjunction 还是 joins two choices, also inside a statement: 我不知道他去还是不去. In such an embedded choice 或者 is wrong. (The 还是 in 虽然……，他还是…… is the adverb still.)

The contrast example uses 那 as a demonstrative: 那个人是我的老师. 那 before a measure word points at something (Level 1); 那 at the head of a clause is the conjunction then. The two 那 have the same shape but different jobs.

examples.text: 这本书很好，但是太贵了。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū hěn hǎo, dànshì tài guì le.
examples.translation: This book is good, but it is too expensive.

examples.reading: nà nǐ jiù bié qù le.
examples.translation: Then you had better not go.

examples.text: 我不知道他去还是不去。
examples.reading: wǒ bù zhīdào tā qù háishi bú qù.
examples.translation: I do not know whether he is going or not.

examples.reading: nàge rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: That person is my teacher.

examples.reading: tā hěn xiǎng qù, dàn méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.translation: He really wants to go, but he has no time.

examples.text: 虽然很累，他还是很高兴。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn lèi, tā háishi hěn gāoxìng.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still happy.

examples.text: 因为太晚了，所以我打车回家。
examples.reading: yīnwèi tài wǎn le, suǒyǐ wǒ dǎchē huí jiā.
examples.translation: It was too late, so I took a taxi home.

lessons.title: 得 and 地: complement and adverbial markers
lessons.summary: 得 after a verb introduces a complement; 地 after an adjective marks how an action is done.
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of how the action turns out: 写得很好看, 来得太晚了. 地 (de) after an adjective or adverb marks how the action is done and stands before the verb: 慢慢地走过来, 认真地听. Both are read neutral.
Check what follows: a verb after the marker means 地 (快乐地唱歌); an adjective phrase after a verb means 得 (写得很好看). 慢慢得走 and 写地很好 are both wrong.
The contrast example uses 的: 这是哥哥的电脑. 的 comes before a noun and marks possession or description; 得 follows a verb; 地 comes before a verb. The same sound has three different jobs.

examples.reading: tā Hànzì xiě de hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: His Chinese characters are beautifully written.
