examples.reading: lǎorén mànmàn de zǒu guòlai le.
examples.translation: The old man walked over slowly.

examples.reading: háizimen kuàilè de chànggē.
examples.translation: The children sing happily.

examples.reading: zhè shì gēge de diànnǎo.
examples.translation: This is my older brother's computer.

examples.reading: nǐ lái de tài wǎn le.
examples.translation: You came too late.

examples.reading: tā rènzhēn de tīng lǎoshī jiǎngkè.
examples.translation: He listens carefully to the teacher's lesson.

lessons.title: 过: past experience
lessons.summary: Verb + 过 says the action has happened at least once; negate with 没(有)…过.
body: 过 (guo) after a verb marks an experience in the past: 我去过中国, 你吃过北京烤鸭吗, 他学过两年汉语. To say it never happened, put 没(有) before the verb and keep 过 after it: 她没坐过火车. Do not use 不 here, and do not replace 过 with 了 in the negative: 没去了 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 了: 他喝了三杯水. 过 says someone has had the experience at some time; 了 says the action was completed on that occasion. 着 marks a lasting state and cannot express experience.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo tā jiā.
examples.translation: I have been to his home.

examples.reading: nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma?
examples.translation: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?

examples.reading: tā méi zuò guo huǒchē.
examples.translation: She has never been on a train.

examples.reading: tā hē le sān bēi shuǐ.
examples.translation: He drank three glasses of water.

examples.reading: tā xué guo liǎng nián Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: He once studied Chinese for two years.

lessons.title: 着: continuing state
lessons.summary: Verb + 着 says a state holds or a posture continues: 门开着, 他拿着一本书.
body: 着 (zhe) after a verb marks a continuing state or posture: 门开着, 灯还亮着, 他穿着一件白衬衫, 他拿着一本书. It often describes a scene or background: 墙上挂着一幅画 (see 存现句).

The contrast example uses 在: 弟弟在做作业. 着 describes a state that holds; 在 / 正在 describe an action happening now. 门开着 is a state (the door is open), while 他在开门 is an action in progress (he is opening the door).

examples.reading: mén kāi zhe.
examples.translation: The door is open.

examples.reading: tā ná zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He is holding a book.

examples.reading: tā chuān zhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
examples.translation: She is wearing a white shirt.

examples.reading: dìdi zài zuò zuòyè.
examples.translation: My younger brother is doing his homework.

examples.reading: dēng hái liàng zhe.
examples.translation: The light is still on.

lessons.title: 呢 吧 的 啊: sentence-final particles
lessons.summary: 呢 marks something going on; 吧 suggests; 的 confirms; 啊 exclaims or softens.
body: In a statement, 呢 (ne) marks that something is going on right now: 爷爷在睡觉呢. 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or request: 我们走吧, 你先休息一会儿吧. 的 (de) at the end confirms with confidence: 他会来的. 啊 (a) adds feeling to an exclamation or softens a remark: 你的汉语说得真好啊！

The contrast example uses 吗: 你喜欢喝咖啡吗？ 吗 makes a plain yes-no question; 呢 / 吧 / 的 / 啊 each color the sentence differently and cannot replace 吗 there. Aspect words such as 过 and 着 are not sentence-final particles.

examples.reading: yéye zài shuìjiào ne.
examples.translation: Grandpa is sleeping.

examples.reading: wǒmen zǒu ba.
examples.translation: Let us go.

examples.reading: tā huì lái de.
examples.translation: He will come.

examples.reading: nǐ xǐhuan hē kāfēi ma?
examples.translation: Do you like coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ de Hànyǔ shuō de zhēn hǎo a!
examples.translation: Your Chinese is really good!

examples.reading: nǐ xiān xiūxi yíhuìr ba.
examples.translation: Have a rest first.

lessons.title: Verb-complement phrases: V + result/degree
lessons.summary: A complement follows the verb and adds its result or degree: 看见, 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + complement: 看 + 见, 做 + 完
body: In a verb-complement phrase the second part tells what happens as a result of the action: 看见 (look and see), 听懂 (listen and understand), 吃完 (finish eating), 听清楚 (hear clearly). Negate it with 没: 我没听清楚. It is different from a verb-object phrase, where the second part is the thing acted on: 看书, 吃饭.
A result complement is not an aspect: 吃完了 says the eating is finished, 吃着 says it is going on.
The contrast example uses a verb-object phrase: 我想吃面条. In 吃面条 the second part is the thing (the object); in 吃完 it is the result (the complement), so 想完面条 is impossible.

examples.reading: wǒ kànjiàn tā le.
examples.translation: I saw him.

examples.reading: tā yǐjīng chī wán fàn le.
examples.translation: He has already finished eating.

examples.reading: wǒ tīng dǒng le.
examples.translation: I understood.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáo.
examples.translation: I would like noodles.

examples.reading: wǒ méi tīng qīngchu.
examples.translation: I did not hear it clearly.

lessons.title: Phrases: …的, serial verbs, pivotal phrases
lessons.summary: 的字短语 stands for a thing; 连谓短语 chains verbs; 兼语短语 shares one person between verbs.
pattern: 请/让 + person + V (兼语短语)
body: 的字短语: 的 after a word or phrase stands for a thing or person: 我的, 红色的, 卖菜的 (the vegetable seller). 连谓短语: two verbs share one subject and happen together or in order: 去买菜, 去图书馆借书. 兼语短语: the object of the first verb is also the subject of the second: 让我帮忙, 请他来.
In a 的字短语 the marker is always 的, never 地 or 得: 卖菜的, not 卖菜地.
The contrast example uses 和: 我买了苹果和香蕉. 和 joins two nouns into one phrase; it does not chain verbs or make a pivotal structure.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan hóngsè de.
examples.translation: I like the red one.

examples.reading: tā qù mǎi cài.
examples.translation: He goes to buy food.

examples.reading: māma ràng wǒ bāngmáng.
examples.translation: Mum asked me to help.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo.
examples.translation: I bought apples and bananas.

examples.reading: mài cài de lái le.
examples.translation: The vegetable seller is here.

examples.reading: wǒ qù túshūguǎn jiè shū.
examples.translation: I am going to the library to borrow books.

lessons.title: Phrase functions: noun, verb, adjective
lessons.summary: A phrase can act as a noun, a verb or an adjective: 新书, 去买菜, 很大.
pattern: 名词性: 新的书 / 我的书
动词性: 去买菜 / 喜欢看书
形容词性: 很大 / 红红的
body: By function, a phrase can behave like a noun (名词性: 一件新衣服, 我的老师), like a verb (动词性: 听音乐, 学汉语), or like an adjective (形容词性: 很干净, 干干净净的). A verb phrase can even be a subject: 学汉语很有意思. Function depends on the head word and on where the phrase sits in the sentence.
The contrast example uses 的: 我的老师是北京人. With most nouns 的 is needed to make a noun phrase (我的书); kinship terms and institutions after a pronoun can drop it (我妈妈, 我们学校).

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
examples.translation: I bought a new piece of clothing.

examples.reading: tā xǐhuan tīng yīnyuè.
examples.translation: He likes listening to music.

examples.reading: zhège fángjiān hěn gānjìng.
examples.translation: This room is very clean.

examples.reading: wǒ de lǎoshī shì Běijīng rén.
examples.translation: My teacher is from Beijing.

examples.reading: xué Hànyǔ hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.translation: Learning Chinese is very interesting.

lessons.title: 什么的: and so on
lessons.summary: 什么的 follows a list to mean and so on: 苹果、香蕉什么的.
body: 什么的 (shénme de) closes a list, or follows one example, to mean and so on, and things like that: 他买了书、本子什么的; 我们去喝点儿茶什么的吧. It is informal. Because the list is open, the items of a longer list can usually be given in any order.
The contrast example uses 和: 我想买牛奶和鸡蛋. 和 links the items and closes the list; 什么的 adds and so on. Do not put 和 at the end in place of 什么的.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le shū, běnzi shénme de.
examples.translation: He bought books, notebooks and so on.

examples.text: 你可以带点儿水果什么的。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ dài diǎnr shuǐguǒ shénme de.
examples.translation: You could bring some fruit or something.

examples.reading: tā xǐhuan dǎ lánqiú shénme de.
examples.translation: He likes playing basketball and things like that.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng mǎi niúnǎi hé jīdàn.
examples.translation: I want to buy milk and eggs.

examples.text: 我们去喝点儿茶什么的吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen qù hē diǎnr chá shénme de ba.
examples.translation: Let us go for tea or something.

lessons.title: 还是……吧: a gentle suggestion
lessons.summary: 还是……吧 suggests an option after thinking it over: 我们还是走吧.
body: 还是……吧 makes a gentle suggestion or a choice after weighing things: 我们还是坐地铁去吧, 外面很冷，还是多穿点儿衣服吧. 还是 can stand after or before the subject (还是我们走吧). It softens advice; 吧 alone can also suggest, but 还是…吧 says this option is better.
The contrast example uses 好吗: 我们明天去，好吗？ 好吗 asks whether the listener agrees; 还是…吧 recommends one option instead of asking.

examples.reading: wǒmen háishi zǒu ba.
examples.translation: We had better go.

examples.text: 外面很冷，还是多穿点儿衣服吧。
examples.reading: wàimian hěn lěng, háishi duō chuān diǎnr yīfu ba.
examples.translation: It is cold outside; you had better put on more clothes.

examples.text: 路上车太多，还是坐地铁去吧。
examples.reading: lù shang chē tài duō, háishi zuò dìtiě qù ba.
examples.translation: There is too much traffic; we had better take the underground.

examples.reading: wǒmen míngtiān qù, hǎo ma?
examples.translation: Shall we go tomorrow?

examples.text: 太晚了，还是明天再说吧。
examples.reading: tài wǎn le, háishi míngtiān zài shuō ba.
examples.translation: It is too late; let us talk about it tomorrow.

lessons.title: 要……了: about to happen
lessons.summary: 要/快要/就要…了 says something is just going to happen.
pattern: 快要 / 就要 + V + 了
body: 要…了, 快要…了, 快…了 and 就要…了 all say an event is about to happen: 要下雨了, 火车快要到了, 他就要回来了. 了 at the end is required. 快要 is one word.
A time word can go before 就要 but not before 快要: 明天就要考试了 is right, 明天快要考试了 is wrong. Also do not use 正 here: 正…了 is wrong, because 正 is for something already in progress.
The contrast example uses 已经: 他已经回家了. 已经 says the event already happened; 要 / 快要 / 就要 say it has not happened yet.

examples.reading: yào xià yǔ le.
examples.translation: It is going to rain.

examples.reading: huǒchē kuàiyào dào le.
examples.translation: The train is almost here.

examples.reading: tā jiù yào huílai le.
examples.translation: He is about to come back.

examples.reading: tā yǐjīng huí jiā le.
examples.translation: He has already gone home.

examples.reading: míngtiān jiù yào kǎoshì le.
examples.translation: The exam is tomorrow.

lessons.title: 都……了: lateness or amount
lessons.summary: 都……了 stresses that something is later or larger than expected.
body: 都……了 stresses surprise or lateness: 都十点了，快睡吧; 他都十八岁了; 都快中午了，他还没起床. It sums up the scale and adds 了. This is not the 都 that sums people before the verb (我们都去).
The contrast example uses 已经: 我已经吃过了. 已经 simply says already; 都…了 adds surprise that it is so late or so much.

examples.reading: dōu shí diǎn le, kuài shuì ba.
examples.translation: It is already ten o'clock; go to sleep.

examples.text: 你都看了两个小时电视了。
examples.reading: nǐ dōu kàn le liǎng ge xiǎoshí diànshì le.
examples.translation: You have been watching TV for two hours already.

examples.text: 都快中午了，他还没起床。
examples.reading: dōu kuài zhōngwǔ le, tā hái méi qǐchuáng.
examples.translation: It is almost noon, and he is still not up.

examples.reading: wǒ yǐjīng chī guo le.
examples.translation: I have already eaten.

examples.text: 这件衣服都穿了五年了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu dōu chuān le wǔ nián le.
examples.translation: I have been wearing this for five years now.

lessons.title: Patient subjects: the thing comes first
lessons.summary: In a patient-subject sentence the thing receives the action: 作业做完了.
body: In a patient-subject sentence the subject is the thing the action happens to: 作业做完了, 这些衣服洗得很干净, 信已经寄出去了, 这本书我看过了. The doer can be left out because it is known or unimportant. This is not the passive with 被 (Level 3).

The contrast example uses the doer as subject: 我做完了作业. A patient-subject sentence puts the thing first (受事主语); an ordinary sentence puts the doer first (施事主语). Several orders are possible with the same words, so the word-order exercise is skipped for some of these examples.

examples.reading: zuòyè zuò wán le.
examples.translation: The homework is done.

examples.reading: zhèxiē yīfu xǐ de hěn gānjìng.
examples.translation: These clothes have been washed very clean.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū wǒ kàn guo le.
examples.translation: I have read this book.

examples.reading: wǒ zuò wán le zuòyè.
examples.translation: I finished the homework.

examples.reading: xìn yǐjīng jì chūqu le.
examples.translation: The letter has already been sent.

lessons.title: Noun-phrase predicates
lessons.summary: A noun phrase of date, age, price or weather can be the predicate directly: 后天星期五, 这个西瓜十五块钱.
body: With dates, weekdays, ages, prices and weather, Chinese often drops 是 and puts a noun phrase directly after the subject: 后天星期五, 我妹妹今年八岁, 这个西瓜十五块钱, 明天晴天. Adding 是 is also possible: 后天是星期五.
Two common mistakes: an ordinary noun of identity still needs 是 (他是老师, not 他老师), and the negative always needs 是: 今天不是星期天, never 今天不星期天.

The contrast examples use 是: 他是老师 and 今天不是星期天. 是 equates the subject with the noun and is required in the negative; the bare noun predicate is used only for date, age, price and weather and sounds more spoken.

examples.reading: hòutiān xīngqīwǔ.
examples.translation: The day after tomorrow is Friday.

examples.reading: zhège xīguā shíwǔ kuài qián.
examples.translation: This watermelon costs fifteen kuai.

examples.reading: míngtiān qíngtiān.
examples.translation: Tomorrow will be sunny.

examples.reading: tā shì lǎoshī.
examples.translation: He is a teacher.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei jīnnián bā suì.
examples.translation: My younger sister is eight this year.

examples.reading: jīntiān bú shì xīngqītiān.
examples.translation: Today is not Sunday.

lessons.title: Attributives: verb phrases and subject-predicate phrases
lessons.summary: A verb phrase or subject-predicate phrase can modify a noun with 的: 我买的书, 身体好的学生.
body: An attributive (定语) comes before the noun and usually takes 的: 我买的书, 昨天来的客人, 穿红衣服的人. A subject-predicate phrase can also be an attributive: 妈妈做的菜, 个子高的同学. Some short attributives drop 的: 汉语老师.
The contrast example uses 地: 他高兴地笑了. An attributive with 的 goes before a noun; an adverbial with 地 goes before a verb. Check what follows the marker, not just the sound: 我买地书 is wrong.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi de shū hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The book I bought is very good.

examples.text: 昨天来的客人是我的老师。
examples.reading: zuótiān lái de kèren shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The guest who came yesterday is my teacher.

examples.reading: māma zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: The food Mum cooks is delicious.

examples.reading: tā gāoxìng de xiào le.
examples.translation: He smiled happily.

examples.text: 穿红衣服的人是我姐姐。
examples.reading: chuān hóng yīfu de rén shì wǒ jiějie.
examples.translation: The person in red is my older sister.

lessons.title: Result complements: 错 懂 好 会 完
lessons.summary: A result complement after the verb says how the action turns out: 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + 完 / 好 / 懂 / 会 / 错
body: 完 (finish), 好 (done well or ready), 懂 (understand), 会 (master a skill) and 错 (wrong) follow the verb as results: 看完, 做好, 听懂, 学会, 写错. 了 usually follows: 我学会游泳了. To say the result did not happen, use 没: 我没听懂. Inserting 不 or 得 (听不懂, 听得懂) says whether the result is possible.
The contrast example uses 得: 她唱得很好听. A result complement attaches the outcome directly to the verb; 得 introduces a description of manner or degree. Do not write 地 there: 唱地很好听 is wrong.

examples.reading: nǐ kàn wán le ma?
examples.translation: Have you finished reading it?

examples.reading: wǒ tīng dǒng lǎoshī de huà le.
examples.translation: I understood what the teacher said.

examples.reading: wǎnfàn zuò hǎo le.
examples.translation: Dinner is ready.

examples.reading: tā chàng de hěn hǎotīng.
examples.translation: She sings beautifully.

examples.reading: wǒ xiě cuò le yí ge zì.
examples.translation: I wrote a character wrong.

examples.reading: wǒ xué huì yóuyǒng le.
examples.translation: I have learned to swim.

lessons.title: Simple directional complements
lessons.summary: A one-syllable direction word follows the verb: 寄来, 上楼, 走进.
pattern: V + 进 / 出 / 回 / 过
body: 简单趋向补语 is one syllable after the verb: 来 toward the speaker, 去 away, 上 up or onto, 下 down or off, 进 into, 出 out of, 回 back, 过 across, 起 up. Examples: 跑上楼, 坐下, 走进教室, 跑回家. With a thing object, 来 / 去 can come before the object: 寄来了一封信.
With a place object, the place goes before 来 / 去: 走进教室来, 回家去; 进来教室 and 回来家 are wrong.
The contrast example uses the compound 上来: 他走上来了. A compound has two syllables (上 + 来); a simple complement has one (上 or 来). 跑上来楼 is wrong: a place object follows the simple 上.

examples.reading: tā pǎo shàng lóu le.
examples.translation: He ran upstairs.

examples.reading: tā gěi wǒ jì lái le yì fēng xìn.
examples.translation: He sent me a letter.

examples.reading: tā zǒu jìn le jiàoshì.
examples.translation: He walked into the classroom.

examples.reading: tā zǒu shànglai le.
examples.translation: He walked up here.

examples.reading: tā pǎo huí jiā le.
examples.translation: He ran home.

examples.reading: tā zuò xià le.
examples.translation: She sat down.

lessons.title: Compound directional complements
lessons.summary: Two-syllable complements combine directions: 上来, 下来, 进来, 出来, 回来.
pattern: V + 下来 / 下去; V + 起来
V + 进来 / 进去; V + 出来 / 出去; V + 回来 / 过来
body: 复合趋向补语 combines a direction with 来 or 去: 上来 / 上去, 下来 / 下去, 进来 / 进去, 出来 / 出去, 回来 / 回去, 过来 / 过去, 起来. The second syllable points relative to the speaker: 来 toward, 去 away. Examples: 走进来, 拿下来, 跑出去, 走过去, 走回去, 站起来.

With motion verbs such as 走, 跑 and 站, a bare 进, 出, 回 or 起 does not normally end the sentence; use the compound form: 他站起来了 and 我们走回去吧, not 他站起了 or 我们走回吧 (下 is an exception: 坐下了 is fine). With a place object, the place goes between: 走进教室来.
The contrast example uses the simple 下: 他走下楼了. 下 alone takes the place object directly; 下来 is its compound form. Both describe movement, but 走下来楼 is wrong.

examples.reading: māma zǒu jìnlai le.
examples.translation: Mum walked in.

examples.text: 他从楼上拿下来一本书。
examples.reading: tā cóng lóu shàng ná xiàlai yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He brought a book down from upstairs.

examples.reading: tā pǎo chūqu le.
examples.translation: He ran out.

examples.reading: tā zǒu xià lóu le.
examples.translation: He walked downstairs.

examples.reading: nǐ kuài zǒu guòqu kànkan ba.
examples.translation: Go over and have a look.

examples.reading: wǒmen zǒu huíqu ba.
examples.translation: Let us walk back.

examples.reading: tā zhàn qǐlai le.
examples.translation: He stood up.

lessons.title: State complements: V + 得 + adjective
lessons.summary: 得 after a verb describes how the action is done: 说得很好, 跑得很快.
pattern: V + 得 + 很 / 非常 + adj
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 他跑得很快, 妹妹长得很高. This is different from a result complement such as 说完, and from an adverbial before the verb with 地 (高兴地说).
When the verb has an object, repeat the verb before 得: 她跳舞跳得很好, 他说汉语说得很流利. A common mistake is 他说汉语得很好; another is writing 地 after the verb (跑地很快).
The contrast example uses the result complement 完: 他说完了. 得 describes manner or degree; a result complement states the outcome directly.

examples.reading: tā tiàowǔ tiào de hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: She dances very well.

examples.reading: tā pǎo de hěn kuài.
examples.translation: He runs very fast.

examples.reading: mèimei zhǎng de hěn gāo.
examples.translation: My younger sister has grown very tall.

examples.reading: tā shuō wán le.
examples.translation: He finished speaking.

examples.reading: tā shuō Hànyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
examples.translation: He speaks Chinese fluently.

lessons.title: Quantity complements: duration and measurement
lessons.summary: Duration follows the verb: 住了两年; measurement follows an adjective: 大两岁.
body: Duration (时量补语) follows the verb, often with 了: 我在中国住了两年, 他等了一个小时, 我们走了半个小时. After an adjective in a comparison, a quantity states the difference: 他比我大三岁, 我的手机比你的贵一百块.

The contrast example uses 次: 我见过他两次. 次 counts occasions, not length; duration counts how long, and adjective + quantity measures a difference. With a pronoun object, number + 次 follows the pronoun (见过他两次, not 见过两次他).

examples.reading: wǒ zài Zhōngguó zhù le liǎng nián.
examples.translation: I lived in China for two years.

examples.reading: tā děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: He waited for an hour.

examples.reading: tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.translation: He is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ jiàn guo tā liǎng cì.
examples.translation: I have met him twice.

examples.text: 我的手机比你的贵一百块。
examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī bǐ nǐ de guì yìbǎi kuài.
examples.translation: My phone costs a hundred kuai more than yours.

examples.reading: wǒmen zǒu le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: We walked for half an hour.

lessons.title: Subject-predicate predicates
lessons.summary: A whole subject-predicate phrase comments on the topic: 他身体很好.
body: In a 主谓谓语句 the predicate itself is a subject-predicate phrase: 他身体很好 (topic 他, comment 身体很好), 北京冬天很冷, 这件事我不清楚. The first noun is the topic, and the following subject belongs to it or is commented on in relation to it.

The contrast example uses an ordinary verb-plus-object sentence: 我喜欢汉语. A subject-predicate predicate comments on a topic; an ordinary sentence states an action with an object. 这件事我不清楚 can also be said as 我不清楚这件事.

examples.reading: tā shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He is in very good health.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù qīngchu.
examples.translation: I am not clear about this matter.

examples.reading: wǒ māma gōngzuò hěn máng.
examples.translation: My mum is very busy with work.

examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: I like Chinese.

examples.translation: Winters in Beijing are very cold.

lessons.title: 还是 choice questions
lessons.summary: A还是B? asks the listener to choose one of two options.
body: 还是 makes an alternative question: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ 你今天去还是明天去？ The answer is one of the two, not yes or no, so do not add 吗 to the sentence. The two choices can usually be given in either order, except in a form like 你懂了还是没懂？, where the yes option comes first. In a question 或者 cannot replace 还是.
The first contrast example uses 吗: 你想喝茶吗？ 吗 makes a yes-no question; 还是 offers two choices. Choose the form that matches the answer you expect.
The second contrast example uses 或者 in a statement: 周末我在家看书或者看电视. In statements or means 或者; in questions it means 还是. Using 还是 in this statement is wrong.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi kāfēi?
examples.translation: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù?
examples.translation: Are you going today or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ dǒng le háishi méi dǒng?
examples.translation: Did you understand or not?

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng hē chá ma?
examples.translation: Would you like some tea?

examples.text: 周末我在家看书或者看电视。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ zài jiā kàn shū huòzhě kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: At weekends I read or watch television at home.

lessons.title: Imperative sentences with 别
lessons.summary: 别 + verb tells someone not to do something; 别…了 tells them to stop.
pattern: 别 + verb + 了 (stop doing it)
body: A negative imperative uses 别 (do not) before the verb: 别着急, 你别走！ The subject 你 is often left out but may stay. 别…了 tells someone to stop what they are doing: 别哭了, 别看电视了，快睡觉吧.
别 is only for commands. For a past fact use 没: 你没走 means you did not leave, which is a statement, not a command; 没着急 or 没哭了 as commands are wrong.
The contrast example uses 不要: 上课的时候不要说话. 别 and 不要 both command someone not to act; 不要 is fuller and more formal, while 别 is short and colloquial.

examples.reading: bié zháojí, mànmàn shuō.
examples.translation: Do not worry; take your time.

examples.reading: bié kàn diànshì le, kuài shuìjiào ba.
examples.translation: Stop watching TV and go to bed.

examples.reading: nǐ bié zǒu!
examples.translation: Do not go!

examples.reading: shàngkè de shíhou búyào shuōhuà.
examples.translation: Do not talk in class.

examples.reading: bié kū le!
examples.translation: Stop crying!

lessons.title: 是 for explanation and characteristics
lessons.summary: 是 plus a quality or category explains what something is like: 这个苹果是甜的.
body: 是 can explain a characteristic or category, often with 的 at the end: 这个苹果是甜的, 这件衣服是毛的, 这张桌子是新的, 他是教书的. It states a fact about the subject rather than an action.
Do not confuse it with the 是……的 that stresses when, where or how a past event happened (我是昨天到的, Level 2 是……的句): here there is no event, only a description. 有 cannot replace 是 here: 这个苹果有甜的 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个苹果很甜. 很 describes the degree; 是…的 affirms the quality as a fact or classification. They are close in meaning but not interchangeable in structure.

examples.reading: zhège píngguǒ shì tián de.
examples.translation: This apple is sweet.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu shì máo de.
examples.translation: This garment is made of wool.

examples.reading: tā shì jiāoshū de.
examples.translation: He is a teacher by profession.

examples.reading: zhège píngguǒ hěn tián.
examples.translation: This apple is very sweet.

examples.reading: zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì xīn de.
examples.translation: This table is new.

lessons.title: 有 + quantity: reaching a measure
lessons.summary: 有 plus a quantity says how deep, long or high something is.
body: 有 with a quantity states that something reaches an extent: 这条河有十米深, 这座山有一千米高, 我弟弟已经有一米八了. It says the thing reaches that measure. To ask, use 有多 + adjective: 你有多高？
The contrast example uses 很: 这条河很深. 很 only says the degree (very deep); 有 + quantity gives a measured amount, so 很十米深 is wrong.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo hé yǒu shí mǐ shēn.
examples.translation: This river is ten metres deep.

examples.text: 我弟弟已经有一米八了。
examples.reading: wǒ dìdi yǐjīng yǒu yì mǐ bā le.
examples.translation: My younger brother is already 1.8 metres tall.

examples.reading: zhè zuò shān yǒu yì qiān mǐ gāo.
examples.translation: This mountain is one thousand metres high.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
examples.translation: This river is very deep.

examples.reading: nǐ yǒu duō gāo?
examples.translation: How tall are you?

lessons.title: Existential sentences: place + verb + 着 + noun
lessons.summary: A place plus a verb with 着 says something is there: 桌子上放着一本书.
body: Place words start the sentence, then a verb with 着, then the thing: 桌子上放着一本书, 墙上挂着一幅画, 门口站着一个人, 教室里坐着很多学生. 着 marks a state, and the thing after it is indefinite, so use 一本 / 一个 / 很多, not 这 / 那.
Do not put 在 after the verb in this pattern: 桌子上放在一本书 is wrong; 在 is used the other way round (书放在桌子上).
The contrast example uses 在: 妹妹在画画儿. An existential sentence describes what is at a place (a state); 在 + verb describes an action happening now.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: There is a book on the table.

examples.reading: qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
examples.translation: There is a picture on the wall.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí ge rén.
examples.translation: Someone is standing at the door.

examples.reading: mèimei zài huà huàr.
examples.translation: My younger sister is drawing.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li zuò zhe hěn duō xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are many students sitting in the classroom.

lessons.title: Comparisons: A 比 B …
lessons.summary: 比 compares two things; 没有 says not as … as; with a verb use 得.
pattern: A + 比 + B + adj (+ 多了 / 一点儿 / 数量)
A + 没有 + B (+ 这么 / 那么) + adj
A + 比 + B + V + 得 + adj; A + V + 得 + 比 + B + adj
body: 比 (bǐ) puts the standard after it: 他比我高. After the adjective you can add the size of the difference: 今天比昨天冷多了, 我比弟弟大两岁. To say A is not as … as B, use 没有, often with 这么 / 那么: 我的房间没有你的那么大; to say A reaches B, use 有: 他有我这么高.
With a verb and 得, 比 B can come before the verb or after 得: 妹妹跑得比我快, 他唱歌比我唱得好. The most common mistake is adding 很 or 非常: 他比我很高 is wrong; say 他比我高多了 or 高一点儿. Also 跟 cannot replace 比: 他跟我高 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 一样: 他和我一样高. 比 shows a difference; 一样 says the two are equal.

examples.reading: tā bǐ wǒ gāo.
examples.translation: He is taller than me.

examples.reading: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.translation: Today is much colder than yesterday.

examples.reading: wǒ méiyǒu gēge gāo.
examples.translation: I am not as tall as my older brother.

examples.reading: tā hé wǒ yíyàng gāo.
examples.translation: He is as tall as me.

examples.reading: mèimei pǎo de bǐ wǒ kuài.
examples.translation: My younger sister runs faster than me.

examples.text: 我的房间没有你的那么大。
examples.reading: wǒ de fángjiān méiyǒu nǐ de nàme dà.
examples.translation: My room is not as big as yours.

examples.reading: tā chàng gē bǐ wǒ chàng de hǎo.
examples.translation: He sings better than me.

lessons.title: 是……的: emphasizing details of an event
lessons.summary: 是……的 stresses when, where, how or who did something: 我是昨天到的.
body: 是……的 emphasizes a detail of a past event: when (我是昨天到的), how (他是坐火车来的), where (我是在书店买的) or who did it (这个菜是妈妈做的). In the affirmative the 是 can be dropped; the 的 stays. Use it to answer when / where / how / who questions about an event that is already known to have happened.

The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 是……的 emphasizes the detail of a known event; 了 simply reports that the action was completed. Both 我昨天去了北京 and 昨天我去了北京 are possible orders, so the word-order exercise is skipped for that example.

examples.reading: wǒ shì zuótiān dào de.
examples.translation: I arrived yesterday.

examples.reading: tā shì zuò huǒchē lái de.
examples.translation: He came by train.

examples.reading: wǒ shì zài shūdiàn mǎi de.
examples.translation: I bought it at the bookshop.

examples.reading: wǒ zuótiān qù le Běijīng.
examples.translation: I went to Beijing yesterday.

examples.reading: zhège cài shì māma zuò de.
examples.translation: This dish was made by Mum.

lessons.title: Pivotal sentences: 请 叫 让 someone do something
lessons.summary: 请/叫/让 take a person, and that person does the next verb: 请他来, 让我走.
body: In a pivotal sentence the object of 请 / 叫 / 让 is also the subject of the next verb: 老师请我们回答问题, 妈妈叫我早点睡, 医生让他多休息. Keep the order verb + person + action: 让他休息, never 让休息他.

The contrast example is a serial-verb sentence: 我去朋友家吃饭. There 我 does both actions (去 and 吃); after 请 / 叫 / 让 it is the person named who does the second action. That is why 让 cannot fill the gap in 我去朋友家吃饭.

examples.reading: lǎoshī qǐng wǒmen huídá wèntí.
examples.translation: The teacher asked us to answer the question.

examples.reading: māma jiào wǒ zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.translation: Mum told me to go to bed early.

examples.reading: tā ràng wǒ xiān zǒu.
examples.translation: He let me leave first.

examples.reading: wǒ qù péngyou jiā chī fàn.
examples.translation: I am going to a friend's place for a meal.

examples.reading: yīshēng ràng tā duō xiūxi.
examples.translation: The doctor told him to rest more.

lessons.title: Double objects with 给: send someone something
lessons.summary: S + V + 给 + person + thing: 他寄给我一个包裹.
body: With verbs such as 送, 寄, 借 and 还, put 给 right after the verb and before the person: 他送给我一张票, 他借给我一本书, 他还给我五十块钱. The thing follows the person; 给 marks the receiver. 对 cannot do this job: 寄对我 is wrong.

The contrast example uses 把: 他把书给了我. The 把 construction (Level 3) moves the thing before the verb; the 给 double-object sentence keeps person and thing after the verb. In speech the thing can also come before 给 (他借一本书给我), so these sentences have more than one possible order.

examples.reading: tā jì gěi wǒ yí ge bāoguǒ.
examples.translation: He sent me a parcel.

examples.reading: wǒ jiè gěi tóngxué yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I lent a classmate a book.

examples.text: 朋友送给我一张电影票。
examples.reading: péngyou sòng gěi wǒ yì zhāng diànyǐng piào.
examples.translation: A friend gave me a cinema ticket.

examples.reading: tā bǎ shū gěi le wǒ.
examples.translation: He gave the book to me.

examples.reading: tā huán gěi wǒ wǔshí kuài qián.
examples.translation: He paid me back fifty kuai.

lessons.title: Alternative complex sentences: 是……，还是……
lessons.summary: (是) A，还是 B offers two clauses as choices.
body: (是)……，还是…… joins two clauses as choices: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？ 我们是今天走，还是明天走？ It is the sentence form of the A还是B? question, and the answer is one clause.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你明天走吗？ 吗 asks for yes or no; 是…还是… asks the listener to pick one of two clauses.

examples.text: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zài jiā kàn shū, háishi qù túshūguǎn?
examples.translation: Will you read at home, or go to the library?

examples.text: 我们是今天走，还是明天走？
examples.reading: wǒmen shì jīntiān zǒu, háishi míngtiān zǒu?
examples.translation: Shall we leave today, or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn, háishi miàntiáo?
examples.translation: Would you like rice, or noodles?

examples.reading: nǐ míngtiān zǒu ma?
examples.translation: Are you leaving tomorrow?

examples.text: 你是自己去，还是我们送你去？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zìjǐ qù, háishi wǒmen sòng nǐ qù?
examples.translation: Are you going on your own, or shall we take you?

lessons.title: Concessive sentences: 虽然……，但是……
lessons.summary: 虽然 admits a fact, 但是 turns to the opposite result.
body: 虽然 (suīrán) concedes something; 但是 turns to the unexpected: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好; 虽然下雨了，但是他还是来了. 虽然 can stand before or after the subject (他的家虽然不大), and 但是 belongs at the head of the second clause. 所以 cannot be paired with 虽然.
The contrast example uses 因为…所以…: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了. 虽然…但是… links concession and turn; 因为…所以… links cause and result, so 因为 and 虽然 cannot replace each other.

examples.text: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn guì, dànshì zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: It is expensive, but the quality is good.

examples.text: 虽然下雨了，但是他还是来了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ le, dànshì tā háishi lái le.
examples.translation: Although it was raining, he still came.

examples.text: 虽然他很累，但是还在工作。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still working.

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.translation: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.

examples.text: 他的家虽然不大，但是很干净。
examples.reading: tā de jiā suīrán bú dà, dànshì hěn gānjìng.
examples.translation: His home is not big, but it is very clean.

lessons.title: Cause and result: 因为……，所以……
lessons.summary: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result.
body: 因为…所以… links a reason and its result: 因为今天是周末，所以图书馆人很多; 因为妈妈病了，所以我没去学校. 因为 can stand alone in an answer, and 所以 introduces the second clause. Do not use 但是 for a result: 因为太累了，但是… is wrong.
The contrast example uses 虽然…但是…: 虽然他很忙，但是每天都运动. A causal sentence says one thing caused another; a concessive sentence admits a fact and turns against it.

examples.text: 因为路很远，所以我们坐车去。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lù hěn yuǎn, suǒyǐ wǒmen zuò chē qù.
examples.translation: Because it is a long way, we are going by car.

examples.text: 因为今天是周末，所以图书馆人很多。
examples.reading: yīnwèi jīntiān shì zhōumò, suǒyǐ túshūguǎn rén hěn duō.
examples.translation: Because it is the weekend, the library is crowded.

examples.text: 因为妈妈病了，所以我没去学校。
examples.reading: yīnwèi māma bìng le, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: Because Mum was ill, I did not go to school.

examples.text: 虽然他很忙，但是每天都运动。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn máng, dànshì měi tiān dōu yùndòng.
examples.translation: Although he is busy, he exercises every day.

examples.text: 因为作业太多了，所以他很晚才睡。
examples.reading: yīnwèi zuòyè tài duō le, suǒyǐ tā hěn wǎn cái shuì.
examples.translation: He had too much homework, so he went to bed very late.

lessons.title: 一……就……: as soon as
lessons.summary: 一……就… links two immediate actions: 我一放学就回家。
body: 一……就…… says the second action follows the first immediately: 他一回家就睡觉了; 老师一说，我就明白了. The subjects may be the same or different; 一 stands right before the first verb and 就 right before the second. The partner of 一 is always 就, never 才.
The contrast example uses 先……再……: 我们先去超市，再回家. 一…就… stresses that there is no gap; 先…再… only lists steps in order.

examples.reading: wǒ yí fàngxué jiù huí jiā.
examples.translation: As soon as school finishes, I go home.

examples.reading: tā yì huí jiā jiù shuìjiào le.
examples.translation: As soon as he got home, he went to sleep.

examples.reading: tā yí kàn shū jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.
examples.translation: As soon as he starts reading, he feels sleepy.

examples.reading: wǒmen xiān qù chāoshì, zài huí jiā.
examples.translation: We will go to the supermarket first, then go home.

examples.reading: lǎoshī yì shuō, wǒ jiù míngbai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the teacher explained, I understood.

lessons.title: 持续态: verb + 着
lessons.summary: 着 after a verb says a state continues or an action keeps going.
body: 着 marks that a state continues (树上挂着很多苹果, 床上躺着一只猫) or that an action keeps going (外面下着雨). V1 + 着 + V2 says how the second action is done: 他坐着看书, 我们走着去吧. It often describes how things are, especially a background scene.
The contrast example uses 在: 哥哥在打篮球. 着 presents a held state or continuation; 在 presents an action in progress at this moment. 在 cannot follow the verb in these sentences: 他坐在看书 is wrong.

examples.reading: shù shàng guà zhe hěn duō píngguǒ.
examples.translation: Many apples are hanging on the tree.

examples.reading: tā zuò zhe kàn shū.
examples.translation: He sits reading.

examples.reading: chuáng shàng tǎng zhe yì zhī māo.
examples.translation: A cat is lying on the bed.

examples.reading: gēge zài dǎ lánqiú.
examples.translation: My older brother is playing basketball.

examples.reading: wàimian xià zhe yǔ.
examples.translation: It is raining outside.

examples.reading: wǒmen zǒu zhe qù ba.
examples.translation: Let us go on foot.

lessons.title: 经历态: verb + 过
lessons.summary: 过 says someone has had the experience at least once: 我去过中国。
body: As an aspect, 过 says an action has been experienced at some time: 我爸爸当过老师, 你坐过飞机吗？ Negate with 没 and keep 过: 我没喝过中国茶, 我从来没见过这么大的西瓜. In the negative, 了 cannot replace 过 (没见了 is wrong).
过 stresses the experience; to simply report what happened on a given occasion, use 了 (我昨天去了北京). 过 can still appear with a time word when the point is the experience: 我昨天去过他家，他不在.
The contrast example uses 了: 下课了，我们走吧. This 了 says a new situation has begun; 过 cannot replace it, because the class ending is not an experience.

examples.reading: wǒ bàba dāng guo lǎoshī.
examples.translation: My dad used to be a teacher.

examples.reading: nǐ zuò guo fēijī ma?
examples.translation: Have you ever flown?

examples.reading: wǒ méi hē guo Zhōngguó chá.
examples.translation: I have never had Chinese tea.

examples.reading: xià kè le, wǒmen zǒu ba.
examples.translation: Class is over; let us go.

examples.text: 我从来没见过这么大的西瓜。
examples.reading: wǒ cónglái méi jiàn guo zhème dà de xīguā.
examples.translation: I have never seen such a big watermelon.

lessons.title: Number + measure: floors, classes, grades
lessons.summary: A number plus a measure names an ordered item: 二楼, 三班, 五年级.
pattern: numeral + measure (+ noun): 二楼, 三班
numeral + 年级 / 层 / 号
body: To name floors, classes, grades and rooms, put the number directly before the word, without 第: 二楼, 三班, 五年级, 四号房间. This is a label for an ordered unit, not a count of things: 三楼 means the third floor, not three floors.
Because it is a label, use 二, never 两: 二楼 and 二班, not 两楼 or 两班. (两 is only for counting: 两个人.)
The contrast example uses 第: 我的座位在第五排. 第 + number gives the position in a row or sequence; number + word names a fixed label such as a floor or a class.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā zài sān lóu.
examples.translation: My home is on the third floor.

examples.reading: wǒmen shì èr bān de xuéshēng.
examples.translation: We are students in Class 2.

examples.reading: wǒ shàng wǔ niánjí.
examples.translation: I am in grade five.

examples.reading: wǒ de zuòwèi zài dì-wǔ pái.
examples.translation: My seat is in the fifth row.

examples.reading: qǐng dào èr lóu lái.
examples.translation: Please come up to the second floor.

lessons.title: Approximate numbers: 几, 十多, 一年多
lessons.summary: 几 gives a small approximate number; 多 after a number or a measure means more than.
body: 几 (jǐ) in a statement means a few or some (under ten): 我有几个苹果, 十几个男生. 多 after a round number means more than: 十多个学生, 两百多块. 多 after the measure means more than that many whole units, with a part left over: 一年多, 五个多月. Do not say 三个多人: people come only in whole units.
The contrast example uses 多少: 你们班有多少人？ 几 suggests a small amount and needs a measure word; 多少 asks about any amount and can go straight before the noun.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu jǐ ge píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I have a few apples.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li yǒu shí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are more than ten students in the classroom.

examples.reading: tā zài Běijīng zhù le yì nián duō.
examples.translation: He lived in Beijing for more than a year.

examples.reading: nǐmen bān yǒu duōshao rén?
examples.translation: How many people are there in your class?

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu liǎng bǎi duō kuài.
examples.translation: This garment costs over two hundred kuai.

examples.reading: wǒmen bān yǒu shí jǐ ge nánshēng.
examples.translation: There are a dozen or so boys in our class.

lessons.title: 老-: a prefix for familiar names, birth order and some nouns
lessons.summary: 老 before a surname makes a friendly form of address, before a number gives birth order among siblings, and is a fixed part of some nouns such as 老师 and 老虎.
pattern: 老 + 大 / 二 / 三 …
老 + noun root (老师, 老虎, 老家)
body: 老 (lǎo) is a prefix with three common jobs. Before a one-syllable surname it makes a friendly, familiar way to address or mention someone of your age or older: 老王, 老张, 老李. Before 大, 二, 三 and so on it gives the order of children in a family: 老大 is the eldest, 老二 the second, 老三 the third. In some nouns it is simply part of the word and adds no idea of age: 老师 (teacher), 老虎 (tiger, even a baby one), 老家 (hometown), 老板 (boss).
The contrast example uses 小 (Level 1): 小李. 小 + surname is the friendly form for someone younger than you; 老 + surname is for someone your age or older. Both attach to the surname only.
Common mistake: putting 老 before a full name or a given name (老王小明). Say 老王, or the full name without 老.

examples.reading: Lǎo Zhāng shì wǒmen de jīnglǐ.
examples.translation: Old Zhang is our manager.

examples.reading: tā shì jiā li de lǎodà.
examples.translation: He is the eldest child in the family.

examples.translation: My hometown is in the south.

examples.translation: Xiao Li is the colleague who just joined.

lessons.title: Suffixes -家, -子 and -员: experts, everyday nouns and staff
lessons.summary: -家 marks an expert or artist, -子 is a common noun ending, and -员 marks a person who does a job or belongs to a group.
pattern: field + 家 (画家, 科学家)
root + 子 (桌子, 帽子, 儿子)
activity + 员 (服务员, 运动员)
body: A suffix attaches to the back of a word. 家 (jiā) after a field names a recognised expert or artist: 画家 (painter), 科学家 (scientist), 音乐家 (musician), 作家 (writer). 子 (zi, neutral tone) is a common ending of everyday nouns: 桌子, 椅子, 帽子, 儿子, 孩子, 筷子. 员 (yuán) names a person who does a job or is a member: 服务员 (waiter), 运动员 (athlete), 演员 (actor), 售货员 (shop assistant).
The contrast example uses 们 (Level 1), which makes a person-noun plural: 演员们. 们 can follow a noun that already has 员 or 家; it adds the idea of many people, not a job.
Common mistake: swapping the suffixes. 家 is for a respected expert (科学家, not 科学员); 员 is for a staff member or player (服务员, not 服务家).

examples.reading: tā bàba shì yí wèi huàjiā.
examples.translation: His father is a painter.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng dāng kēxuéjiā.
examples.translation: I want to be a scientist.

examples.translation: Waiter, please give me a pair of chopsticks.

examples.reading: tā shì yì míng yóuyǒng yùndòngyuán.
examples.translation: She is a swimmer (a swimming athlete).

examples.translation: Where is my hat?

examples.reading: tāmen de érzi jīnnián wǔ suì.
examples.translation: Their son is five this year.

examples.reading: yǎnyuánmen dōu hěn lèi.
examples.translation: The actors are all very tired.

lessons.title: Compass words: 东 南 西 北, 北方 南方 东方 西方, and 中间
lessons.summary: 东, 南, 西 and 北 combine with 边 for a side of a place and with 方 for a direction or region; 中间 means in the middle or between.
pattern: N + 的 + 东边 / 南边 / 西边 / 北边
东方 / 南方 / 西方 / 北方 (+ 的 + N)
在 + A 和 B + 中间
body: 东 (dōng, east), 南 (nán, south), 西 (xī, west) and 北 (běi, north) are bound words. After a place noun they take 边: 学校的东边, 城市的北边. With 方 they name a direction or a large region: 北方 (the north of a country), 南方, 东方 (the east; also the East), 西方 (the west; also the West, Western countries). Compound directions put east or west first: 东南, 西北.
中间 (zhōngjiān) is the middle of something or the space between two things: 在超市和书店中间. 中 alone does not work as a place word here.

The contrast example uses 右 (Level 2): 往右走. 左 and 右 give direction relative to the speaker, while the compass words give a fixed direction. Common mistake: using a bare compass word or 方 for a side of a small place (中国的北, 超市东方). Use 北方 for a region and 东边 for the side of a building.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā zài chéngshì de běibian.
examples.translation: My home is on the north side of the city.

examples.translation: Western holidays are different from Chinese ones.

examples.reading: dōngfāng de tiān yǐjīng liàng le.
examples.translation: The sky in the east is already light.

examples.translation: Please go right; the bank is just there.

lessons.title: Modal verbs 需要, 应该/该, 愿意 and 得 (děi)
lessons.summary: 需要 says something is needed, 应该 and 该 say what is right or expected, 愿意 says someone is willing, and 得 (děi) says you have to.
pattern: A + 应该 / 该 / 得 + V
body: 需要 (xūyào) means need. It can take a verb (你需要多休息) or a noun (我需要一张地图), and its subject can be a thing: 这个问题需要好好想一想. 应该 (yīnggāi) and the shorter, more spoken 该 (gāi) say what is right or expected: 你应该早点儿告诉我, 你不该这么晚才回家. 愿意 (yuànyì) says a person is willing, and it can take 很: 我很愿意帮助你.
得 (děi) is spoken and means have to: 我得早点儿睡. It is written like the particle 得 (de) but read děi and stands before a verb. Its negative is 不用 (no need), not 不得.

The contrast example uses 会 (Level 1) for a prediction: 明天会下雨吗？ 会 can talk about weather; 愿意 cannot, because weather has no will. Common mistake: using 愿意 with a thing as subject, or saying 不得 for no need to.

examples.reading: wǒ xūyào yì zhāng dìtú.
examples.translation: I need a map.

examples.text: 这个问题需要好好想一想。
examples.reading: zhège wèntí xūyào hǎohǎo xiǎng yi xiǎng.
examples.translation: This problem needs careful thought.

examples.reading: nǐ bù gāi zhème wǎn cái huí jiā.
examples.translation: You shouldn't come home so late.

examples.reading: nǐ yīnggāi zǎo diǎnr gàosu wǒ.
examples.translation: You should have told me earlier.

examples.reading: wǒ hěn yuànyì bāngzhù nǐ.
examples.translation: I am very willing to help you.

examples.translation: There's an exam tomorrow, so I have to go to bed early.

examples.translation: Will it rain tomorrow?

lessons.title: Separable verbs: 放假 见面 结婚 洗澡 and 离开 完成 分开
lessons.summary: Verb-object words like 见面 open up for 了, 过, a measure or 的; verb-complement words like 离开 open up for 得 or 不.
pattern: V + 了 / 过 / 个 / number + measure + O (见过一次面)
V + 得 / 不 + C (离不开, 完得成)
body: Verb-object separable words have a verb part and an object part. 放假 (have a holiday), 见面 (meet), 结婚 (marry) and 洗澡 (take a bath) let other words go between the two parts: 放了一个星期的假, 见过一次面, 是去年结的婚, 洗个澡. Because the word already contains an object, it cannot take another one: say 跟他见面, not 见面他.
Verb-complement words have a verb and a result: 离开 (leave), 完成 (finish), 分开 (separate). 得 or 不 goes between the parts to say can or cannot: 离得开 / 离不开, 完得成 / 完不成, 分不开.

The contrast example uses 帮助, an ordinary verb that takes an object directly: 他经常帮助我. 帮忙 (Level 2) is separable and cannot: 他经常帮忙我 is wrong, 他经常帮我的忙 is right. Common mistake: putting the object or the measure after the whole word, as in 见面他 or 见面一次.

examples.text: 学校放了一个星期的假。
examples.reading: xuéxiào fàng le yí ge xīngqī de jià.
examples.translation: The school had a week's holiday.

examples.reading: wǒmen liǎ zhǐ jiàn guo liǎng cì miàn.

examples.translation: The two of them are very close; they can't be separated.

examples.reading: tā jīngcháng bāngzhù wǒ.
examples.translation: He often helps me.

lessons.title: 怎样: asking how, in what way and what kind
lessons.summary: 怎样 asks about manner before a verb, about a state at the end of a sentence, and about kind before 的 + noun.
body: 怎样 (zěnyàng) is a slightly more formal partner of 怎么 and 怎么样. Before a verb it asks how something is done: 这个字怎样写？ 我们应该怎样学好汉语？ At the end of a sentence it asks about a state or an opinion: 你最近身体怎样？ 你看这件衣服怎样？ Before 的 and a noun it asks what kind: 他是一个怎样的人？
The contrast example uses 怎么 for surprise or why: 你怎么又迟到了？ 怎么 can ask why or how come; 怎样 only asks how or what kind, so 你怎样又迟到了 is wrong.
Common mistake: using 怎么 before 的 (一个怎么的人). Before 的 + noun use 怎样 or 怎么样.

examples.reading: zhège zì zěnyàng xiě?
examples.translation: How do you write this character?

examples.reading: nǐ zuìjìn shēntǐ zěnyàng?
examples.translation: How has your health been lately?

examples.reading: tā shì yí ge zěnyàng de rén?
examples.translation: What kind of person is he?

examples.text: 我们应该怎样学好汉语？
examples.reading: wǒmen yīnggāi zěnyàng xuéhǎo Hànyǔ?
examples.translation: How should we learn Chinese well?

examples.reading: nǐ kàn zhè jiàn yīfu zěnyàng?
examples.translation: What do you think of this piece of clothing?

examples.reading: nǐ zěnme yòu chídào le?
examples.translation: How come you're late again?

lessons.title: Question words without a question: anything, anyone, anywhere and something
lessons.summary: A question word followed by 都 or 也 means any or every (什么都, 谁都); the same word twice links two clauses; and in a statement a question word can mean something, somewhere or someone.
pattern: QW + 都 / 也 + (不 / 没) + V
V + 点儿 + 什么 / 在哪儿 + V
body: A question word does not always ask a question. Before 都 or 也 it means any or every, and with 不 or 没 it means nothing, nobody or nowhere: 他什么都不想吃, 谁都知道这件事, 周末我哪儿也没去, 怎么走都可以. The question word comes before 都 or 也, in front of the verb.

The same question word can appear in two clauses, linked by 就, and the two refer to the same thing: 你想吃什么就吃什么 (eat whatever you want). In a statement a question word can also stand for something, somewhere or someone not named: 吃点儿什么吧, 我好像在哪儿见过他.

The contrast example is an ordinary question: 你周末去哪儿了？ Here 哪儿 asks for a place and needs an answer. With 都 or 也, in the double pattern, or in a statement, the question word asks nothing. Common mistake: leaving the question word after the verb (我都不想吃什么); say 我什么都不想吃.

examples.reading: tā shénme dōu bù xiǎng chī.
examples.translation: He doesn't want to eat anything.

examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ nǎr yě méi qù.
examples.translation: I didn't go anywhere at the weekend.

examples.reading: wǒ hǎoxiàng zài nǎr jiàn guo tā.
examples.translation: I seem to have seen him somewhere.

examples.text: 你饿了就吃点儿什么吧。
examples.reading: nǐ è le jiù chī diǎnr shénme ba.
examples.translation: If you're hungry, eat something.

examples.translation: Where did you go at the weekend?

lessons.title: 别人 (other people) and 咱们 (we, including you)
lessons.summary: 别人 means other people and stands alone as a pronoun; 咱们 means we and always includes the person you are speaking to.
body: 别人 (biéren) means other people, anyone except the person in question. It works like a pronoun: as subject (别人都走了), as object (他总是想着别人) and before 的 (别人的东西). 咱们 (zánmen) means we and always includes the listener; it is common in spoken northern Chinese: 咱们一起去吃饭吧, 咱们班.
The contrast example uses 我们 (Level 1): 老师，我们先走了，您慢慢吃. The speakers leave and the teacher stays, so the listener is not included and 咱们 is wrong; 我们 can include or exclude the listener.
Common mistake: using 别的 for people on its own (别的都走了 for other people left). 别的 needs a noun or means other things; for people say 别人 or 别的人.

examples.text: 这是别人的东西，你不能拿。
examples.reading: zhè shì biéren de dōngxi, nǐ bù néng ná.
examples.translation: This belongs to someone else; you can't take it.

examples.reading: zánmen yìqǐ qù chī fàn ba.
examples.translation: Let's go and eat together.

examples.text: 别人都走了，只有他还在。
examples.reading: biéren dōu zǒu le, zhǐyǒu tā hái zài.
examples.translation: Everyone else has left; only he is still here.

examples.text: 咱们班的同学都很友好。
examples.reading: zánmen bān de tóngxué dōu hěn yǒuhǎo.
examples.translation: The students in our class are all friendly.

examples.text: 你要多听听别人的意见。
examples.reading: nǐ yào duō tīngting biéren de yìjiàn.
examples.translation: You should listen more to other people's opinions.

examples.text: 老师，我们先走了，您慢慢吃。
examples.reading: lǎoshī, wǒmen xiān zǒu le, nín mànmàn chī.
examples.translation: Teacher, we're leaving now; take your time eating.

lessons.title: 别的 and 其他: other things, other people
lessons.summary: 别的 and 其他 both mean other; 别的 can stand alone for other things, and 其他 often means the rest of a known group.
pattern: 除了 A，其他 + N + 都…
body: 别的 (bié de) means other. It goes before a noun (别的颜色) or stands alone for other things (你还想要别的吗？). 其他 (qítā) also means other and usually points to the rest of a known group: 其他同学都回家了, 除了小王，其他人都来了. Used alone it takes 的: 其他的都没买.
The contrast example uses 别人 (row 7): 我没有把这件事告诉别人. For other people, 别人 is the pronoun; 别的 and 其他 need a noun such as 人 to mean people.
Common mistake: putting 别人 before a noun as if it meant other (别人颜色). Use 别的颜色 or 其他颜色.

examples.reading: nǐ hái xiǎng yào bié de ma?
examples.translation: Would you like anything else?

examples.text: 我不喜欢这个颜色，有别的颜色吗？
examples.reading: wǒ bù xǐhuan zhège yánsè, yǒu bié de yánsè ma?
examples.translation: I don't like this colour; do you have another colour?

examples.reading: qítā tóngxué dōu huí jiā le.
examples.translation: The other students have all gone home.

examples.text: 除了小王，其他人都来了。
examples.reading: chúle Xiǎo Wáng, qítā rén dōu lái le.

examples.text: 我只买了水果，其他的都没买。

examples.text: 我没有把这件事告诉别人。
examples.reading: wǒ méiyǒu bǎ zhè jiàn shì gàosu biéren.

lessons.title: Measure words for objects, places, vehicles and speech: 把 双 张 种 层 封 页 辆 节 所 班 段 头 句
lessons.summary: Each measure word goes between a number or 这/那 and a noun, and fits a kind of thing: 把 for things with handles, 张 for flat things, 辆 for vehicles, 句 for sentences.
pattern: number / 这 / 那 + measure + N
一把雨伞, 两张票, 几辆车, 一句话
body: 把 (bǎ) is for things you hold by a handle: 一把雨伞, 一把椅子. 双 (shuāng) is a pair: 一双鞋, 一双筷子. 张 (zhāng) is for flat things: 一张票, 一张纸, 一张桌子. 种 (zhǒng) is a kind: 这种楼. 层 (céng) is a floor or layer: 六层. 封 (fēng) is for letters, 页 (yè) for pages: 一封三页的信. 辆 (liàng) is for vehicles: 几辆车.

节 (jié) counts class periods: 这节课. 所 (suǒ) is for schools and hospitals: 那所大学. 班 (bān) counts scheduled runs of a bus, train or plane: 下一班车. 段 (duàn) is a stretch or section: 这段路, 这段话. 头 (tóu) is for large animals: 一头牛. 句 (jù) counts sentences: 一句话.

The contrast example uses 位 (Level 2), the polite measure for people: 一位新同学. In the same sentence 班 is a noun (a class of students), not the measure word for runs of a bus. Common mistake: using 个 or the wrong measure for vehicles and animals (一个车, 一张牛); say 一辆车, 一头牛.

examples.text: 外面下雨了，你带一把雨伞吧。

examples.translation: This kind of building usually has six floors.

examples.reading: dì yī jié kè bā diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The first class starts at eight.

examples.text: 这封信有三页，是那所大学寄来的。
examples.reading: zhè fēng xìn yǒu sān yè, shì nà suǒ dàxué jìlai de.
examples.translation: This letter is three pages long; that university sent it.

examples.text: 路上有一头牛，后面的几辆车都停下来了。
examples.reading: lù shang yǒu yì tóu niú, hòumian de jǐ liàng chē dōu tíng xiàlai le.
examples.translation: There was a cow on the road, and the cars behind it all stopped.

examples.text: 这段话里有一句我不懂。
examples.reading: zhè duàn huà li yǒu yí jù wǒ bù dǒng.

examples.reading: wǒmen bān yǒu yí wèi xīn tóngxué.
examples.translation: There is a new student in our class.

lessons.title: Units and borrowed measures: 公斤 斤 角 毛 刻 米, 碗 盘
lessons.summary: 公斤 and 斤 weigh, 角 and 毛 count tenths of a yuan, 刻 is a quarter of an hour, 米 is a metre, and 碗 and 盘 borrow a bowl and a plate as measures.
pattern: number + 公斤 / 斤 / 米 (+ N)
…块 / 元 + number + 毛 / 角
body: 公斤 (gōngjīn) is a kilogram and 斤 (jīn) is half a kilogram, the usual unit in Chinese markets: 两斤苹果. 米 (mǐ) is a metre; height is said 一米八 (1.8 metres). 刻 (kè) is a quarter of an hour: 三点一刻 (3:15), 三点三刻 (3:45).
Money: 1 元 = 10 角 = 100 分. In speech 块 replaces 元 and 毛 replaces 角: 三块五毛 in speech, 三元五角 in writing. Borrowed measures use a container: 一碗米饭, 一盘饺子.

The contrast example uses 分钟 (Level 1): 二十分钟. 分 counts minutes and goes with any number; 刻 only counts quarters, so you say 一刻 or 三刻, never 二十刻. Common mistake: mixing spoken and written money words (三元五毛). Keep 块 with 毛 and 元 with 角.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng mǎi liǎng jīn píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I'd like to buy a kilo of apples.

examples.reading: zhège xiāngzi yǒu èrshí gōngjīn.
examples.translation: This suitcase weighs twenty kilos.

examples.reading: yí ge miànbāo sān kuài wǔ máo.
examples.translation: A loaf of bread costs three yuan fifty.

examples.reading: zhè zhāng piào sān yuán wǔ jiǎo.
examples.translation: This ticket costs 3.50 yuan.

examples.reading: xiànzài shì sān diǎn yí kè.
examples.translation: It is a quarter past three.

lessons.title: Measures for actions: 口, 回, 遍 and 声
lessons.summary: After a verb, 口 counts mouthfuls, 回 counts times, 遍 counts complete runs from start to end, and 声 counts sounds or short spoken words.
pattern: V + (了) + number + 口 / 回 / 遍 / 声 (+ O)
body: A verbal measure counts how many times an action happens. 口 (kǒu) counts mouthfuls: 喝了一口茶, 尝了一口. 回 (huí) is a spoken word for times, like 次: 我去过两回. 遍 (biàn) counts a complete run from beginning to end: 读三遍, 看了两遍. 声 (shēng) counts a sound or a short word: 笑了一声, 跟我说一声 (let me know).
The number and measure follow the verb (and 了 or 过). A noun object usually comes after them (喝了一口茶), but a pronoun comes before them: 叫了我一声.

The contrast example uses 次 (Level 2): 游三次泳. 次 simply counts occurrences; 遍 adds the idea of doing the whole thing through, so 游三遍泳 is wrong. Common mistake: using 遍 for going somewhere (去过两遍上海); say 两次 or 两回.

examples.reading: tā hē le yì kǒu chá.
examples.translation: He took a sip of tea.

examples.text: 老师让我们把课文读三遍。

examples.translation: The teacher had us read the text three times.

examples.reading: nà jiā fànguǎn wǒ qù guo liǎng huí.

examples.translation: She gave a laugh and said nothing.

examples.translation: I had a taste; it was too spicy.

examples.translation: I go swimming three times a week.

lessons.title: Doubled measure words: 个个, 张张 mean every single one
lessons.summary: A doubled measure word such as 个个 or 张张 means every one of them; it stands before the verb, usually with 都.
pattern: 个个 / 张张 / 本本 / 样样 / 天天
body: Doubling a measure word gives the meaning every single one: 同学个个都很努力, 照片张张都很好看. The same works with other measures: 本本 (every book), 样样 (every kind), 件件 (every piece). Time words double the same way: 天天 (every day). The doubled measure comes after the thing it counts and before the verb, and it usually goes with 都.
The contrast example uses 每 (Level 2): 每个人都有自己的爱好. 每 needs a measure word after it and goes before the noun; the doubled measure replaces 每 + measure and follows the noun.
Common mistake: putting the doubled measure after the verb (我喜欢张张照片). Say 这些照片我张张都喜欢 or 每张照片我都喜欢.

examples.text: 我们班的同学个个都很努力。
examples.reading: wǒmen bān de tóngxué gègè dōu hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: Every student in our class works hard.

examples.text: 这些照片张张都很好看。
examples.reading: zhèxiē zhàopiàn zhāngzhāng dōu hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: Every one of these photos is lovely.

examples.reading: tā zuò de cài yàngyàng dōu hǎochī.
examples.translation: Every dish he makes is delicious.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs that compare: 比较, 更, 还 and 越
lessons.summary: 比较 means fairly or relatively, 更 means even more, 还 means even more in a 比 sentence or passably before 不错, and 越……越 means the more … the more.
pattern: A + 比较 / 更 + Adj / V
A + 比 B + 还 + Adj；A + 还 + 不错 / 可以
A + 越 + V + 越 + Adj
body: 比较 (bǐjiào) gives a mild degree, fairly or relatively: 今天比较冷. 更 (gèng) means even more and implies a comparison with something already mentioned: 我喜欢春天，更喜欢秋天. 还 (hái) as a degree adverb has two uses: in a 比 sentence it means even more, often with surprise (今天比昨天还热); before 不错 or 可以 it means passably, not bad (这个饭馆的菜还不错).
越 (yuè) is used twice: 越 + verb + 越 + adjective says one thing grows with another: 他的汉语越说越好. The fixed phrase 越来越 (more and more) is taught with the fixed phrases.

The contrast example uses 最 (Level 2): 他跑得最快. 最 picks the top one in a group; 更 and 还 compare with one other thing. Common mistake: putting 很 or 非常 in a 比 sentence (今天比昨天很热). After 比 use 更 or 还, or nothing.

examples.text: 今天比较冷，多穿点儿衣服。
examples.reading: jīntiān bǐjiào lěng, duō chuān diǎnr yīfu.
examples.translation: It's fairly cold today; put on more clothes.

examples.text: 我喜欢春天，更喜欢秋天。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan chūntiān, gèng xǐhuan qiūtiān.
examples.translation: I like spring, and I like autumn even more.

examples.reading: zhège fànguǎn de cài hái búcuò.
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant is not bad.

examples.reading: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān hái rè.
examples.translation: Today is even hotter than yesterday.

examples.reading: tā de Hànyǔ yuè shuō yuè hǎo.
examples.translation: The more he speaks Chinese, the better it gets.

examples.text: 我们三个人里，他跑得最快。
examples.reading: wǒmen sān ge rén li, tā pǎo de zuì kuài.
examples.translation: Of the three of us, he runs the fastest.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs for strength: 特别, 挺, 有些 and 极
lessons.summary: 特别 means especially or particularly, 挺 is a spoken quite, 有些 means a bit (usually of something unwelcome), and 极 means extremely, before an adjective or in Adj + 极了.
pattern: A + 特别 / 挺 / 有些 / 极 + Adj / V
body: 特别 (tèbié) means very or particularly: 他对我们特别好. 特别是 + noun picks out one member of a group: 我喜欢水果，特别是苹果. 挺 (tǐng) is spoken and means quite; it often has 的 at the end: 这本书挺有意思的.

有些 (yǒuxiē) as an adverb means a bit, like 有点儿, usually for something unwelcome: 我有些担心他. 极 (jí) means extremely. Before an adjective it is formal (这一点极重要); after an adjective, 极了 is spoken and strong: 好极了.

The contrast example uses 有些 as a pronoun (Level 1), meaning some: 有些人不喜欢吃辣的. Before a noun 有些 means some; before an adjective or verb it means a bit. Common mistake: putting 了 after 极 + adjective (极好了). Say 极好 or 好极了.

examples.text: 我喜欢水果，特别是苹果。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan shuǐguǒ, tèbié shì píngguǒ.
examples.translation: I like fruit, especially apples.

examples.reading: tā duì wǒmen tèbié hǎo.
examples.translation: He is especially good to us.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū tǐng yǒu yìsi de.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒuxiē dānxīn tā.
examples.translation: I'm a bit worried about him.

examples.reading: nǐ de zhǔyi hǎo jí le!
examples.translation: Your idea is excellent!

examples.translation: This point is extremely important.

examples.reading: yǒuxiē rén bù xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.translation: Some people don't like spicy food.

lessons.title: Scope adverbs: 就 (only), 一块儿, 一共, 只, 到处 and 只是
lessons.summary: 就 and 只 limit to only, 只是 means merely, 一共 adds up a total, 一块儿 means together, and 到处 means everywhere.
pattern: 就 + N / pronoun / number；A + 只 + V
A + 一共 + number / 多少
A + 一块儿 + V；到处 + 都 + …
body: 就 (jiù) can mean only and stands before a noun, a pronoun or a number: 今天就我一个人在家. 只 (zhǐ) means only and stands before the verb: 我只有一百块钱. 只是 (zhǐshì) means merely, just: 我只是问问. Between clauses 只是 can also mean it's just that, a soft but.
一共 (yígòng) means in total and goes with a number or 多少: 这些东西一共多少钱？ 一块儿 (yíkuàir) is a spoken word for together, like 一起: 咱们一块儿去爬山吧. 到处 (dàochù) means everywhere and usually goes with 都: 到处都是花.

The contrast example uses 都 (Level 1): 这些菜我都喜欢吃. 都 says each of the things mentioned before it; 一共 adds things up to a number, so it needs a number or 多少 after it. Common mistake: putting 只 before a subject (只我知道). Say 只有我知道 or 就我知道.

examples.reading: jīntiān jiù wǒ yí ge rén zài jiā.
examples.translation: Today I'm the only one at home.

examples.reading: zánmen yíkuàir qù pá shān ba.
examples.translation: Let's go climbing together.

examples.reading: zhèxiē dōngxi yígòng duōshao qián?
examples.translation: How much are these things altogether?

examples.translation: I only have a hundred yuan.

examples.reading: chūntiān dào le, dàochù dōu shì huā.
examples.translation: Spring has come and there are flowers everywhere.

examples.translation: I'm just asking; I don't want to buy it.

lessons.title: Time adverbs: 才, 马上, 先, 一会儿, 刚, 刚刚 and 一直
lessons.summary: 才 says later than expected, 马上 right away, 先 first, 一会儿 in a moment, 刚 and 刚刚 just now, and 一直 all along.
pattern: A + 马上 / 一会儿 + (就) + V
A + 刚 / 刚刚 / 一直 / 先 + V
body: 才 (cái) after a time word says the action happened later than expected: 他七点半才到. 马上 (mǎshàng) means right away, often with 就 or 就要: 电影马上就要开始了. 先 (xiān) means first: 你先坐一下. 一会儿 (yíhuìr) before a verb means in a moment: 我一会儿就来; after a verb it means for a while.

刚 (gāng) and 刚刚 (gānggāng) mean just, a very short time ago: 我刚到家. 刚 is an adverb and stays after the subject; 刚刚 can also be a time word and stand before the subject: 刚刚你去哪儿了？ 一直 (yìzhí) means continuously, all along: 雨一直下了三天.

The contrast example uses 已经 (Level 2): 我们已经认识很多年了. 已经 says a point has been reached, however long ago; 刚 says something happened only a moment ago, so it cannot go with 很多年. Common mistake: ending a 刚 sentence with 了 (我刚到家了). Say 我刚到家.

examples.text: 电影七点开始，他七点半才到。
examples.reading: diànyǐng qī diǎn kāishǐ, tā qī diǎn bàn cái dào.
examples.translation: The film started at seven, but he didn't arrive until half past.

examples.reading: diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù yào kāishǐ le.
examples.translation: The film is about to start.

examples.reading: nǐ xiān zuò yíxià, wǒ qù dào chá.
examples.translation: Have a seat first; I'll go and pour some tea.

examples.text: 你等一下，我一会儿就来。
examples.reading: nǐ děng yíxià, wǒ yíhuìr jiù lái.
examples.translation: Wait a moment; I'll be there shortly.

examples.text: 我刚到家，你就打电话来了。
examples.reading: wǒ gāng dào jiā, nǐ jiù dǎ diànhuà lái le.
examples.translation: I had only just got home when you called.

examples.reading: gānggāng nǐ qù nǎr le?
examples.translation: Where did you go just now?

examples.reading: yǔ yìzhí xià le sān tiān.
examples.translation: It rained non-stop for three days.

examples.text: 我们已经认识很多年了。
examples.reading: wǒmen yǐjīng rènshi hěn duō nián le.
examples.translation: We have known each other for many years.

lessons.title: Frequency adverbs: 总, 总是, 常常 and 又
lessons.summary: 总 and 总是 mean always, 常常 means often, and 又 means again for something that has happened or that comes round regularly.
pattern: A + 总 / 总是 / 常常 + V
body: 总 (zǒng) and 总是 (zǒngshì) mean always, every time: 他总是忘带钥匙, 周末他总在家看书. 总 is shorter and more spoken. 常常 (chángcháng) means often, less than always: 我常常跟朋友一起去游泳. Its negative is 不常.
又 (yòu) means again for something that has already happened, usually with 了: 他昨天又迟到了. It is also used for something that comes round regularly: 明天又是星期一了.

The contrast example uses 再 (Level 1): 我想再看一遍. 再 is again for something that has not happened yet; 又 is again for something that has. Common mistake: using 又 for a future wish (我想又看一遍) or 再 for a past event (他昨天再迟到了).

examples.reading: tā zǒngshì wàng dài yàoshi.
examples.translation: He always forgets to bring his keys.

examples.reading: tā zuótiān yòu chídào le.
examples.translation: He was late again yesterday.

examples.reading: zhōumò tā zǒng zài jiā kàn shū.
examples.translation: At weekends he is always at home reading.

examples.text: 我常常跟朋友一起去游泳。
examples.reading: wǒ chángcháng gēn péngyou yìqǐ qù yóuyǒng.
examples.translation: I often go swimming with friends.

examples.reading: míngtiān yòu shì xīngqīyī le.
examples.translation: Tomorrow is Monday again.

examples.text: 这个电影很好看，我想再看一遍。
examples.reading: zhège diànyǐng hěn hǎokàn, wǒ xiǎng zài kàn yí biàn.
examples.translation: This film is great; I want to see it again.

lessons.title: 一边……一边……: doing two things at once
lessons.summary: 一边 before each of two verbs says one person does both actions at the same time.
pattern: A + 一边 + V1 (+ O)，一边 + V2 (+ O)
A + 边 + V1 + 边 + V2
body: 一边 (yìbiān) is used in pairs: 一边 + verb, 一边 + verb. It says one subject does two actions at the same time: 他一边听音乐，一边写作业. Both verbs must be actions that last for a while, such as 听, 看, 走, 唱, 聊. With one-syllable verbs and no objects, speech often shortens it to 边走边聊.
The contrast example uses 着 (Level 2) between two verbs: 孩子们唱着歌回家了. With V1 + 着 + V2 the first action is only the manner of the main one; with 一边……一边…… the two actions have equal weight.
Common mistake: using 一边 with two different subjects (我一边做饭，他一边看电视) or with an action that is over in a moment (一边到, 一边开门). Use 一边……一边…… for one person and two lasting actions.

examples.text: 他一边听音乐，一边写作业。
examples.reading: tā yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān xiě zuòyè.
examples.translation: He listens to music while doing his homework.

examples.reading: wǒmen yìbiān zǒu yìbiān liáo ba.
examples.translation: Let's chat as we walk.

examples.text: 妈妈一边做饭，一边唱歌。
examples.reading: māma yìbiān zuò fàn, yìbiān chàng gē.
examples.translation: Mum sings while she cooks.

examples.text: 不要一边吃饭一边看手机。
examples.reading: búyào yìbiān chī fàn yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
examples.translation: Don't look at your phone while you eat.

examples.text: 他一边开车，一边打电话，太危险了。
examples.reading: tā yìbiān kāichē, yìbiān dǎ diànhuà, tài wēixiǎn le.
examples.translation: He was on the phone while driving; that's too dangerous.

examples.reading: háizimen chàng zhe gē huí jiā le.
examples.translation: The children went home singing.

lessons.title: Adverbs of likelihood and necessity: 大概, 必须, 差不多, 一定, 好像, 几乎
lessons.summary: 大概 means probably, 必须 must, 差不多 about the same or almost, 一定 certainly, 好像 seems, and 几乎 almost.
pattern: A + 大概 / 好像 / 一定 + V
A + 差不多；A + 几乎 + 没 / 每…
body: 大概 (dàgài) means probably: 他大概已经到家了. 好像 (hǎoxiàng) means it seems: 外面好像下雨了. 一定 (yídìng) means certainly; with a person's plan it is a promise (我一定来), and with a guess it means must be (他一定很累了). 必须 (bìxū) means must, have to: 开车的时候必须小心. Its negative is 不用 or 不必, never 不必须.
差不多 (chàbuduō) as a predicate means about the same: 颜色差不多; before a verb it means almost: 饭差不多做好了. 几乎 (jīhū) means almost, nearly, and often goes with 没 or 每: 他几乎没吃东西.

The contrast example uses 可能 (Level 2): 明天可能会下雨. 可能 says something may happen; 必须 says it has to, and 几乎 says it nearly did. Common mistake: using 差不多 or 几乎 as a guess about the future (我差不多明天来). Use 大概 or 可能.

examples.reading: tā dàgài yǐjīng dào jiā le.
examples.translation: He has probably got home already.

examples.reading: kāichē de shíhou bìxū xiǎoxīn.
examples.translation: You must be careful when driving.

examples.text: 这两件衣服的颜色差不多。
examples.reading: zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu de yánsè chàbuduō.
examples.translation: These two pieces of clothing are about the same colour.

examples.reading: nǐ fàngxīn, wǒ yídìng lái.
examples.translation: Don't worry, I'll definitely come.

examples.reading: wàimian hǎoxiàng xià yǔ le.
examples.translation: It seems to be raining outside.

examples.reading: tā jīhū méi chī dōngxi.
examples.translation: He ate almost nothing.

examples.reading: míngtiān kěnéng huì xià yǔ.
examples.translation: It may rain tomorrow.

lessons.title: Attitude adverbs: 当然, 其实, 终于, emphatic 才 and 就
lessons.summary: 当然 means of course, 其实 actually, 终于 at last; 才 can mean only (a small amount) or stress a strong denial, and 就 can stress that something is exactly so.
pattern: A + 当然 / 其实 / 终于 + V
才 + number；A + 才 + 不 + V + 呢；这才是…
body: 当然 (dāngrán) means of course: 你当然要帮他. 其实 (qíshí) means actually, in fact, and corrects what people think: 其实他是日本人. 终于 (zhōngyú) means at last, after a long wait: 车终于来了.

才 (cái) has two attitude uses. Before a number it means only, a small amount: 现在才七点. In 才不……呢 or 这才是 it stresses the speaker's view strongly: 我才不相信他的话呢, 这才是真正的朋友. 就 (jiù) can stress that something is exactly so or very near: 我家就在学校旁边.

The contrast example uses 就 as a link between clauses (Level 2): 你不去，我就一个人去. That 就 means then, in that case; the attitude 就 stresses a fact. Common mistake: using 终于 for something that came quickly. 终于 needs a wait or an effort before it.

examples.text: 他是你的朋友，你当然要帮他。
examples.reading: tā shì nǐ de péngyou, nǐ dāngrán yào bāng tā.
examples.translation: He's your friend; of course you should help him.

examples.text: 大家都以为他是中国人，其实他是日本人。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu yǐwéi tā shì Zhōngguó rén, qíshí tā shì Rìběn rén.
examples.translation: Everyone thought he was Chinese, but actually he is Japanese.

examples.text: 等了一个小时，车终于来了。
examples.reading: děng le yí ge xiǎoshí, chē zhōngyú lái le.
examples.translation: After an hour's wait the bus finally came.

examples.text: 现在才七点，你再睡一会儿吧。
examples.reading: xiànzài cái qī diǎn, nǐ zài shuì yíhuìr ba.
examples.translation: It's only seven; sleep a bit longer.

examples.reading: wǒ cái bù xiāngxìn tā de huà ne!
examples.translation: I don't believe a word he says!

examples.reading: zhè cái shì zhēnzhèng de péngyou.
examples.translation: Now that is a true friend.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā jiù zài xuéxiào pángbiān.
examples.translation: My home is right next to the school.

examples.reading: nǐ bú qù, wǒ jiù yí ge rén qù.
examples.translation: If you won't go, I'll go on my own.

lessons.title: 不用 and 不必: there is no need to
lessons.summary: 不用 and 不必 both say there is no need; 不用 is spoken, 不必 a little more formal, and both are the negative of 必须, 得 and 要.
pattern: A + 不用 / 不必 + V
body: 不用 (búyòng) and 不必 (búbì) say something is not necessary: 你不用担心, 大家不必等我. 不用 is the everyday spoken form; 不必 is slightly more formal. Either can stand alone with 了 to turn down an offer politely: 不用了，谢谢.
They are the negative of 必须 (must), 得 (děi, have to) and 要 (need to): 明天不用上班. The negative of 必须 is never 不必须.

The contrast example uses 别 (Level 2): 你别忘了带钥匙. 别 forbids or warns (don't); 不用 and 不必 only say there is no need, and nobody ever needs to forget, so 你不用忘了 makes no sense. Common mistake: saying 不必须 for no need.

examples.text: 你不用担心，我自己能去。
examples.reading: nǐ búyòng dānxīn, wǒ zìjǐ néng qù.
examples.translation: Don't worry; I can go by myself.

examples.translation: No need, thank you.

examples.translation: Tomorrow is Saturday, so there's no need to go to work.
