examples.translation: I was too busy, so I didn't call you.

lessons.title: V1 了 O (就) V2: once one thing is done, the next follows
lessons.summary: In a contracted sentence, 了 after the first verb says that action will be or was completed, and the second action follows, often with 就.
pattern: S + V1 + 了 + O + (就) + V2
下了课就去打球; 你到了北京给我打个电话
body: Two actions can be packed into one clause with no comma. 了 after the first verb marks it as completed before the second one starts: 我们下了课就去打球 (as soon as class is over), 你到了北京给我打个电话 (once you get to Beijing). This works for future plans as well as for past events: the 了 here means once it is done, not past time.
就 before the second verb stresses that the second action follows right away or naturally: 他吃了饭就走了, 你看了就知道了. It can be left out, as in 你到了北京给我打个电话.
The contrast example uses 一……就…… (我一到家就给你打电话), which stresses that the second action follows immediately. V1 了 O 就 V2 only says that the first one is completed first.
A common mistake is to drop 了 after the first verb when completion matters (我写完作业就睡觉 is fine because 完 shows completion, but 我写作业就睡觉 is not). Mark the first action as done.

examples.reading: wǒmen xià le kè jiù qù dǎ qiú.
examples.translation: We'll go and play ball as soon as class is over.

examples.reading: tā chī le fàn jiù zǒu le.
examples.translation: He left right after eating.

examples.text: 你到了北京给我打个电话。
examples.reading: nǐ dào le Běijīng gěi wǒ dǎ ge diànhuà.
examples.translation: Give me a call once you get to Beijing.

examples.reading: wǒ xiě wán le zuòyè jiù shuìjiào.
examples.translation: I'll go to bed once I've finished my homework.

examples.reading: nǐ kàn le jiù zhīdào le.
examples.translation: You'll see once you've had a look.

examples.text: 我一到家就给你打电话。
examples.reading: wǒ yí dào jiā jiù gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: I'll call you the moment I get home.

lessons.title: Approximate numbers 2: 大概 and two neighbouring numbers
lessons.summary: 大概 before a number means about, and two neighbouring numbers side by side (两三, 七八, 十五六) mean two or three, seven or eight, and so on.
pattern: neighbouring numbers + M + N: 三四本书, 十五六个人
body: 大概 (dàgài) before a number phrase or before the verb says the number is a rough estimate: 从这儿到机场大概要四十分钟, 我大概十点到家.

Two neighbouring numbers in a row also give an estimate, with no word between them: 三四本书 (three or four books), 七八天, 两三天 (use 两, not 二). With teens and tens, only the last digit changes: 十五六个人 (fifteen or sixteen people). The measure word follows the second number.
The contrast example uses 多 after a round number (二十多个学生), the approximate form from the earlier level, which means more than twenty. Neighbouring numbers give a range of two; 多 gives a floor.
A common mistake is to put 和 or 或 between the numbers (三和四本书) or a measure word after each one (三个四个). Say the two numbers together and add one measure word.

examples.text: 从这儿到机场大概要四十分钟。
examples.reading: cóng zhèr dào jīchǎng dàgài yào sìshí fēnzhōng.
examples.translation: It takes about forty minutes from here to the airport.

examples.reading: wǒ dàgài shí diǎn dào jiā.
examples.translation: I'll be home at about ten.

examples.text: 他一个人吃了三四碗米饭。
examples.reading: tā yí ge rén chī le sān sì wǎn mǐfàn.
examples.translation: He ate three or four bowls of rice by himself.

examples.text: 这次旅行大概要七八天。
examples.reading: zhè cì lǚxíng dàgài yào qī bā tiān.
examples.translation: This trip will take about seven or eight days.

examples.text: 昨天来了十五六个客人。
examples.reading: zuótiān lái le shíwǔ liù ge kèrén.
examples.translation: Fifteen or sixteen guests came yesterday.

examples.reading: tā guò liǎng sān tiān jiù huílai.
examples.translation: She'll be back in two or three days.

examples.text: 我们班有二十多个学生。
examples.reading: wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are over twenty students in our class.

lessons.title: 敢: to dare to do something
lessons.summary: 敢 is a modal verb meaning "dare to"; it goes before the verb and is negated with 不敢 (or 没敢 for a past moment).
pattern: A + 不敢 / 没敢 + V
A + 敢 + V + 吗？ / A + 敢不敢 + V？
body: 敢 (gǎn) is a modal verb: it stands before another verb and says that someone has the courage to do it. 他什么都敢试 means he dares to try anything. The usual negative is 不敢 (does not dare); for one moment in the past, 没敢 is also common: 我没敢问他. Questions are 你敢跳吗？ or 你敢不敢跳？. A sentence with nobody as the subject, 没人敢……, means nobody dares.
The contrast example uses 勇敢 (brave), an adjective. 勇敢 describes a person (一个很勇敢的孩子) and cannot take a verb after it; 敢 is the modal verb that takes the verb.
Common mistake: 我不勇敢一个人睡. Use the modal verb: 我不敢一个人睡.

examples.reading: mèimei bù gǎn mō nà zhī dà gǒu.
examples.translation: My younger sister does not dare to touch that big dog.

examples.reading: zhème gāo, nǐ gǎn tiào ma?
examples.translation: It is this high. Do you dare to jump?

examples.text: 他胆子很大，什么都敢试。
examples.reading: tā dǎnzi hěn dà, shénme dōu gǎn shì.
examples.translation: He is very bold; he dares to try anything.

examples.reading: kǎo de bù hǎo, wǒ bù gǎn huí jiā.
examples.translation: I did badly in the exam, so I do not dare to go home.

examples.reading: méi rén gǎn shuō tā cuò le.
examples.translation: Nobody dares to say he is wrong.

examples.text: 他是一个很勇敢的孩子。
examples.reading: tā shì yí ge hěn yǒnggǎn de háizi.
examples.translation: He is a very brave child.

lessons.title: 各 各位 各种 任何 此: each, all kinds, any, this
lessons.summary: 各 means each of a group, 各位 addresses a group politely, 各种 means all kinds of, 任何 means any at all, and 此 is a formal word for this.
pattern: 任何 + N + 都 / 也 …
body: 各 (gè) before a noun or measure word means each member of a group: 各国 (every country), 各个班. 各位 (gèwèi) is a polite way to address a group: 各位同学, 各位老师. 各种 (gè zhǒng) means all kinds of: 各种水果. 任何 (rènhé) means any at all; it usually comes with 都 or 也, or after a negative: 任何人都不能进去, 没有任何问题.
此 (cǐ) is the formal, written word for this. It is used mostly in set words: 从此 (from then on), 此时 (at this moment), 因此 (therefore).

The contrast example uses 每 (each, every), from HSK 2. 每 goes with a measure word and usually 都: 每个人都有一张票. 各 is more formal and often goes straight before the noun (各国); 任何 stresses that there is no exception.
Common mistake: 这家店卖任何水果. 任何 does not go in a plain affirmative object; say 这家店卖各种水果, or 任何水果都有.

examples.reading: gèwèi tóngxué, qǐng ānjìng.
examples.translation: Everyone, please be quiet.

examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn mài gè zhǒng shuǐguǒ.
examples.translation: This shop sells all kinds of fruit.

examples.reading: rènhé rén dōu bù néng jìnqu.
examples.translation: Nobody at all may go in.

examples.reading: tā méiyǒu rènhé wèntí.
examples.translation: He has no problems at all.

examples.reading: gè guó de rén dōu lái cānjiā le.
examples.translation: People from every country came to take part.

examples.reading: cóngcǐ tā zài yě méi chídào guo.
examples.translation: From then on he was never late again.

examples.reading: měi ge rén dōu yǒu yì zhāng piào.
examples.translation: Everyone has a ticket.

lessons.title: Special measure words: 打 袋 棵 台 幅
lessons.summary: Some nouns take their own measure word: 打 for a dozen, 袋 for a bag of, 棵 for trees and plants, 台 for machines, 幅 for pictures.
pattern: number + 打 / 袋 / 棵 / 台 / 幅 + N
body: These measure words belong to particular nouns. 打 (dá) is a dozen: 一打鸡蛋. 袋 (dài) is a bag of something: 两袋面包, 一袋米. 棵 (kē) counts trees and plants: 三棵树, 一棵草. 台 (tái) counts machines: 一台电脑, 两台空调. 幅 (fú) counts pictures, paintings and maps: 一幅画.
The contrast example uses 个, the general measure word from HSK 1. 个 goes with many nouns (一个主意, 一个人), but with a tree, a computer or a painting a speaker expects 棵, 台 or 幅.
Common mistake: 一个树 or 一个电脑. Say 一棵树, 一台电脑.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yì dá jīdàn.
examples.translation: I bought a dozen eggs.

examples.reading: māma mǎi le liǎng dài miànbāo.
examples.translation: Mum bought two bags of bread.

examples.reading: yuànzi li yǒu sān kē shù.
examples.translation: There are three trees in the yard.

examples.text: 办公室新买了一台电脑。
examples.reading: bàngōngshì xīn mǎi le yì tái diànnǎo.
examples.translation: The office has bought a new computer.

examples.reading: kètīng li guà zhe yì fú dìtú.
examples.translation: A map hangs in the living room.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu yí ge hǎo zhǔyi.
examples.translation: I have a good idea.

lessons.title: Borrowed measure words: 一脸 一手 一盒 一屋子 一桌子
lessons.summary: A noun such as 脸, 手, 盒, 屋子 or 桌子 can work as a measure word: 一盒 is a box of, and 一脸, 一手, 一屋子, 一桌子 mean a face, a hand, a room or a table full of.
pattern: 一 + 脸 / 手 / 屋子 / 桌子 + N (full of, all over)
body: A container or a body part can be borrowed as a measure word. 盒 (hé) is a box of: 一盒巧克力, 两盒牛奶. With 一, the words 脸 (liǎn), 手 (shǒu), 屋子 (wūzi) and 桌子 (zhuōzi) mean the whole face, hand, room or table is covered or filled: 一脸不高兴 (a face full of displeasure), 一手油 (oily hands), 一屋子客人 (a roomful of guests), 一桌子菜 (a table covered with dishes).
The contrast example uses 张, the measure word for the noun 桌子: 二十张桌子. There 桌子 is the thing being counted; in 一桌子菜 it is the measure word, and the thing is 菜.
Common mistake: 两桌子菜 to mean a table full of dishes. The full-of reading needs 一; with other numbers 桌 counts tables at a banquet (两桌菜).

examples.reading: tā yì liǎn bù gāoxìng de zǒu le.
examples.translation: He left with a sulky look all over his face.

examples.reading: tā zuò wán fàn, nòng le yì shǒu yóu.
examples.translation: After cooking he had oil all over his hands.

examples.reading: tā sòng wǒ yì hé qiǎokèlì.
examples.translation: She gave me a box of chocolates.

examples.reading: jiā li lái le yì wūzi kèrén.
examples.translation: A whole roomful of guests came to the house.

examples.text: 客人还没到，爷爷已经做好了一桌子菜。
examples.reading: kèrén hái méi dào, yéye yǐjīng zuò hǎo le yì zhuōzi cài.
examples.translation: Before the guests arrived, Grandpa had already cooked a whole tableful of dishes.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li yǒu èrshí zhāng zhuōzi.
examples.translation: There are twenty desks in the classroom.

lessons.title: Verbal measure words 场 顿 趟: a spell of, a meal or scolding, a trip
lessons.summary: 场 counts a spell of rain or illness and whole events, 顿 counts meals and scoldings, and 趟 counts trips there and back.
pattern: V + (了) + number + 场 / 顿 / 趟 (+ N)
body: These measure words count how many times an action happens, and each suits certain verbs. 场 (cháng) counts a spell of weather or illness: 下了一场大雨, 生了一场病. Read 场 as chǎng when it counts a whole show or match: 一场电影, 一场比赛. 顿 (dùn) counts meals and also beatings or scoldings: 吃一顿饭, 骂了他一顿. 趟 (tàng) counts trips to a place and back: 去一趟银行, 跑一趟.
The contrast example uses 次, the general verbal measure word from HSK 2: 再说一次. 次 just counts times; 场, 顿 and 趟 add what kind of event it was.
Common mistake: 我去了一次趟北京. Use one measure word: 我去了一趟北京.

examples.reading: zuótiān xià le yì cháng dà yǔ.
examples.translation: There was a heavy downpour yesterday.

examples.text: 我们一起看了一场足球比赛。
examples.reading: wǒmen yìqǐ kàn le yì chǎng zúqiú bǐsài.
examples.translation: We watched a football match together.

examples.reading: wǒ qǐng nǐ chī yí dùn fàn ba.
examples.translation: Let me treat you to a meal.

examples.reading: tā bèi bàba mà le yí dùn.
examples.translation: He got a scolding from his dad.

examples.reading: wǒ děi qù yí tàng yínháng.
examples.translation: I have to make a trip to the bank.

examples.reading: máfan nǐ pǎo yí tàng.
examples.translation: Sorry to trouble you to make the trip.

examples.reading: nǐ zài shuō yí cì.
examples.translation: Say it once more.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs 十分 更加 稍微 尤其 多么
lessons.summary: 十分 means very, 更加 means even more, 稍 and 稍微 mean a little, 尤其 means especially, and 多么 makes an exclamation.
pattern: 稍 / 稍微 + V / Adj + 一点儿 / 一下 / 有点儿
body: 十分 (shífēn) is a written-style very: 十分高兴. 更加 (gèngjiā) is a fuller form of 更, even more, often in comparisons over time: 空气更加新鲜了. 稍 (shāo) and 稍微 (shāowēi) mean slightly; they rarely stand alone and usually take 一点儿, 一下 or 有点儿: 稍等一下, 稍微有点儿大.
尤其 (yóuqí) picks out one item from a group: 我喜欢运动，尤其是游泳. 多么 (duōme) makes an exclamation and normally ends with 啊: 多么美啊！. It does not go in a plain statement.
The contrast example uses 有点儿 (a bit, usually for something unwelcome), from HSK 2: 今天有点儿冷. It goes before the adjective; 一点儿 goes after it (冷一点儿), so 今天一点儿冷 is wrong.
Common mistake: 多么 in a plain statement, as in 这里多么美. Make it an exclamation with 啊 (这里多么美啊！), or use 十分 for a statement.

examples.text: 这个消息让大家十分高兴。
examples.reading: zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā shífēn gāoxìng.
examples.translation: The news made everyone very happy.

examples.reading: yǔ hòu kōngqì gèngjiā xīnxiān le.
examples.translation: After the rain the air is even fresher.

examples.reading: qǐng nǐ shāo děng yíxià.
examples.translation: Please wait a moment.

examples.text: 这件衣服稍微有点儿大。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu shāowēi yǒudiǎnr dà.
examples.translation: This garment is a little on the big side.

examples.text: 我喜欢运动，尤其是游泳。
examples.reading: wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, yóuqí shì yóuyǒng.
examples.translation: I like sports, especially swimming.

examples.reading: zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng duōme měi a!
examples.translation: How beautiful the scenery here is!

examples.reading: jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lěng.
examples.translation: It is a bit cold today.

lessons.title: Scope adverbs 共 全 光 仅 仅仅 至少: in all, entirely, only, at least
lessons.summary: 共 means in all, 全 means entirely or all, 光 and 仅 / 仅仅 mean only, and 至少 means at least.
pattern: 光 / 仅 / 仅仅 / 至少 + V / number
body: 共 (gòng) is the short written form of 一共, in all: 这本书共有十二课. 全 (quán) says all of the group or the whole thing: 他们全都来了. 光 (guāng) is a spoken only, often in advice: 不能光吃肉. 仅 (jǐn) and 仅仅 (jǐnjǐn) are formal only and stress how little: 仅用了三天, 他仅仅是个孩子. 至少 (zhìshǎo) means at least: 至少要喝八杯水.
The contrast example uses 只 (only), the everyday word from HSK 2: 我只带了十块钱. 光, 仅 and 仅仅 are its spoken and formal relatives; 至少 is the opposite direction, a lower limit.
Common mistake: 全 for in total. 全班 means the whole class; for a sum, use 共 or 一共: 一共三十人.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū gòng yǒu shí'èr kè.
examples.translation: This book has twelve lessons in all.

examples.reading: tāmen quán dōu lái le.
examples.translation: They all came.

examples.text: 你不能光吃肉，也要吃菜。
examples.reading: nǐ bù néng guāng chī ròu, yě yào chī cài.
examples.translation: You cannot eat only meat; you should eat vegetables too.

examples.text: 这座桥仅用了一年就建好了。
examples.reading: zhè zuò qiáo jǐn yòng le yì nián jiù jiàn hǎo le.
examples.translation: This bridge took only a year to build.

examples.reading: tā jǐnjǐn shì ge háizi.
examples.translation: He is only a child.

examples.reading: měi tiān zhìshǎo yào hē bā bēi shuǐ.
examples.translation: You should drink at least eight glasses of water a day.

examples.reading: wǒ zhǐ dài le shí kuài qián.
examples.translation: I only brought ten yuan.

lessons.title: Time adverbs 按时 从来 从 本来 已: on time, ever, originally, already
lessons.summary: 按时 means on time, 从来 and 从 with a negative mean never, 本来 means originally, and 已 is the written form of 已经.
pattern: 从来 / 从 + 不 / 没 + V
本来 + V …, (后来 / 可是 …)
body: 按时 (ànshí) means at the set time: 按时吃药, 按时交作业. 从来 (cónglái) means ever, and nearly always comes with a negative: 从来不 for a habit, 从来没 (……过) for experience: 我从来没去过国外. The single word 从 does the same in writing: 他从不喝酒.
本来 (běnlái) means originally, at first, and the next clause usually says what changed: 我本来想去，后来有事没去成. 已 (yǐ) is the short, formal form of 已经: 飞机已到达北京.
The contrast example uses 一直 (all along, continuously), from HSK 2: 他一直住在北京. 一直 works in an affirmative sentence; 从来 usually needs a negative, so 他从来住在北京 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我从来去过上海. Add the negative, 我从来没去过上海, or use 一直 or 常常 for a positive habit.

examples.reading: tā měi tiān ànshí chī yào.
examples.translation: He takes his medicine on time every day.

examples.reading: qǐng ànshí jiāo zuòyè.
examples.translation: Please hand in your homework on time.

examples.reading: wǒ cónglái méi qù guo guówài.
examples.translation: I have never been abroad.

examples.reading: tā cóng bù hē jiǔ.
examples.translation: He never drinks alcohol.

examples.text: 我本来想去，后来有事没去成。
examples.reading: wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù, hòulái yǒu shì méi qù chéng.
examples.translation: I meant to go, but then something came up and I could not.

examples.reading: fēijī yǐ dàodá Běijīng.
examples.translation: The plane has already arrived in Beijing.

examples.reading: tā yìzhí zhù zài Běijīng.
examples.translation: He has always lived in Beijing.

lessons.title: Time adverbs 赶紧 赶快 忽然 将 将要: hurry, suddenly, will
lessons.summary: 赶紧 and 赶快 urge someone to hurry, 忽然 says something happened suddenly, and 将 / 将要 mark the future in a formal way.
pattern: 将 / 将要 + V (+ 了)
body: 赶紧 (gǎnjǐn) and 赶快 (gǎnkuài) mean hurry up and do it, often in suggestions or commands: 我们赶紧回家吧, 你赶快去医院看看. 忽然 (hūrán) says an event happened without warning: 忽然停电了, 他忽然想起一件事. 将 (jiāng) and 将要 (jiāngyào) are formal markers of the future: 新学期将在九月开始, 火车将要进站了.

There are two contrast examples. 突然 (sudden) can be an adjective as well as an adverb: 这个消息太突然了. 忽然 is only an adverb, so 太忽然了 is wrong. 马上 (right away), from HSK 2, is the everyday word for an action about to happen: 我马上就来; 将要 belongs to announcements and writing.
Common mistake: 赶快 for something that happens by itself, as in 赶快下雨了. 赶快 needs a person who hurries; for weather use 快要下雨了.

examples.text: 快下雨了，我们赶紧回家吧。
examples.reading: kuài xià yǔ le, wǒmen gǎnjǐn huí jiā ba.
examples.translation: It is about to rain; let us hurry home.

examples.reading: nǐ gǎnkuài qù yīyuàn kànkan.
examples.translation: Go and see a doctor at the hospital quickly.

examples.text: 我们正在吃饭，忽然停电了。
examples.reading: wǒmen zhèngzài chīfàn, hūrán tíng diàn le.
examples.translation: We were eating when the power suddenly went out.

examples.reading: tā hūrán xiǎngqǐ yí jiàn shì.
examples.translation: He suddenly remembered something.

examples.reading: xīn xuéqī jiāng zài jiǔyuè kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The new term will begin in September.

examples.reading: huǒchē jiāngyào jìn zhàn le.
examples.translation: The train is about to pull into the station.

examples.reading: zhège xiāoxi tài tūrán le.
examples.translation: This news is too sudden.

examples.reading: děngdeng wǒ, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
examples.translation: Wait for me, I am coming right away.

lessons.title: Frequency adverbs 重新 往往 偶尔 再次 老: again, usually, occasionally, always
lessons.summary: 重新 means do over again, 往往 says what usually happens in a situation, 偶尔 means occasionally, 再次 means once more, and 老 complains that something keeps happening.
pattern: A + 往往 / 偶尔 / 老 + V
body: 重新 (chóngxīn) means start again and do it differently or from the beginning: 请重新写一遍. 往往 (wǎngwǎng) states what tends to happen under certain conditions, from experience: 年轻人往往睡得很晚; it is not used for a single future plan. 偶尔 (ǒu'ěr) means now and then: 我偶尔也会喝一点儿咖啡. 再次 (zàicì) is a formal once again: 他再次获得了第一名.
老 (lǎo) before a verb means always, in a complaining tone: 你怎么老忘关灯？, 这几天老是下雨. This 老 is an adverb, not the prefix in 老王.
The contrast example uses 又 (again), from HSK 2: 他昨天来了，今天又来了. 又 is for a repeat that has already happened; 再 is for one that has not, so 今天再来了 is wrong. 再次 is the formal word and works for both.
Common mistake: 我往往明天去 for a plan. 往往 is for a pattern you have seen; for a plan use 常常 or a time word.

examples.reading: xiě cuò le, qǐng chóngxīn xiě yí biàn.
examples.translation: That is written wrongly; please write it out again.

examples.reading: niánqīngrén wǎngwǎng shuì de hěn wǎn.
examples.translation: Young people tend to go to bed late.

examples.text: 我偶尔也会喝一点儿咖啡。
examples.reading: wǒ ǒu'ěr yě huì hē yìdiǎnr kāfēi.
examples.translation: I drink a little coffee now and then too.

examples.reading: tā zàicì huòdé le dì-yī míng.
examples.translation: He won first place once again.

examples.reading: nǐ zěnme lǎo wàng guān dēng?
examples.translation: Why do you keep forgetting to turn off the light?

examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān lǎoshì xià yǔ.
examples.translation: It has been raining all the time these last few days.

examples.text: 他昨天来了，今天又来了。
examples.reading: tā zuótiān lái le, jīntiān yòu lái le.
examples.translation: He came yesterday, and today he came again.

lessons.title: 故意 互相 相互: on purpose, each other
lessons.summary: 故意 means on purpose; 互相 and 相互 mean each other, with 相互 the more formal one.
pattern: A 和 B / plural subject + 互相 / 相互 + V
body: 故意 (gùyì) says someone did something on purpose, often something unkind: 他故意不接我的电话. 我不是故意的 is the usual way to say it was an accident.

互相 (hùxiāng) and 相互 (xiānghù) say that each person does the action to the other, so the subject is plural: 兄弟俩从小就互相照顾. 相互 is more formal and can also stand before 的 and a noun: 相互的理解. In everyday speech 互相 is far more common.
The contrast example uses 一起 (together), from HSK 1: 我们一起去打篮球吧. 一起 says people do the same thing side by side; 互相 says they do it to one another, so 我们互相去打篮球 is wrong.
Common mistake: 他互相帮助我. 互相 needs a plural subject and no object for the other person: 我们互相帮助.

examples.reading: duìbuqǐ, wǒ bú shì gùyì de.
examples.translation: Sorry, I did not do it on purpose.

examples.reading: tā gùyì bù jiē wǒ de diànhuà.
examples.translation: He is deliberately not answering my calls.

examples.text: 兄弟俩从小就互相照顾。
examples.reading: xiōngdì liǎ cóngxiǎo jiù hùxiāng zhàogù.
examples.translation: The two brothers have looked after each other since they were small.

examples.text: 我们要相互学习，共同进步。
examples.reading: wǒmen yào xiānghù xuéxí, gòngtóng jìnbù.
examples.translation: We should learn from each other and make progress together.

examples.text: 这两个问题是相互影响的。
examples.reading: zhè liǎng ge wèntí shì xiānghù yǐngxiǎng de.
examples.translation: These two problems affect each other.

examples.reading: tāmen liǎ hùxiāng kàn le yì yǎn.
examples.translation: The two of them glanced at each other.

examples.reading: wǒmen yìqǐ qù dǎ lánqiú ba.
examples.translation: Let us go and play basketball together.

lessons.title: 却: but, yet (after the subject)
lessons.summary: 却 is an adverb meaning but or yet; it goes after the subject of the second clause, where 但是 goes before it.
body: 却 (què) marks a result that goes against what the first clause leads you to expect: 天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫. Because it is an adverb, it stands after the subject and before the verb or adjective, never at the very front of the clause.
The contrast example uses the conjunction 但是 (but), from HSK 2: 他很聪明，但是他不努力. 但是 comes before the subject; 却 comes after it. The two can even appear together: 但是他却不努力.
Common mistake: 却他不愿意. Move 却 after the subject: 他却不愿意.

examples.text: 他学了三年汉语，水平却不太高。
examples.reading: tā xué le sān nián Hànyǔ, shuǐpíng què bú tài gāo.
examples.translation: He has studied Chinese for three years, yet his level is still not very high.

examples.text: 天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫。
examples.reading: tiānqì hěn lěng, tā què zhǐ chuān le yí jiàn chènshān.
examples.translation: It is cold, yet he is wearing only a shirt.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng bāng tā, tā què bú yuànyì.
examples.translation: I wanted to help him, but he was not willing.

examples.reading: dōngxi bú guì, zhìliàng què hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: The goods are cheap, yet the quality is good.

examples.text: 大家都到了，他却还没来。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu dào le, tā què hái méi lái.
examples.translation: Everyone has arrived, but he still has not come.

examples.text: 他很聪明，但是他不努力。
examples.reading: tā hěn cōngming, dànshì tā bù nǔlì.
examples.translation: He is clever, but he does not work hard.

lessons.title: 也许 and 恐怕: perhaps, I am afraid that
lessons.summary: 也许 means perhaps; 恐怕 also means probably but adds worry that the outcome is unwelcome.
pattern: A + 也许 / 恐怕 + V
body: 也许 (yěxǔ) makes a guess: 也许是我记错了. 恐怕 (kǒngpà) makes a guess about something you do not want: 恐怕要下雨了, 这件事恐怕不太好办. Both are adverbs that can stand at the front of the sentence or right after the subject, so 老师也许还在办公室 and 也许老师还在办公室 are both correct.
The contrast example uses the verb 害怕 (to be afraid of): 妹妹很害怕大狗. 害怕 takes an object and can follow 很; 恐怕 is only a guessing adverb, so 很恐怕大狗 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我恐怕狗. To fear something, use 怕 or 害怕: 我怕狗.

examples.text: 恐怕要下雨了，带上伞吧。
examples.reading: kǒngpà yào xià yǔ le, dài shang sǎn ba.
examples.translation: I am afraid it is going to rain; take an umbrella.

examples.reading: yěxǔ shì wǒ jì cuò le.
examples.translation: Perhaps I remembered it wrong.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì kǒngpà bú tài hǎo bàn.
examples.translation: I am afraid this will not be easy to sort out.

examples.reading: xiànzài qù kǒngpà yǐjīng wǎn le.
examples.translation: I am afraid it is already too late to go now.

examples.reading: lǎoshī yěxǔ hái zài bàngōngshì.
examples.translation: The teacher may still be in the office.

examples.reading: mèimei hěn hàipà dà gǒu.
examples.translation: My younger sister is very scared of big dogs.

lessons.title: Mood uses of 才 就 并 还: insisting, denying, reproaching
lessons.summary: Besides their time meanings, 才 and 就 add emphasis, 并 before a negative denies what someone assumed, and 还 in 还……呢 reproaches.
pattern: 并 + 不 / 没 + V; 还 + N / V + 呢
body: 才 (cái) can insist or contradict: 我才不跟他去呢！ (I certainly will not), 这才是我想要的生活 (this, and nothing less, is the life I want). 就 (jiù) can stress that it is exactly this and nothing else: 我就要这件, 银行就在超市对面.
并 (bìng) before 不 or 没 denies an assumption: 这道题并不难 (it is not hard at all, whatever you think). 还 (hái) in 还……呢 reproaches someone for falling short of what they should be: 你还是哥哥呢，怎么不帮帮妹妹？
The contrast example uses 才 in its time meaning, from HSK 3: 会议九点才开始 (not until nine). There 才 says later than expected; in 我才不去呢 it is pure emphasis.
Common mistake: 这道题并难. 并 in this sense needs a negative after it: 并不难, 并没有.

examples.reading: wǒ cái bù gēn tā qù ne!
examples.translation: I am certainly not going with him!

examples.reading: zhè cái shì wǒ xiǎng yào de shēnghuó.
examples.translation: This is the life I really want.

examples.text: 我就要这件，别的都不要。
examples.reading: wǒ jiù yào zhè jiàn, bié de dōu bú yào.
examples.translation: I want this one and no other.

examples.reading: yínháng jiù zài chāoshì duìmiàn.
examples.translation: The bank is right across from the supermarket.

examples.text: 这道题并不难，你再想想。
examples.reading: zhè dào tí bìng bù nán, nǐ zài xiǎngxiang.
examples.translation: This question is not hard at all; think again.

examples.text: 你还是哥哥呢，怎么不帮帮妹妹？
examples.reading: nǐ hái shì gēge ne, zěnme bù bāngbang mèimei?
examples.translation: And you call yourself her big brother? Why will you not help your little sister?

examples.reading: huìyì jiǔ diǎn cái kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The meeting does not start until nine.

lessons.title: 竟然 究竟 到底 难道: surprise, pressing questions, rhetorical questions
lessons.summary: 竟然 says something is surprising, 究竟 and 到底 press for the real answer in a question, and 难道 starts a rhetorical question ending in 吗.
pattern: 究竟 / 到底 + question word …？
body: 竟然 (jìngrán) says the fact goes beyond what you expected: 他竟然一个人做完了. 究竟 (jiūjìng) and 到底 (dàodǐ) go into a question with a question word or an A-not-A form and demand the real answer: 你究竟想去哪儿？, 这到底是怎么回事？. They are not used with 吗. 到底 can also mean in the end, after all: 他到底还是来了.
难道 (nándào) opens a rhetorical question and the sentence normally ends in 吗: 难道你忘了明天要考试吗？ means surely you have not forgotten. 难道 is not used with a question word such as 哪儿.
The contrast example uses 原来 (so that is how it is), from HSK 3: 原来他是你哥哥！. 原来 marks finding out the truth; 竟然 marks being surprised by it.
Common mistake: 你到底去不去吗？. 到底 already makes the question; drop 吗: 你到底去不去？

examples.reading: tā jìngrán yí ge rén zuò wán le.
examples.translation: He actually finished it all by himself.

examples.text: 他平时很少锻炼，竟然跑了第一名。
examples.reading: tā píngshí hěn shǎo duànliàn, jìngrán pǎo le dì-yī míng.
examples.translation: He hardly ever exercises, yet he actually came first in the race.

examples.reading: nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng qù nǎr?
examples.translation: Where exactly do you want to go?

examples.reading: zhè dàodǐ shì zěnme huí shì?
examples.translation: What on earth is going on?

examples.text: 难道你忘了明天要考试吗？
examples.reading: nándào nǐ wàng le míngtiān yào kǎoshì ma?
examples.translation: Surely you have not forgotten there is an exam tomorrow?

examples.reading: nándào bú shì ma?
examples.translation: Is it not so?

examples.reading: tā dàodǐ háishi lái le.
examples.translation: He came after all.

examples.reading: yuánlái tā shì nǐ gēge!
examples.translation: So he is your brother!

lessons.title: 正好 千万 确实 只好 差点儿: just right, be sure to, indeed, had to, almost
lessons.summary: 正好 means just right or by luck, 千万 urges or warns, 确实 confirms, 只好 means there was no choice, and 差点儿 means almost.
pattern: 正好 + V / clause; V + 得 + 正好
千万 + 要 / 别 + V
确实 / 只好 / 差（一）点儿 + V
body: 正好 (zhènghǎo) says the timing or amount is just right, often by luck: 你来得正好, 我正好有空. 千万 (qiānwàn) strongly urges or warns and comes before 要, 别 or 不要: 你千万别告诉他. 确实 (quèshí) confirms that something really is so: 他说的确实是真的.
只好 (zhǐhǎo) says there was no better choice: 没有车了，我们只好走回家. 差点儿 (chàdiǎnr), also 差一点儿, says something almost happened but did not: 我差点儿迟到了, 我差一点儿忘了你的生日.
The contrast example uses 一定 (surely, must), from HSK 2: 他一定是生病了. 一定 can make a confident guess in a statement; 千万 only urges or warns, so 他千万是生病了 is wrong.
Common mistake: 千万去 with nothing between. Keep 要 or 别: 你千万要去.

examples.text: 你来得正好，帮我搬一下桌子。
examples.reading: nǐ lái de zhènghǎo, bāng wǒ bān yíxià zhuōzi.
examples.translation: You have come at just the right moment; help me move this table.

examples.reading: wǒ zhènghǎo yǒu kòng, péi nǐ qù ba.
examples.translation: I happen to be free; I will go with you.

examples.reading: nǐ qiānwàn bié gàosu tā.
examples.translation: Whatever you do, do not tell him.

examples.reading: tā shuō de quèshí shì zhēn de.
examples.translation: What he said really is true.

examples.text: 没有车了，我们只好走回家。
examples.reading: méiyǒu chē le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒu huí jiā.
examples.translation: There were no more buses, so we had to walk home.

examples.reading: wǒ chàdiǎnr chídào le.
examples.translation: I was almost late.

examples.text: 我差一点儿忘了你的生日。
examples.reading: wǒ chà yìdiǎnr wàng le nǐ de shēngrì.
examples.translation: I almost forgot your birthday.

examples.reading: tā yídìng shì shēngbìng le.
examples.translation: He must be ill.

lessons.title: 自 当 由 随着 等: from, when, along with, until
lessons.summary: 自 and 由 mark a starting point, 当……的时候 marks the moment something happens, 随着 means as something changes, and 等 means once or by the time something happens.
pattern: V + 自 + place; 自 + time + 起
当 + clause + 的时候 / 时
由 + place + V; 随着 + change; 等 + clause, (再 …)
body: 自 (zì) is a formal from. It often follows a verb, as in 来自上海, or opens a time phrase with 起: 自今天起. 由 (yóu) also marks a starting place: 我们由这里出发. 当 (dāng) frames the moment of an event with 的时候 or 时: 当我到家的时候，雨已经停了.

随着 (suízhe) means along with or as: the second clause changes because the first does: 随着天气变冷，感冒的人多了起来. 等 (děng) here is a preposition meaning once or by the time; the next clause usually has 再 or 就: 等你回来，我们再吃饭.
The contrast example uses 从 (from), from HSK 2: 他从小就喜欢画画. 从 is the everyday word for from; 自 and 由 are formal.
Common mistake: 当我到家，雨停了. 当 needs 的时候 or 时 to close the clause: 当我到家的时候.

examples.reading: tā láizì Shànghǎi.
examples.translation: He comes from Shanghai.

examples.text: 图书馆自今天起免费开放。
examples.reading: túshūguǎn zì jīntiān qǐ miǎnfèi kāifàng.
examples.translation: From today the library is open free of charge.

examples.text: 当我到家的时候，雨已经停了。
examples.reading: dāng wǒ dào jiā de shíhou, yǔ yǐjīng tíng le.
examples.translation: By the time I got home, the rain had stopped.

examples.reading: wǒmen yóu zhèlǐ chūfā.
examples.translation: We set off from here.

examples.text: 随着天气变冷，感冒的人多了起来。
examples.reading: suízhe tiānqì biàn lěng, gǎnmào de rén duō le qǐlai.
examples.translation: As the weather gets colder, more people are catching colds.

examples.reading: děng nǐ huílai, wǒmen zài chīfàn.
examples.translation: We will eat once you are back.

examples.reading: tā cóng xiǎo jiù xǐhuan huà huà.
examples.translation: He has loved drawing since he was little.

lessons.title: 将 由 叫 让: the formal 把, the person in charge, the passive doer
lessons.summary: 将 is a formal 把 that brings the object forward, 由 names the person responsible for an action, and 叫 and 让 introduce the doer in a spoken passive.
pattern: thing + 叫 / 让 + doer + V + other
body: 将 (jiāng) works like 把 in written or formal Chinese: 请将手机关掉, 他将这件事告诉了大家. As with 把, the verb needs something after it (掉, 了大家). 由 (yóu) names who is in charge of doing something: 这件事由我负责, 晚会由小李主持.
叫 (jiào) and 让 (ràng) make a spoken passive: the thing that is affected comes first and the doer follows 叫 or 让: 我的雨伞叫谁拿走了, 牛奶让猫喝光了. The doer must be named; use 人 when it is unknown.
The contrast example uses 被, the main passive marker from HSK 3: 他的钱包被偷了. 被 can drop the doer, as here; 叫 and 让 cannot.
Common mistake: 我的钱包让偷了. With 让 or 叫, name a doer: 我的钱包让人偷了.

examples.reading: qǐng jiāng shǒujī guān diào.
examples.translation: Please switch off your phones.

examples.text: 他将这件事告诉了大家。
examples.reading: tā jiāng zhè jiàn shì gàosu le dàjiā.
examples.translation: He told everyone about this.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ fùzé.
examples.translation: I am in charge of this matter.

examples.reading: wǎnhuì yóu Xiǎo Lǐ zhǔchí.
examples.translation: The evening party is hosted by Xiao Li.

examples.reading: wǒ de yǔsǎn jiào shéi ná zǒu le?
examples.translation: Who has taken my umbrella?

examples.reading: niúnǎi ràng māo hē guāng le.
examples.translation: The milk was all drunk up by the cat.

examples.reading: tā de qiánbāo bèi tōu le.
examples.translation: His wallet was stolen.

lessons.title: 由于 + noun phrase: because of, owing to
lessons.summary: 由于 as a preposition puts a noun phrase in front of the sentence to give the cause: 由于大雾 (because of the fog).
body: 由于 (yóuyú) means because of. Followed by a noun phrase, it is a preposition and names the cause: 由于大雾，飞机没能起飞, 由于他的帮助，我很快找到了工作. It is more formal than 因为. The phrase usually opens the sentence, but it can also follow the subject: 他由于工作的原因常去外地.
The same word also links whole clauses (由于天气不好，……); that use is taught with the conjunctions.
The contrast example uses 为了 (in order to), from HSK 3: 为了不迟到，我早早就出门了. 为了 gives a purpose that lies ahead; 由于 gives a cause that already exists.
Common mistake: 由大雾，飞机没起飞. 由 alone means from or by; the cause needs 由于.

examples.text: 由于大雾，飞机没能起飞。
examples.reading: yóuyú dà wù, fēijī méi néng qǐfēi.
examples.translation: Because of the thick fog, the plane could not take off.

examples.text: 由于时间关系，我们就讲到这里。
examples.reading: yóuyú shíjiān guānxi, wǒmen jiù jiǎng dào zhèlǐ.
examples.translation: Because of the time, we will stop here.

examples.text: 由于他的帮助，我很快找到了工作。
examples.reading: yóuyú tā de bāngzhù, wǒ hěn kuài zhǎodào le gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Thanks to his help, I quickly found a job.

examples.text: 他由于工作的原因常去外地。
examples.reading: tā yóuyú gōngzuò de yuányīn cháng qù wàidì.
examples.translation: Because of his work he often travels to other cities.

examples.text: 运动会由于大雨改到了下周。
examples.reading: yùndònghuì yóuyú dà yǔ gǎi dào le xià zhōu.
examples.translation: The sports meeting was moved to next week because of the heavy rain.

examples.text: 为了不迟到，我早早就出门了。
examples.reading: wèile bù chídào, wǒ zǎozǎo jiù chūmén le.
examples.translation: So as not to be late, I left home early.

lessons.title: 对于 and 与: regarding, with
lessons.summary: 对于 introduces the thing an attitude or opinion is about, and 与 is a formal 跟 or 和 that introduces the other party.
pattern: A + 对于 + N + Adj / V
A + 与 + B + V (见面 / 有关 / 不同)
body: 对于 (duìyú) introduces what an opinion, attitude or effect is about: 对于这个问题，大家的看法不同, 这本书对于初学者很有用. It can open the sentence or follow the subject: 他对于工作非常认真. In most of these sentences 对 also works.

与 (yǔ) is a written-style 跟: it introduces the other person or thing in 见面, 有关系, 不同 and similar expressions: 我要与王经理见面, 这件事与你没有关系, 今天的天气与昨天不同. The same 与 can also join two nouns as and; that use is taught with the conjunctions.
The contrast example uses 关于 (about, on the topic of), from HSK 3: 一篇关于环境保护的文章. 关于 names a topic and often forms 关于……的 before a noun; it cannot stand after the subject, so 这本书关于初学者很有用 is wrong.
Common mistake: 对于你没有关系. Relationships take 与 or 跟: 与你没有关系.

examples.text: 对于这个问题，大家的看法不同。
examples.reading: duìyú zhège wèntí, dàjiā de kànfǎ bù tóng.
examples.translation: People have different views on this question.

examples.text: 这本书对于初学者很有用。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū duìyú chūxuézhě hěn yǒuyòng.
examples.translation: This book is very useful for beginners.

examples.reading: tā duìyú gōngzuò fēicháng rènzhēn.
examples.translation: He is very conscientious about his work.

examples.reading: wǒ yào yǔ Wáng jīnglǐ jiànmiàn.
examples.translation: I am going to meet Manager Wang.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì yǔ nǐ méiyǒu guānxi.
examples.translation: This has nothing to do with you.

examples.text: 今天的天气与昨天不同。
examples.reading: jīntiān de tiānqì yǔ zuótiān bù tóng.
examples.translation: The weather today is different from yesterday.

examples.text: 他写了一篇关于环境保护的文章。
examples.reading: tā xiě le yì piān guānyú huánjìng bǎohù de wénzhāng.
examples.translation: He wrote an article about environmental protection.

lessons.title: 作为 按 按照: as, according to
lessons.summary: 作为 means in the role of, and 按 / 按照 mean according to a rule, plan or order.
pattern: 按 / 按照 + rule / plan + V
body: 作为 (zuòwéi) names the role or identity from which someone speaks or acts: 作为学生，你应该好好学习, 作为朋友，我想提醒你一句. 按照 (ànzhào) means according to and goes before a rule, a plan or an instruction: 按照计划, 按照规定. 按 (àn) means the same and is common before short words and in spoken requests: 按顺序, 按我说的做.
The contrast example uses 按时 (on time), the time adverb: 飞机按时起飞了. 按时 is one word that goes straight before the verb; 按照 needs a noun after it, so 飞机按照起飞了 is wrong.
Common mistake: 按照他，这样不对. To give someone's opinion, say 在他看来 or 他认为; 按照 goes with rules and plans.

examples.text: 作为学生，你应该好好学习。
examples.reading: zuòwéi xuésheng, nǐ yīnggāi hǎohǎo xuéxí.
examples.translation: As a student, you should study hard.

examples.text: 作为朋友，我想提醒你一句。
examples.reading: zuòwéi péngyou, wǒ xiǎng tíxǐng nǐ yí jù.
examples.translation: As a friend, I want to give you a word of warning.

examples.reading: qǐng àn shùnxù páiduì.
examples.translation: Please queue in order.

examples.text: 我们按照计划完成了任务。
examples.reading: wǒmen ànzhào jìhuà wánchéng le rènwu.
examples.translation: We completed the task according to plan.

examples.text: 按照规定，这里不能抽烟。
examples.reading: ànzhào guīdìng, zhèlǐ bù néng chōuyān.
examples.translation: Under the rules, smoking is not allowed here.

examples.reading: nǐ jiù àn wǒ shuō de zuò ba.
examples.translation: Just do as I say.

examples.reading: fēijī ànshí qǐfēi le.
examples.translation: The plane took off on time.

lessons.title: 并 而 与: joining verbs, adjectives and nouns
lessons.summary: 并 joins two verb phrases done by the same subject, 而 joins two adjectives, and 与 is a formal and between nouns.
body: Chinese uses different words for and depending on what is joined. 并 (bìng) joins two actions of one subject, the second following the first: 会议讨论并通过了这个计划. 而 (ér) joins two adjectives, in written style: 简单而有效, 聪明而可爱. 与 (yǔ) joins two nouns like 和, but is more formal: 老师与学生.
The contrast example uses 而且 (and also, moreover), from HSK 3: 这家店的菜便宜，而且很好吃. 而且 links two clauses and adds a further point; 与 cannot do that, so 便宜，与很好吃 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我喜欢唱歌与跳舞 is acceptable in writing, but 他聪明与可爱 is not: 与 joins nouns, not predicates. Use 他聪明而可爱 or 他又聪明又可爱.

examples.text: 会议讨论并通过了这个计划。
examples.reading: huìyì tǎolùn bìng tōngguò le zhège jìhuà.
examples.translation: The meeting discussed and approved the plan.

examples.text: 他听完并记下了老师的话。
examples.reading: tā tīng wán bìng jì xià le lǎoshī de huà.
examples.translation: He listened to the end and wrote down what the teacher said.

examples.reading: zhège fāngfǎ jiǎndān ér yǒuxiào.
examples.translation: This method is simple and effective.

examples.text: 她是一个聪明而可爱的女孩。
examples.reading: tā shì yí ge cōngming ér kě'ài de nǚhái.
examples.translation: She is a clever and lovely girl.

examples.text: 老师与学生都参加了比赛。
examples.reading: lǎoshī yǔ xuésheng dōu cānjiā le bǐsài.
examples.translation: Teachers and students both took part in the competition.

examples.text: 这家店的菜便宜，而且很好吃。
examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn de cài piányi, érqiě hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant is cheap, and it tastes good too.

lessons.title: Clause links 此外 而 既然 甚至 不过 并且
lessons.summary: 此外 adds another point, 而 sets two facts against each other, 既然 starts from a known fact, 甚至 goes to an extreme, 不过 adds a mild but, and 并且 adds a further action.
body: 此外 (cǐwài) means besides, in addition, and is followed by a comma or a new clause: ……很近，此外，价格也不贵. 并且 (bìngqiě) means and also; it adds a second action or fact, often with the same subject: 他同意了，并且帮我说服了大家. 而 (ér) between clauses sets two subjects side by side in contrast: 哥哥喜欢安静，而弟弟喜欢热闹.

既然 (jìrán) starts from a fact both people accept and draws a conclusion or suggestion, usually with 就: 既然来了，就多住几天吧. 甚至 (shènzhì) means even, the extreme case: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭. 不过 (búguò) is a softer but: 这个办法不错，不过有点儿麻烦.
The contrast example uses 因为 (because), from HSK 2: 因为堵车，他迟到了半个小时. 因为 simply gives a cause; 既然 needs a conclusion or suggestion after it, so it does not fit a plain report of what happened.
Common mistake: 既然下雨了，我昨天没去. 既然 leads to a decision, not a past report; say 因为下雨了，我昨天没去, or 既然下雨了，我们就别去了.

examples.text: 这家酒店离机场很近，此外，价格也不贵。
examples.reading: zhè jiā jiǔdiàn lí jīchǎng hěn jìn, cǐwài, jiàgé yě bú guì.
examples.translation: This hotel is close to the airport; besides, it is not expensive.

examples.text: 哥哥喜欢安静，而弟弟喜欢热闹。
examples.reading: gēge xǐhuan ānjìng, ér dìdi xǐhuan rènao.
examples.translation: The older brother likes quiet, whereas the younger one likes a lively scene.

examples.text: 既然来了，就多住几天吧。
examples.reading: jìrán lái le, jiù duō zhù jǐ tiān ba.
examples.translation: Since you are here, stay a few more days.

examples.reading: tā máng de shènzhì wàng le chīfàn.
examples.translation: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.

examples.text: 这个办法不错，不过有点儿麻烦。
examples.reading: zhège bànfǎ búcuò, búguò yǒudiǎnr máfan.
examples.translation: This method is good, but it is a bit of a bother.

examples.text: 他同意了我的意见，并且帮我说服了大家。
examples.reading: tā tóngyì le wǒ de yìjiàn, bìngqiě bāng wǒ shuōfú le dàjiā.
examples.translation: He agreed with me and also helped me win everyone over.

examples.text: 因为堵车，他迟到了半个小时。
examples.reading: yīnwèi dǔchē, tā chídào le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: Because of a traffic jam, he was half an hour late.

lessons.title: Clause links 不光 不仅 另外 要是 因此 由于 加上
lessons.summary: 不光 and 不仅 mean not only, 另外 adds something else, 要是 means if, 因此 means therefore, 由于 gives a cause clause, and 加上 adds one more reason.
pattern: 不仅 / 不光 + A，还 / 也 / 而且 + B
由于 + cause，(因此) + result; reason 1，加上 + reason 2
body: 不仅 (bùjǐn) and its spoken twin 不光 (bùguāng) mean not only; the second clause adds with 还, 也 or 而且: 他不光会开车，还会修车. 另外 (lìngwài) means in addition and often stands alone before a comma: 我没时间，另外，我也不太想去. 要是 (yàoshi) is a spoken if, usually with 就 in the result.

由于 (yóuyú) followed by a whole clause gives the cause, and 因此 (yīncǐ) introduces the result: 由于工作太忙，他很久没回家了, 他每天锻炼，因此身体很好. 加 is used mostly as 加上 (on top of that), adding one more reason before the result: 路太远，加上又下雨，我们就没去.
The contrast example uses 而且 (moreover), from HSK 3, the usual partner of 不仅: 他不仅聪明，而且很努力. 而且 opens the second half; 不仅 opens the first.
Common mistake: 因此 at the start of the cause clause, as in 因此天气不好，比赛取消了. 因此 introduces the result; the cause takes 由于 or 因为.

examples.text: 他不光会开车，还会修车。
examples.reading: tā bùguāng huì kāichē, hái huì xiū chē.
examples.translation: He can not only drive but also repair cars.

examples.text: 不仅学生喜欢他，老师也喜欢他。
examples.reading: bùjǐn xuésheng xǐhuan tā, lǎoshī yě xǐhuan tā.
examples.translation: Not only do the students like him, the teachers do too.

examples.text: 我没时间，另外，我也不太想去。
examples.reading: wǒ méi shíjiān, lìngwài, wǒ yě bú tài xiǎng qù.
examples.translation: I have no time; besides, I do not really want to go.

examples.text: 要是有问题，随时给我打电话。
examples.reading: yàoshi yǒu wèntí, suíshí gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: If there is a problem, call me any time.

examples.text: 他每天锻炼，因此身体很好。
examples.reading: tā měi tiān duànliàn, yīncǐ shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He exercises every day, so he is very healthy.

examples.text: 由于工作太忙，他很久没回家了。
examples.reading: yóuyú gōngzuò tài máng, tā hěn jiǔ méi huí jiā le.
examples.translation: Because work has been so busy, he has not been home for a long time.

examples.text: 路太远，加上又下雨，我们就没去。
examples.reading: lù tài yuǎn, jiāshang yòu xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù méi qù.
examples.translation: It was too far, and on top of that it was raining, so we did not go.

examples.text: 他不仅聪明，而且很努力。
examples.reading: tā bùjǐn cōngming, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: He is not only clever but also hard-working.

lessons.title: Particles 等 者 之 就是: and so on, the person who, of, that is all
lessons.summary: 等 ends a list (and so on), 者 makes a noun for a person who does something, 之 is a written of in set forms such as 之一 and 三分之一, and 就是 at the end of a sentence means that is all there is to it.
pattern: V / N + 者 (作者, 读者)
N + 之一; number + 分之 + number; clause + 就是 (了)
body: 等 (děng) after a list says there are more items like these, and can be followed by the general noun: 苹果、香蕉等水果. 者 (zhě) attaches to a verb or noun to make a word for the person: 作者 (author), 读者 (reader), 记者 (reporter). 之 (zhī) is a written-style 的 that survives in fixed forms: 学生之一 (one of the students), 三分之一 (one third).
就是 at the end of a sentence, often with 了, reassures: just do it and that is all: 这事你别管了，我来办就是了.
The contrast example uses the suffix 们, from HSK 1: 记者们都来了. 们 makes a person noun plural; 者 makes the person noun in the first place.
Common mistake: 三分的一. Fractions need 之: 三分之一.

examples.text: 我去超市买了苹果、香蕉等水果。
examples.reading: wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi le píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo děng shuǐguǒ.
examples.translation: I went to the supermarket and bought apples, bananas and other fruit.

examples.text: 这本书的作者是一位老师。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The author of this book is a teacher.

examples.text: 这本杂志有很多年轻读者。
examples.reading: zhè běn zázhì yǒu hěn duō niánqīng dúzhě.
examples.translation: This magazine has many young readers.

examples.text: 他是我们班最好的学生之一。
examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì hǎo de xuésheng zhī yī.
examples.translation: He is one of the best students in our class.

examples.reading: sān fēn zhī yī de tóngxué méi lái.
examples.translation: A third of the classmates did not come.

examples.text: 这事你别管了，我来办就是了。
examples.reading: zhè shì nǐ bié guǎn le, wǒ lái bàn jiùshì le.
examples.translation: Leave this to me; I will just take care of it.

examples.reading: jìzhěmen dōu lái le.
examples.translation: The reporters have all come.

lessons.title: Interjections 啊 and 嗯: surprise, asking again, agreeing
lessons.summary: 啊 at the start of a sentence shows surprise, realisation or a request to repeat, depending on its tone; 嗯 says yes, I see, or asks a puzzled question.
body: An interjection stands alone at the front of the sentence, followed by a comma, a question mark or an exclamation mark. 啊 changes meaning with its tone: ā shows surprise or admiration (啊，下雪了！), á asks someone to repeat (啊？你说什么？), à shows sudden understanding (啊，原来是你！). 嗯 with a falling tone, ǹ, says yes or I see (嗯，我知道了); with a rising tone, ń, it asks a puzzled question (嗯？他怎么还没来？).
The contrast example uses 啊 as a sentence-final particle, from HSK 1: 你快来啊！. At the end, toneless a softens or urges; at the front, with a tone, it is an interjection.
Common mistake: putting a particle such as 吗 or 呢 where the interjection goes, as in 吗？你说什么？. Particles only end sentences.

examples.reading: ā, xià xuě le!
examples.translation: Oh, it is snowing!

examples.reading: á? nǐ shuō shénme?
examples.translation: Huh? What did you say?

examples.reading: à, yuánlái shì nǐ!
examples.translation: Ah, so it is you!

examples.reading: ǹ, wǒ zhīdào le.
examples.translation: Mm, I see.

examples.reading: ń? tā zěnme hái méi lái?
examples.translation: Hm? Why has he still not come?

examples.reading: ǹ, zhège zhǔyi búcuò.
examples.translation: Mm, that is a good idea.

examples.reading: nǐ kuài lái a!
examples.translation: Come quickly!

lessons.title: Number + adjective + measure word: 一大杯, 一小块, 一整天
lessons.summary: A few short adjectives such as 大, 小 and 整 can go between the number and the measure word: 一大杯水, 一小块蛋糕, 一整天.
pattern: number + 大 / 小 / 整 + MW + N
body: Between the number and the measure word, Chinese allows only a few one-syllable adjectives, mainly 大 (big), 小 (small) and 整 (whole): 一大杯水 (a big glass of water), 一小块蛋糕 (a small piece of cake), 一整天 (a whole day), 两大箱书 (two big boxes of books), 一大群孩子 (a big crowd of children).
The contrast example uses 很 + adjective + 的 after the measure word: 一个很大的房子. A longer or modified adjective cannot go between the number and the measure word; it follows the measure word with 的.
Common mistake: 一很大杯水 or 一漂亮件衣服. Only bare 大, 小, 整 and a few others go inside; say 一件很漂亮的衣服.

examples.text: 他一口气喝了一大杯水。
examples.reading: tā yìkǒuqì hē le yí dà bēi shuǐ.
examples.translation: He drank a big glass of water in one go.

examples.reading: wǒ zhǐ chī le yì xiǎo kuài dàngāo.
examples.translation: I only ate a small piece of cake.

examples.reading: wǒ děng le nǐ yì zhěng tiān.
examples.translation: I waited for you a whole day.

examples.reading: tā bān lái le liǎng dà xiāng shū.
examples.translation: He brought over two big boxes of books.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí dà qún háizi.
examples.translation: A big crowd of children is standing at the door.

examples.text: 他住在一个很大的房子里。
examples.reading: tā zhù zài yí ge hěn dà de fángzi li.
examples.translation: He lives in a very big house.

lessons.title: Four-character frames 一A一B, 无A无B, 有A有B
lessons.summary: 一A一B shows wholeness or alternation (一模一样, 一问一答), 无A无B means without any (无忧无虑), and 有A有B means having both, full of life (有说有笑).
body: These frames put two related words into a fixed four-character shape. 一A一B expresses wholeness or two actions taking turns: 一模一样 (exactly alike), 一心一意 (wholeheartedly), 一问一答 (one asks, the other answers). 无A无B means completely without: 无忧无虑 (carefree), 无影无踪 (without a trace). 有A有B means having both, lively and full: 有说有笑 (chatting and laughing), 有声有色 (vivid).

Each expression is fixed: you cannot move A and B into another frame. The contrast example uses AABB reduplication, from HSK 3: 洗得干干净净. AABB repeats an adjective for vividness; it is not one of these frames, so 无干无净 is not a word.
Common mistake: making up a new four-character form by analogy, such as 有忧有虑. Learn each expression as a whole.

examples.translation: The children live a carefree life.

examples.reading: xiǎotōu pǎo de wúyǐng-wúzōng.
examples.translation: The thief ran off without a trace.

examples.text: 大家坐在一起有说有笑。

examples.translation: Everyone sat together, chatting and laughing.

examples.translation: Mum washed the clothes spotlessly clean.

lessons.title: Fixed phrases: 来得及/来不及, 有的是, 说不定, 不怎么, 就是说
lessons.summary: Five set phrases of everyday speech: there is or is not enough time, there is plenty of something, maybe, not very, and that is to say.
pattern: 来得及 / 来不及 + V
N + 有的是; 说不定 + clause
不怎么 + V / Adj; ……，(这)就是说……
body: 来得及 (láidejí) means there is still time to do something, and 来不及 (láibují) means it is too late: 现在出发还来得及; 快跑，要来不及了. Both can be followed by a verb (来不及吃早饭) but not by a noun. 有的是 (yǒudeshì) comes after a noun and means there is plenty of it: 时间有的是. 说不定 (shuōbudìng) means maybe, it could well be, and stands before the clause or the verb: 说不定会下雨.

不怎么 (bù zěnme) softens a negative: not very, not much. 我不怎么喜欢吃辣的 is gentler than 我不喜欢. 就是说 or 这就是说 (that is to say, which means) restates or draws the consequence of what was just said: 商店九点关门，就是说我们还有一个小时.

The contrast example uses 赶不上 with a vehicle: 我们赶不上火车了. 来不及 cannot take a noun object, so 来不及火车 is wrong; with a train or bus say 赶不上. A common mistake is mixing up 说不定 and 不一定: 说不定会下雨 leans towards yes (it may well rain), while 不一定会下雨 leans towards no (it won't necessarily rain).

examples.reading: xiànzài chūfā hái láidejí.
examples.translation: If we leave now, we can still make it.

examples.reading: kuài pǎo, yào láibují le!
examples.translation: Run, we're going to be late!

examples.translation: Don't worry, there's plenty of time.

examples.text: 天这么阴，说不定会下雨。
examples.reading: tiān zhème yīn, shuōbudìng huì xià yǔ.
examples.translation: The sky is so dark, it might rain.

examples.reading: wǒ bù zěnme xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.translation: I don't really like spicy food.

examples.text: 商店九点关门，就是说我们还有一个小时。
examples.reading: shāngdiàn jiǔ diǎn guānmén, jiùshì shuō wǒmen hái yǒu yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: The shop closes at nine, which means we still have an hour.

examples.text: 票卖完了，这就是说我们只能明天来。
examples.reading: piào mài wán le, zhè jiùshì shuō wǒmen zhǐ néng míngtiān lái.
examples.translation: The tickets are sold out, which means we can only come tomorrow.

examples.reading: wǒmen gǎn bu shàng huǒchē le.
examples.translation: We're not going to make the train.

lessons.title: Frames for degree, scope and purpose: 一天比一天, 在……方面, 够……的, 拿……来说, 为了……而……
lessons.summary: Five fixed frames: a steady change (一天比一天), a field (在……方面), a strong degree (够……的), an example (拿……来说) and a purpose (为了……而……).
pattern: 一 + M + 比 + 一 + M + Adj
在 + N + 方面; 够 + Adj + 的; 拿 + N + 来说
body: 一 + measure word + 比 + 一 + measure word says something changes step by step or that each one beats the last: 天气一天比一天冷了, 一个比一个高. 在……方面 names the field a comment is about: 在学习方面，他很努力. 够……的 marks a high degree in speech, often with 真: 今天真够冷的, 这条路够长的.
拿……来说 introduces an example: 拿我来说 (take me, for instance), 拿北京来说. 为了……而…… links a purpose to an action in a more written style: 他为了理想而努力. 而 sits between the purpose and the verb.

The contrast example uses 因为: 因为身体不舒服，他今天没来上班. 因为 gives a cause; 为了 gives a goal. Feeling unwell is not a goal, so 为了身体不舒服 is wrong. A common mistake is dropping 的 in 够……的 (今天真够冷 sounds cut off) or using 拿……说 without 来.

examples.reading: tiānqì yì tiān bǐ yì tiān lěng le.
examples.translation: The weather is getting colder day by day.

examples.reading: zài xuéxí fāngmiàn, tā hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: When it comes to studying, he works very hard.

examples.reading: jīntiān zhēn gòu lěng de.
examples.translation: It's really cold today.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo lù gòu cháng de.
examples.translation: This road is pretty long.

examples.text: 拿我来说，我每天都跑步。
examples.reading: ná wǒ lái shuō, wǒ měi tiān dōu pǎobù.
examples.translation: Take me, for example: I run every day.

examples.text: 拿北京来说，冬天非常冷。
examples.reading: ná Běijīng lái shuō, dōngtiān fēicháng lěng.
examples.translation: Take Beijing: the winters are very cold.

examples.reading: tā wèile lǐxiǎng ér nǔlì.
examples.translation: He works hard for his ideals.

examples.text: 因为身体不舒服，他今天没来上班。
examples.reading: yīnwèi shēntǐ bù shūfu, tā jīntiān méi lái shàngbān.
examples.translation: He did not come to work today because he was not feeling well.

lessons.title: Emphatic frames: 再也不/没, 怎么都不, 说什么也得, X也得X，不X也得X
lessons.summary: Four frames that push a statement to the extreme: never again, not however hard you try, must at any cost, and must whether you like it or not.
pattern: 再也 + 不 / 没 + V
怎么 + 都 / 也 + 不 / 没 + V
说什么 / 怎么(着) + 也得 + V; V也得V，不V也得V
body: 再也不 + verb says something will never happen again: 我再也不喝酒了. 再也没 + verb says it has not happened since: 他走了以后，再也没回来过. 怎么都 or 怎么也 + a negative says that no matter how you try, the result does not come: 这个门怎么都打不开, 我怎么也没想到他会来.
说什么也得 and 怎么（着）也得 say something must happen at any cost: 你说什么也得来, 我怎么着也得把作业写完. V也得V，不V也得V says the action is unavoidable, wanted or not: 这药你吃也得吃，不吃也得吃.

The contrast example uses 又 for a repeated past event: 小李又忘了带钥匙. 再 looks forward (再也不 = never again from now on); 又 looks back at something that has already happened again, so 再忘了 is wrong in a plain statement. A common mistake is 再不也 or 也再不: the order is always 再 + 也 + 不 or 没.

examples.reading: wǒ zài yě bù hē jiǔ le.
examples.translation: I'm never drinking again.

examples.text: 他走了以后，再也没回来过。
examples.reading: tā zǒu le yǐhòu, zài yě méi huílai guo.
examples.translation: After he left, he never came back.

examples.reading: zhège mén zěnme dōu dǎ bu kāi.
examples.translation: This door just won't open, whatever I do.

examples.text: 我怎么也没想到他会来。
examples.reading: wǒ zěnme yě méi xiǎngdào tā huì lái.
examples.translation: I never imagined he would come.

examples.reading: nǐ shuō shénme yě děi lái!
examples.translation: You have to come, no matter what!

examples.text: 我怎么着也得把作业写完。
examples.reading: wǒ zěnmezhe yě děi bǎ zuòyè xiě wán.
examples.translation: Whatever happens, I have to finish my homework.

examples.text: 这药你吃也得吃，不吃也得吃。
examples.reading: zhè yào nǐ chī yě děi chī, bù chī yě děi chī.
examples.translation: You're taking this medicine whether you like it or not.

examples.reading: Xiǎo Lǐ yòu wàng le dài yàoshi.
examples.translation: Xiao Li forgot his keys again.

lessons.title: Frames of acceptance: 能V一X是一X, 有什么好V的, X是X，Y是Y, X就是了, X是X
lessons.summary: Five colloquial frames for making the best of things, dismissing something, keeping things apart, and saying that is all there is to it.
pattern: 能 + V + 一X + 是 + 一X; (没)有什么(好) + V + 的
body: 能 + verb + 一X是一X says every little bit counts, so do as much as you can: 钱不多，能省一块是一块. (没)有什么(好) + verb + 的 says there is nothing worth doing it about: 这有什么好哭的 (what is there to cry about), 这种小事没什么好说的.

X是X，Y是Y keeps two things apart: 生意是生意，朋友是朋友 (business and friendship are different matters). X是X on its own repeats a noun to say it is what it is: 孩子到底是孩子 (kids are kids). X就是了 at the end of a sentence means just do X, that is all, and often reassures: 你别生气，我去就是了; 有问题你问我就是了.
The contrast example uses 好 + verb meaning easy to: 这个问题很好回答. In 有什么好V的, 好 means worth; in 很好回答 it means easy. A common mistake is leaving out 的 at the end of 有什么好V的 (有什么好哭 sounds unfinished).

examples.text: 钱不多，能省一块是一块。
examples.reading: qián bù duō, néng shěng yí kuài shì yí kuài.
examples.translation: Money is tight; every yuan saved counts.

examples.reading: zhè yǒu shénme hǎo kū de?
examples.translation: What is there to cry about?

examples.text: 这种小事没什么好说的。
examples.reading: zhè zhǒng xiǎo shì méi shénme hǎo shuō de.
examples.translation: There's nothing worth saying about a small thing like this.

examples.text: 生意是生意，朋友是朋友。
examples.reading: shēngyi shì shēngyi, péngyou shì péngyou.
examples.translation: Business is business, and friends are friends.

examples.text: 孩子到底是孩子，玩儿起来什么都忘了。
examples.reading: háizi dàodǐ shì háizi, wánr qǐlai shénme dōu wàng le.
examples.translation: Kids are kids after all: once they start playing, they forget everything.

examples.reading: nǐ bié shēngqì, wǒ qù jiùshì le.
examples.translation: Don't be angry, I'll go, all right?

examples.reading: yǒu wèntí nǐ wèn wǒ jiùshì le.
examples.translation: If you have questions, just ask me.

examples.reading: zhège wèntí hěn hǎo huídá.
examples.translation: This question is easy to answer.

lessons.title: Colloquial frames: 还X呢, 你V你的吧, 让你V你就V, X就X点儿吧
lessons.summary: Four spoken frames: mocking a title someone does not live up to, telling someone to carry on, telling someone to just do as told, and accepting a drawback.
pattern: 你 + V + 你的(+ N) + 吧; 让 / 叫 + 你 + V + 你就 + V
Adj + 就 + Adj + (点儿) + 吧
body: 还 + noun + 呢 mocks someone who does not live up to a title: 还大学生呢，连这个字都不认识 (and you call yourself a university student). 你V你的吧 tells someone to carry on with their own business: 你忙你的吧，不用管我.
让你V你就V or 叫你V你就V means do as you are told, without arguing: 让你走你就走; 叫你吃你就吃吧. X就X（点儿）吧 accepts a drawback: 贵就贵点儿吧 (so it costs a bit more, fine); 远就远吧.
The contrast example uses 还 + verb + 呢 meaning still: 外面还下着雨呢. That is a plain statement of time; the mocking frame has a noun after 还 (还老师呢). A common mistake is 你忙你吧 without 的: the frame needs 你的.

examples.text: 还大学生呢，连这个字都不认识。
examples.reading: hái dàxuéshēng ne, lián zhège zì dōu bú rènshi.
examples.translation: Some university student you are, you can't even read this character.

examples.text: 还老师呢，自己都写错了。
examples.reading: hái lǎoshī ne, zìjǐ dōu xiě cuò le.
examples.translation: Some teacher you are: you got it wrong yourself.

examples.reading: nǐ máng nǐ de ba, bú yòng guǎn wǒ.
examples.translation: You get on with your work, don't mind me.

examples.text: 让你走你就走，别问那么多。
examples.reading: ràng nǐ zǒu nǐ jiù zǒu, bié wèn nàme duō.
examples.translation: When you're told to go, just go, and don't ask so many questions.

examples.reading: jiào nǐ chī nǐ jiù chī ba.
examples.translation: If you're told to eat, just eat.

examples.text: 贵就贵点儿吧，质量好就行。
examples.reading: guì jiù guì diǎnr ba, zhìliàng hǎo jiù xíng.
examples.translation: So it costs a bit more, never mind, as long as the quality is good.

examples.reading: yuǎn jiù yuǎn ba, wǒmen zuò chē qù.
examples.translation: It's far, so what, we'll take the bus.

examples.reading: wàimian hái xià zhe yǔ ne.
examples.translation: It is still raining outside.

lessons.title: Degree complements 死了 and 得厉害: extremely, terribly
lessons.summary: After an adjective or a feeling verb, 死了 and 得厉害 say the degree is extreme: 热死了, 疼得厉害.
pattern: feeling verb + 死 + O + 了
body: 死了 (sǐ le) after an adjective or a verb of feeling is a spoken way to say extremely: 今天热死了, 我饿死了, 他高兴死了. It does not mean anyone died. With a feeling verb that takes an object, the object goes between 死 and 了: 我想死你了.
厉害 (lìhai) as a degree complement needs 得 before it: 他的头疼得厉害, 这几天我忙得厉害. It mostly describes something unpleasant (pain, worry, being busy). 死了 is more casual than 得厉害.

The contrast example uses 极了: 这道菜好吃极了. 极了 is neutral and fine in writing and for good things; 死了 is casual and usually complains. A common mistake is adding 得 before 死了 (疼得死了) or dropping it before 厉害 (疼厉害).

examples.reading: jīntiān rè sǐ le.
examples.translation: It's boiling today.

examples.reading: wǒ è sǐ le, kuài chī fàn ba.
examples.translation: I'm starving, let's eat.

examples.text: 考试通过了，他高兴死了。
examples.reading: kǎoshì tōngguò le, tā gāoxìng sǐ le.
examples.translation: He passed the exam and was over the moon.

examples.reading: tā de tóu téng de lìhai.
examples.translation: His head hurts badly.

examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān wǒ máng de lìhai.
examples.translation: I've been terribly busy these last few days.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng sǐ nǐ le!
examples.translation: I've missed you so much!

examples.reading: zhè dào cài hǎochī jí le.
examples.translation: This dish is absolutely delicious.

lessons.title: Potential complement 得了 / 不了: can or cannot manage
lessons.summary: V得了 and V不了 (liǎo) say whether an action can happen at all, or whether there is too much to finish.
body: 了 read liǎo after 得 or 不 is a potential complement. V不了 says something cannot happen: 明天的会他来不了了, 这件事我永远忘不了. With eating and drinking it also means there is too much to finish: 这么多菜，我们吃不了. 外面雨这么大，飞机起飞得了吗 asks whether it can happen at all. V得了 is the positive form, common in questions and answers: 你一个人搬得了这张桌子吗; 这点儿小事我做得了.
Read the complement liǎo, not le: 来不了 (lái bu liǎo). A final 了 (le) can still follow, as in 他来不了了.

The contrast example uses the result complement 完 in its potential form: 作业太多，今天写不完. 写不完 says there is too much to finish; 写不了 would say the writing cannot happen at all (no pen, no time). A common mistake is putting 不 before the verb (不来了 means will not come, a decision, not cannot come).

examples.text: 外面雨这么大，飞机起飞得了吗？
examples.reading: wàimian yǔ zhème dà, fēijī qǐfēi de liǎo ma?
examples.translation: With rain this heavy outside, can the plane take off?

examples.text: 你一个人搬得了这张桌子吗？
examples.reading: nǐ yí ge rén bān de liǎo zhè zhāng zhuōzi ma?
examples.translation: Can you move this table on your own?

examples.reading: míngtiān de huì tā lái bu liǎo le.
examples.translation: He can't make tomorrow's meeting.

examples.reading: zhè diǎnr xiǎo shì wǒ zuò de liǎo.
examples.translation: I can handle a small thing like this.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ yǒngyuǎn wàng bu liǎo.
examples.translation: I'll never forget this.

examples.reading: tā bìng le, cānjiā bu liǎo bǐsài.
examples.translation: He's ill and can't take part in the competition.

examples.reading: zuòyè tài duō, jīntiān xiě bu wán.
examples.translation: There's too much homework to finish today.

lessons.title: Rhetorical questions with 难道……吗？
lessons.summary: 难道 turns a question into a challenge: the speaker expects the opposite answer and shows surprise or reproach.
body: 难道 (nándào) starts a rhetorical question: the speaker does not want information but insists on the opposite. 难道你没看见墙上的通知吗 means surely you saw it. 难道 can stand before or after the subject, and 吗 usually ends the sentence, though it is sometimes left out: 这么简单的题，难道你也不会？
A negative question with 难道 means a positive (你难道不想家吗 = you must miss home); a positive one means a negative (难道我说错了吗 = I didn't say anything wrong).

The contrast example uses 到底: 他到底来不来？ 到底 presses for a real answer in a genuine question; 难道 expects no answer. 到底 cannot go with 吗, and 难道 cannot go with an A-not-A question such as 来不来. A common mistake is answering a 难道 question as if it were a real one.

examples.text: 难道你没看见墙上的通知吗？
examples.reading: nándào nǐ méi kànjiàn qiáng shang de tōngzhī ma?
examples.translation: Surely you saw the notice on the wall?

examples.reading: tā nándào méi gàosu nǐ ma?
examples.translation: Don't tell me he didn't tell you?

examples.text: 这么简单的题，难道你也不会？
examples.reading: zhème jiǎndān de tí, nándào nǐ yě bú huì?
examples.translation: A question this easy, and you can't do it either?

examples.reading: nándào wǒ shuō cuò le ma?
examples.translation: Did I say something wrong, then?

examples.reading: nǐ nándào bù xiǎng jiā ma?
examples.translation: Don't you miss home?

examples.reading: tā dàodǐ lái bu lái?
examples.translation: Is he coming or not?

lessons.title: Rhetorical questions with question words: 谁说, 哪儿知道, 有什么, 怎么能
lessons.summary: A question word in a rhetorical question asks nothing: 谁说我不去？ means I am going; 我哪儿知道？ means I have no idea.
pattern: S + 哪儿 / 怎么 + 能 / 知道 + ……？
有什么 + Adj + 的？; V + 什么？
body: 谁, 哪儿, 什么 and 怎么 can make a rhetorical question that states the opposite. 谁说我不去 means of course I am going. 我哪儿知道他的电话 means I don't know his number. 跑三公里有什么难的 means it is not hard at all. 我怎么能不管他呢 means I must look after him.
Verb + 什么 tells someone to stop doing something: 你急什么 (what's the rush, calm down), 你笑什么. The tone, often with 呢 at the end, shows that no answer is wanted.

The contrast example is a real question with 谁: 刚才谁给你打电话了？ The speaker wants a name. Context decides: with 说 or 知道 and a strong tone, 谁 is rhetorical; asking about a fact, it is a real question. A common mistake is putting 哪儿 after the verb: rhetorical 哪儿 stands before the verb (我哪儿知道), while a 哪儿 after the verb asks about a real place.

examples.reading: shéi shuō wǒ bú qù?
examples.translation: Who says I'm not going?

examples.reading: wǒ nǎr zhīdào tā de diànhuà?
examples.translation: How would I know his phone number?

examples.reading: pǎo sān gōnglǐ yǒu shénme nán de?
examples.translation: What's so hard about running three kilometres?

examples.reading: wǒ zěnme néng bù guǎn tā ne?
examples.translation: How could I not look after him?

examples.reading: nǐ jí shénme?
examples.translation: What's the rush?

examples.reading: gāngcái shéi gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà le?
examples.translation: Who called you just now?

lessons.title: 把 with a reduplicated verb (擦一擦, 洗了洗) and with V + 了 (把药吃了)
lessons.summary: In a 把 sentence the verb cannot stand bare: reduplicate it for a quick action (把桌子擦一擦) or add 了 for a finished one (把牛奶喝了).
pattern: S + 把 + O + V + (一 / 了) + V
S + 把 + O + V + 了
body: 把 moves the object before the verb to say what is done to it, and the verb must carry something after it. A reduplicated verb says do it briefly or casually: 你把桌子擦一擦, 我们把房间打扫打扫吧. 一 goes between one-syllable verbs (擦一擦, 读一读); for a finished action use 了 (妈妈把菜洗了洗).
Verb + 了 after 把 + object says the thing has been dealt with, often used up or gone: 我把那杯牛奶喝了, 快把药吃了, 他把旧手机卖了.
The contrast example uses 被: 我的手机被弟弟弄坏了. With 把 the doer is the subject (弟弟把手机弄坏了); with 被 the thing affected is the subject. A common mistake is a bare verb after 把: 我把饭吃 is wrong; say 我把饭吃了.

examples.reading: nǐ bǎ zhuōzi cā yi cā.
examples.translation: Give the table a wipe.

examples.reading: māma bǎ cài xǐ le xǐ.
examples.translation: Mum gave the vegetables a rinse.

examples.text: 我们把房间打扫打扫吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen bǎ fángjiān dǎsǎo dǎsǎo ba.
examples.translation: Let's give the room a clean.

examples.text: 你再把这个句子读一读。
examples.reading: nǐ zài bǎ zhège jùzi dú yi dú.
examples.translation: Read this sentence through once more.

examples.reading: wǒ bǎ nà bēi niúnǎi hē le.
examples.translation: I drank that glass of milk.

examples.reading: kuài bǎ yào chī le!
examples.translation: Take your medicine, quickly!

examples.text: 我的手机被弟弟弄坏了。
examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī bèi dìdi nòng huài le.
examples.translation: My phone got broken by my little brother.

lessons.title: 把 with a count or duration after the verb (读了两遍) and with an adverbial before the verb (都, 轻轻地, 往……一放)
lessons.summary: After 把 + object the verb can be followed by how many times or how long, or preceded by an adverbial such as 都, 轻轻地 or 往桌子上.
pattern: S + 把 + O + V + 了 + number + 遍 / 次 / time
S + 把 + O + adverbial + V (+ other)
body: A 把 sentence can end with a count of times or a length of time: 老师把课文读了两遍, 他把这个问题想了很久, 他把车修了一下午. The count still comes after the verb, never before it.
An adverbial can also stand between the object and the verb: 你把门轻轻地关上, 你把这些水果都吃了吧, 他把书往桌子上一放，就走了. 都 placed here sums up the object (all the fruit), so it follows the object.

The contrast example uses 过 without 把: 这部电影我看过三次. A count of past experiences with 过 is not a 把 sentence; put the object first as a topic instead. A common mistake is putting the count before the verb (把课文两遍读了).

examples.reading: lǎoshī bǎ kèwén dú le liǎng biàn.
examples.translation: The teacher read the text twice.

examples.text: 他把这个问题想了很久。
examples.reading: tā bǎ zhège wèntí xiǎng le hěn jiǔ.
examples.translation: He thought about this problem for a long time.

examples.reading: tā bǎ chē xiū le yí xiàwǔ.
examples.translation: He spent the whole afternoon fixing the car.

examples.reading: nǐ bǎ mén qīngqīng de guān shàng.
examples.translation: Close the door gently.

examples.text: 你把这些水果都吃了吧。
examples.reading: nǐ bǎ zhèxiē shuǐguǒ dōu chī le ba.
examples.translation: Eat up all this fruit.

examples.text: 他把书往桌子上一放，就走了。
examples.reading: tā bǎ shū wǎng zhuōzi shàng yí fàng, jiù zǒu le.
examples.translation: He dropped the book on the table and left.

examples.reading: zhè bù diànyǐng wǒ kàn guo sān cì.
examples.translation: I've seen this film three times.

lessons.title: Spoken passives with 叫 and 让
lessons.summary: In speech 叫 and 让 work like 被: the thing affected is the subject, the doer follows 叫/让, and the verb needs a result or 了.
pattern: S + 叫 / 让 + doer + V + result / 了
S + 叫 / 让 + doer + 给 + V + 了
body: 叫 (jiào) and 让 (ràng) make a passive in everyday speech, usually for something unwelcome: 那本小说叫同学借走了, 我的作业让小狗弄脏了, 我的手机让妹妹拿去玩了. 给 can stand before the verb for emphasis: 钱包叫小偷给偷了.
Unlike 被, 叫 and 让 must name the doer (同学, 小狗, 妹妹). The verb also needs something after it: a result (打破, 弄脏), a direction (借走) or a count (批评了一顿).
The contrast example uses 被 with no doer: 我的电脑被修好了. 被 can leave the doer out; 叫 and 让 cannot, so 电脑叫修好了 is wrong. A common mistake is a bare verb: 杯子叫他打 is incomplete; say 杯子叫他打破了.

examples.text: 那本小说叫同学借走了。
examples.reading: nà běn xiǎoshuō jiào tóngxué jiè zǒu le.
examples.translation: That novel was borrowed by a classmate.

examples.text: 我的作业让小狗弄脏了。
examples.reading: wǒ de zuòyè ràng xiǎo gǒu nòng zāng le.
examples.translation: My homework got dirtied by the puppy.

examples.reading: bēizi jiào tā dǎ pò le.
examples.translation: The cup was broken by him.

examples.text: 我的手机让妹妹拿去玩了。
examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī ràng mèimei ná qù wánr le.
examples.translation: My phone was taken by my little sister to play with.

examples.reading: qiánbāo jiào xiǎotōu gěi tōu le.
examples.translation: The wallet was stolen by a thief.

examples.reading: tā ràng lǎobǎn pīpíng le yí dùn.
examples.translation: He got told off by his boss.

examples.reading: wǒ de diànnǎo bèi xiū hǎo le.
examples.translation: My computer has been fixed.

lessons.title: Pivot sentences: praising or blaming someone for doing something, choosing someone as something
lessons.summary: 表扬/批评 + person + what they did gives the reason for praise or blame; 选/收 + person + 做/当/为 + role names a role.
pattern: S + 表扬 / 批评 + person + VP
S + 选 / 收 + person + 做 / 当 / 为 + role
body: In these pivot sentences one person is the object of the first verb and the subject of what follows. With 表扬 (praise) and 批评 (criticise), the second part says what the person did: 老师表扬小明帮助同学, 妈妈批评弟弟不吃早饭.
With 选 (choose, elect) and 收 (take on), the second verb 做, 当 or 为 (wéi, more formal) names the role: 我们选他当班长, 王老师收我做学生, 大家选她为代表, 公司选小李做经理.

The contrast example uses 请, from the earlier pivot sentences: 他请我去他家吃饭. 请 asks someone to do something that has not happened yet; 表扬 and 批评 comment on something already done. A common mistake is using 是 for the role (选他是班长); use 当, 做 or 为.

examples.text: 老师表扬小明帮助同学。
examples.reading: lǎoshī biǎoyáng Xiǎo Míng bāngzhù tóngxué.
examples.translation: The teacher praised Xiao Ming for helping his classmates.

examples.text: 妈妈批评弟弟不吃早饭。
examples.reading: māma pīpíng dìdi bù chī zǎofàn.
examples.translation: Mum told my little brother off for skipping breakfast.

examples.reading: wǒmen xuǎn tā dāng bānzhǎng.
examples.translation: We elected him class monitor.

examples.reading: Wáng lǎoshī shōu wǒ zuò xuésheng.
examples.translation: Teacher Wang took me on as a student.

examples.reading: dàjiā xuǎn tā wéi dàibiǎo.
examples.translation: Everyone chose her as their representative.

examples.reading: gōngsī xuǎn Xiǎo Lǐ zuò jīnglǐ.
examples.translation: The company picked Xiao Li to be manager.

examples.reading: tā qǐng wǒ qù tā jiā chī fàn.
examples.translation: He invited me to his place for dinner.

lessons.title: Causative pivot sentences: 使 / 让 + person + result (这个消息使我很难过)
lessons.summary: 使 and 让 say that a thing or event causes a person to feel or do something: 这个消息使我很难过.
pattern: thing / event + 使 / 让 + person + Adj / VP
body: The subject of a causative 使 or 让 is often a thing or an event, and the person in the middle feels or does the result: 这个消息使我很难过, 他的话让我想起了小时候, 这首歌让我很想家. 人 can stand for anyone: 长时间看手机让人很累.
使 (shǐ) is more formal and written; 让 is the everyday word. A negative usually goes before 让: 你别让我失望.

The contrast example uses 让 as a passive marker: 我的伞让风吹走了. There the subject (the umbrella) suffers the action; in the causative the subject causes a feeling. 使 has no passive use, so 伞使风吹走了 is wrong. A common mistake is putting a possessive in the middle (让我的很想家): the middle slot is the person, 我.

examples.reading: zhège xiāoxi shǐ wǒ hěn nánguò.
examples.translation: This news made me very sad.

examples.text: 他的话让我想起了小时候。
examples.reading: tā de huà ràng wǒ xiǎng qǐ le xiǎoshíhou.
examples.translation: His words reminded me of my childhood.

examples.reading: zhè shǒu gē ràng wǒ hěn xiǎng jiā.
examples.translation: This song makes me really homesick.

examples.text: 长时间看手机让人很累。
examples.reading: cháng shíjiān kàn shǒujī ràng rén hěn lèi.
examples.translation: Looking at a phone for a long time wears you out.

examples.reading: nǐ bié ràng wǒ shīwàng.
examples.translation: Don't let me down.

examples.reading: wǒ de sǎn ràng fēng chuī zǒu le.
examples.translation: My umbrella got blown away by the wind.

lessons.title: Comparisons with 不如 and 跟……相比
lessons.summary: A不如B says A is not as good as B (or not as Adj as B); 跟/和……相比 sets up what something is compared with.
pattern: 跟 / 和 + B + 相比，A + ……
body: A不如B (bùrú) means A is not as good as B: 我的汉语不如他. With an adjective it says A is less so than B: 坐公共汽车不如坐地铁快. It can also recommend the second option: 一个人去不如大家一起去 (better to go together).
跟……相比 or 和……相比 (xiāngbǐ) opens a sentence with the thing compared against, and the comment follows: 跟去年相比，今年的游客多了很多; 和城市相比，农村的空气好多了.
The contrast example uses 没有……那么: 这个房间没有那个房间那么大. 没有 needs an adjective (没有……大); 不如 can stand without one. A common mistake is mixing 比 and 不如 (A比不如B) or adding 很 after 不如 B (不如他很好).

examples.reading: wǒ de Hànyǔ bùrú tā.
examples.translation: My Chinese isn't as good as his.

examples.text: 坐公共汽车不如坐地铁快。
examples.reading: zuò gōnggòng qìchē bùrú zuò dìtiě kuài.
examples.translation: Taking the bus isn't as fast as the subway.

examples.text: 一个人去不如大家一起去。
examples.reading: yí ge rén qù bùrú dàjiā yìqǐ qù.
examples.translation: Going alone isn't as good as all going together.

examples.text: 跟去年相比，今年的游客多了很多。
examples.reading: gēn qùnián xiāngbǐ, jīnnián de yóukè duō le hěn duō.
examples.translation: Compared with last year, there are many more tourists this year.

examples.text: 和城市相比，农村的空气好多了。
examples.reading: hé chéngshì xiāngbǐ, nóngcūn de kōngqì hǎo duō le.
examples.translation: The air in the countryside is much better than in the city.

examples.text: 这个房间没有那个房间那么大。
examples.reading: zhège fángjiān méiyǒu nàge fángjiān nàme dà.
examples.translation: This room isn't as big as that one.

lessons.title: Double negatives for emphasis: 不得不, 不能不, 没有……不……, 不是不……
lessons.summary: Two negatives make a strong positive: 不得不 (have no choice but to), 不能不 (must), 没有一个人不…… (everyone), 不是不…… (it is not that … not).
pattern: S + 不得不 / 不能不 / 不会不 + V
没有 + (一个)人 + 不 + V
不是不 + V，是 / 而是 ……
body: A double negative says something positive, more strongly than the plain form. 不得不 (bùdébù) means have no choice but to: 我们不得不回家. 不能不 means must, cannot fail to: 你不能不参加. 不会不 means surely will: 他不会不知道这件事.
没有 + (一个)人 + 不 + verb means everyone: 没有人不知道这件事, 我们班没有一个人不喜欢他. 不是不 + verb softens a refusal by giving the real reason: 我不是不想去，是没有时间. In higher levels you will meet 非……不可, must.

The contrast example has a single negative: 他已经三天没来上课了. One 没 just negates a past event; it is not emphatic. A common mistake is turning 不得不 into 没得不, or reading a double negative as a negative: 不能不去 means you must go.

examples.text: 雨太大了，我们不得不回家。
examples.reading: yǔ tài dà le, wǒmen bùdébù huí jiā.
examples.translation: The rain was so heavy we had to go home.

examples.text: 这么重要的会，你不能不参加。
examples.reading: zhème zhòngyào de huì, nǐ bù néng bù cānjiā.
examples.translation: You can't miss a meeting this important.

examples.text: 我们班没有一个人不喜欢他。
examples.reading: wǒmen bān méiyǒu yí ge rén bù xǐhuan tā.
examples.translation: There's nobody in our class who doesn't like him.

examples.reading: tā bú huì bù zhīdào zhè jiàn shì.
examples.translation: He's bound to know about this.

examples.text: 我不是不想去，是没有时间。
examples.reading: wǒ bú shì bù xiǎng qù, shì méiyǒu shíjiān.
