A common mistake is to put 非常 after 得: 高兴得非常 is wrong; 非常 goes before the adjective (非常高兴).

examples.text: 听到这个消息，她高兴得不得了。
examples.reading: tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā gāoxìng de bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: When she heard the news she was overjoyed.

examples.text: 这几天热得不得了，大家都不想出门。
examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān rè de bùdéliǎo, dàjiā dōu bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.translation: It has been terribly hot these days, and nobody wants to go out.

examples.text: 孩子们想妈妈想得不得了。
examples.reading: háizimen xiǎng māma xiǎng de bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: The children miss their mother terribly.

examples.text: 他担心得不得了，一夜没睡。
examples.reading: tā dānxīn de bùdéliǎo, yí yè méi shuì.
examples.translation: He was worried sick and didn't sleep all night.

examples.text: 她喜欢这只小猫喜欢得不得了。
examples.reading: tā xǐhuan zhè zhī xiǎo māo xǐhuan de bùdéliǎo.
examples.translation: She absolutely adores this kitten.

examples.reading: zhè shǒu gē hǎotīng jí le.
examples.translation: This song sounds wonderful.

lessons.title: 下来 and 下去 for states: settling down, being handed down, carrying on
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 下来 marks a change into a calmer, slower or still state, or something kept from the past until now; 下去 marks carrying on from now into the future.
pattern: V / Adj + 下来 (become still or calm; past to now)
V / Adj + 下去 (go on, continue)
body: 下来 and 下去 also describe states, not only movement downwards. 下来 says something settles from movement or noise into stillness, slowness or darkness: 安静下来, 停了下来, 天色暗了下来. It also says something has been kept from the past until now: 爷爷年轻时的照片都保存了下来.
下去 says an action or state continues from now on: 请继续说下去, 你一定要坚持下去. With an adjective it says a bad trend goes on: 再这样瘦下去. So 下来 looks back from the past to now, and 下去 looks forward from now.
The contrast example uses 起来: 大家都笑了起来. 起来 says something starts, which is the next lesson's point; laughter that starts is 笑起来, not 笑下来.
A common mistake is to use 下去 for settling down: a room becomes quiet with 安静下来, and a car comes to a stop with 停下来. Keep 下去 for going on.

examples.text: 老师一进来，教室里马上安静下来了。
examples.reading: lǎoshī yí jìnlai, jiàoshì li mǎshàng ānjìng xiàlai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the teacher came in, the classroom went quiet.

examples.reading: chē mànmàn tíng le xiàlai.
examples.translation: The car slowly came to a stop.

examples.text: 爷爷年轻时的照片都保存了下来。
examples.reading: yéye niánqīng shí de zhàopiàn dōu bǎocún le xiàlai.
examples.translation: Grandpa's photos from when he was young have all been kept.

examples.text: 你说得很好，请继续说下去。
examples.reading: nǐ shuō de hěn hǎo, qǐng jìxù shuō xiàqu.
examples.translation: You're doing well; please go on.

examples.text: 学外语很难，但是你一定要坚持下去。
examples.reading: xué wàiyǔ hěn nán, dànshì nǐ yídìng yào jiānchí xiàqu.
examples.translation: Learning a foreign language is hard, but you must keep at it.

examples.text: 再这样瘦下去，你的身体会出问题的。
examples.reading: zài zhèyàng shòu xiàqu, nǐ de shēntǐ huì chū wèntí de.
examples.translation: If you keep getting thinner like this, your health will suffer.

examples.text: 听了这个笑话，大家都笑了起来。
examples.reading: tīng le zhège xiàohua, dàjiā dōu xiào le qǐlai.
examples.translation: Everyone burst out laughing at the joke.

lessons.title: 起来, 过来 and 过去 for states: starting, coming round, passing out
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 起来 marks a state or action that starts; 过来 marks a return to a normal state (醒过来, 明白过来); 过去 marks losing the normal state (晕过去, 睡过去).
pattern: V + 过来 (back to normal) / V + 过去 (out of normal)
body: 起来 after a verb or adjective says something begins and goes on: 天气暖和起来了, 两个人吵起来了. With an object, the object goes between 起 and 来: 孩子们唱起歌来了. 起来 also has meanings learned as words: 想起来 (remember), 看起来 (look, seem).

过来 says someone comes back to a normal, conscious or correct state: 病人醒过来了, 他终于明白过来. 过去 is the opposite: someone loses that state, faints or falls asleep: 一位老人晕了过去, 他躺在沙发上就睡过去了. So 醒过来 but 晕过去; they are not interchangeable.
The contrast example uses 下来: 他的话让大家冷静了下来. 下来 says a state settles and becomes calm (previous lesson), not that something starts or recovers.
A common mistake is to put the object after 起来: say 下起雨来, not 下起来雨.

examples.text: 一到周末，这条街就热闹起来了。
examples.reading: yí dào zhōumò, zhè tiáo jiē jiù rènao qǐlai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the weekend comes, this street livens up.

examples.text: 两个人一见面就吵起来了。
examples.reading: liǎng ge rén yí jiànmiàn jiù chǎo qǐlai le.
examples.translation: The two of them started arguing the moment they met.

examples.reading: háizimen chàng qǐ gē lai le.
examples.translation: The children have started singing.

examples.reading: bìngrén zhōngyú xǐng guòlai le.
examples.translation: The patient finally came round.

examples.text: 他听了半天才明白过来。
examples.reading: tā tīng le bàntiān cái míngbai guòlai.
examples.translation: He listened for ages before it finally dawned on him.

examples.text: 他太累了，躺在沙发上就睡过去了。
examples.reading: tā tài lèi le, tǎng zài shāfā shang jiù shuì guòqu le.
examples.translation: He was so tired that he fell fast asleep as soon as he lay on the sofa.

examples.text: 因为太热，一位老人晕了过去。
examples.reading: yīnwèi tài rè, yí wèi lǎorén yūn le guòqu.
examples.translation: It was so hot that an old man fainted.

examples.text: 他的话让大家冷静了下来。
examples.reading: tā de huà ràng dàjiā lěngjìng le xiàlai.
examples.translation: His words calmed everyone down.

lessons.title: 得 + phrase: so … that (a verb phrase, a clause or a set phrase after 得)
lessons.summary: After a verb or adjective, 得 can introduce a whole verb phrase, a subject-predicate clause or a set phrase that describes the resulting state: 笑得说不出话来, 讲得大家都笑了, 说得一清二楚.
pattern: V / Adj + 得 + set phrase (一清二楚, 要命…)
body: At HSK 2 the part after 得 is a simple adjective (说得很好). Here it grows. It can be a verb phrase showing how extreme the state was: 他笑得说不出话来, 她累得连饭都不想吃了. It can be a full clause with its own subject: 老师讲得大家都笑了 (the teacher spoke so well that everyone laughed), 外面冷得我直发抖. It can also be a set phrase: 说得一清二楚 (perfectly clear), 忙得要命 (terribly busy).
All three forms mean so … that: the first part names the cause, and the part after 得 shows the result or how far things went. Nothing else can stand between the verb and 得.
The contrast example uses 地: 她轻轻地关上了门. 地 marks how an action is done and stands before the verb; 得 stands after the verb or adjective and introduces the resulting state.
A common mistake is to put 很 or 非常 straight after the verb instead of 得: 他笑很说不出话来 is wrong; keep 得.

examples.reading: tā xiào de shuō bu chū huà lai.
examples.translation: He laughed so hard he couldn't speak.

examples.text: 她累得连饭都不想吃了。
examples.reading: tā lèi de lián fàn dōu bù xiǎng chī le.
examples.translation: She was so tired she didn't even want to eat.

examples.reading: lǎoshī jiǎng de dàjiā dōu xiào le.
examples.translation: The teacher told it so well that everyone laughed.

examples.reading: wàimian lěng de wǒ zhí fādǒu.
examples.translation: It's so cold outside that I can't stop shivering.

examples.text: 他把事情的经过说得一清二楚。
examples.reading: tā bǎ shìqing de jīngguò shuō de yì qīng èr chǔ.
examples.translation: He explained exactly what had happened, perfectly clearly.

examples.reading: zhè jǐ tiān tā máng de yàomìng.
examples.translation: He has been terribly busy these days.

examples.reading: tā qīngqīng de guānshang le mén.
examples.translation: She closed the door gently.

lessons.title: 有着 and V有: formal 'has' and 'bears' (有着悠久的历史, 印有名字)
lessons.summary: 有着 + an abstract object says something has or contains a quality, history or feeling, in a formal style; V + 有 (印有, 写有, 画有) says something is printed, written or drawn on a surface.
pattern: place + V (印 / 写 / 画 / 刻) + 有 + object
body: 有着 (yǒuzhe) is a formal, written way to say has, mostly with abstract and weighty objects: history, friendship, feelings, dreams, differences. 这座城市有着两千多年的历史. The object usually has a modifier with 的; 有着 is not used for everyday things (say 我有一辆车, not 我有着一辆车), and it has no negative form with 没.
V + 有 says something is attached to or marked on a surface: 杯子上印有学校的名字, 信封上写有收信人的地址. The sentence starts with the place (杯子上, 信封上). It is formal, typical of notices and descriptions.
The contrast example uses V着: 台上坐着几位老师. V着 is the everyday sentence of existence (HSK 2–3) and works with any posture or placement verb; V有 is formal and used for writing, printing and similar marks.
A common mistake is to use 有着 with a concrete, simple object or with a number alone: 他有着两个哥哥 sounds wrong; say 他有两个哥哥.

examples.text: 这座城市有着两千多年的历史。
examples.reading: zhè zuò chéngshì yǒuzhe liǎng qiān duō nián de lìshǐ.
examples.translation: This city has a history of more than two thousand years.

examples.text: 这两个人之间有着很深的感情。
examples.reading: zhè liǎng ge rén zhījiān yǒuzhe hěn shēn de gǎnqíng.
examples.translation: There is a deep bond between these two people.

examples.text: 每个人都有着自己的梦想。
examples.reading: měi ge rén dōu yǒuzhe zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
examples.translation: Everyone has a dream of their own.

examples.text: 杯子上印有学校的名字。
examples.reading: bēizi shang yìn yǒu xuéxiào de míngzi.
examples.translation: The school's name is printed on the cup.

examples.text: 信封上写有收信人的地址。
examples.reading: xìnfēng shang xiě yǒu shōuxìnrén de dìzhǐ.
examples.translation: The recipient's address is written on the envelope.

examples.reading: tái shang zuò zhe jǐ wèi lǎoshī.
examples.translation: Several teachers are sitting on the stage.

lessons.title: 把 + O + 一 + V (a quick gesture) and 把 + O1 + V + O2
lessons.summary: 把 + O + 一 + V describes a quick, sudden movement, usually followed by what happens next; 把 + O1 + V + O2 lets the verb keep a second object, such as the person told or the part removed.
pattern: S + 把 + O + 一 + V，(就) + result
S + 把 + O1 + V (了) + O2
body: In 把 + O + 一 + V, the 一 makes the verb a short, sudden act, often a gesture: 他把门一关 (he shut the door, just like that), 妈妈把眼睛一瞪, 他把手一挥. The verb is a bare single verb with no 了, and the sentence almost always goes on to say what followed: 他把手一挥，大家就安静了.

In 把 + O1 + V + O2, the verb still has an object after it. O2 can be the person who receives something (把这件事告诉了经理, 把这个好消息告诉大家) or the part or result affected (把橘子剥了皮, she peeled the orange). O1 is what is handled; O2 completes the verb.
The contrast example uses 在: 请把车停在门口. This is the basic 把 sentence with a place after the verb (HSK 3), where the object ends up in a place; 在 is not a second object.
A common mistake is to add 了 to the quick-gesture form: 他把门一关了 is wrong; the 一 already marks the action as instant.

examples.text: 他把门一关，就躺到了床上。
examples.reading: tā bǎ mén yì guān, jiù tǎng dào le chuáng shang.
examples.translation: He shut the door and lay down on the bed.

examples.text: 妈妈把眼睛一瞪，孩子马上不说话了。
examples.reading: māma bǎ yǎnjing yí dèng, háizi mǎshàng bù shuōhuà le.
examples.translation: Mum just glared, and the child fell silent at once.

examples.text: 他把手一挥，大家就安静了。
examples.reading: tā bǎ shǒu yì huī, dàjiā jiù ānjìng le.
examples.translation: He gave a wave of his hand and everyone went quiet.

examples.text: 我已经把这件事告诉了经理。
examples.reading: wǒ yǐjīng bǎ zhè jiàn shì gàosu le jīnglǐ.
examples.translation: I've already told the manager about this.

examples.text: 你把这个好消息告诉大家吧。
examples.reading: nǐ bǎ zhège hǎo xiāoxi gàosu dàjiā ba.
examples.translation: Go and tell everyone the good news.

examples.text: 妈妈把橘子剥了皮，递给我。
examples.reading: māma bǎ júzi bāo le pí, dì gěi wǒ.
examples.translation: Mum peeled the orange and handed it to me.

examples.reading: qǐng bǎ chē tíng zài ménkǒu.
examples.translation: Please park the car at the entrance.

lessons.title: Serial verbs with cause, contrast or condition: 生病没来, 有钱不花, 有问题问我
lessons.summary: Two verb phrases can follow each other with no linking word and still mean cause (生病没来), contrast (有车不开) or condition (有问题可以问我); context gives the relation.
pattern: V1 (cause) + V2 (result): 生病没来上课
有 + N + 不 + V (contrast): 有车不开
有 + N + V2 (condition): 有问题问我
body: At HSK 2 two verbs in a row mean purpose or means (坐地铁去机场). Here the same structure carries other relations. Cause: 他有事没来开会 (he had something on, so he didn't come). Contrast: 她有车不开 (she has a car but doesn't drive it), 他借了钱不还 (he borrowed money and won't pay it back). Condition: 你有问题可以随时问我 (if you have questions, ask me), 有空来我家玩儿吧.
No 因为, 但是 or 如果 is needed; the order of events and the meaning of the verbs show the relation. The first verb phrase comes first in time or logic, so the two parts cannot swap.
The contrast example uses the basic serial pattern: 他坐地铁去机场. The first verb is the means and the second the purpose; there is no cause, contrast or condition.
A common mistake is to add a comma and a conjunction where the short form is natural, or to reverse the order: 他没来开会有事 is wrong.

examples.text: 你有问题可以随时问我。
examples.reading: nǐ yǒu wèntí kěyǐ suíshí wèn wǒ.
examples.translation: If you have any questions, you can ask me at any time.

examples.text: 她有车不开，每天骑自行车上班。
examples.reading: tā yǒu chē bù kāi, měi tiān qí zìxíngchē shàngbān.
examples.translation: She has a car but doesn't drive it; she cycles to work every day.

examples.reading: tā yǒu shì méi lái kāihuì.
examples.translation: He had something on, so he didn't come to the meeting.

examples.reading: yǒu kòng lái wǒ jiā wánr ba.
examples.translation: Come over to my place when you have time.

examples.reading: tā jiè le qián bù huán.
examples.translation: He borrowed money and won't pay it back.

examples.reading: tā zuò dìtiě qù jīchǎng.
examples.translation: He takes the underground to the airport.

lessons.title: A + Adj + B + amount: comparing without 比 (他大我三岁)
lessons.summary: With a short adjective such as 大, 小, 高, 早 or 晚, Chinese can compare without 比 by putting B right after the adjective and the exact difference at the end: 哥哥大我三岁.
pattern: A + 早 / 晚 + B + amount + V
body: The usual comparison is A 比 B + Adj + amount: 哥哥比我大三岁. A shorter pattern drops 比 and puts B straight after the adjective: 哥哥大我三岁 (my brother is three years older than me), 我高他五厘米, 弟弟小我两岁. With 早 and 晚 a verb phrase can follow: 他早我一年进公司, 妹妹晚我两年上大学.

The pattern works only with a few one-syllable adjectives of age, size, height or time (大, 小, 高, 矮, 早, 晚), and the amount at the end is required: 他大我 alone is not a sentence. B is usually a person or a pronoun.
The contrast example uses 比: 这个房间比那个大十平方米. With 比, B comes before the adjective; in the short pattern B comes after it. Do not use both at once.
A common mistake is to mix the two patterns: 他比大我三岁 is wrong; say 他比我大三岁 or 他大我三岁.

examples.reading: gēge dà wǒ sān suì.
examples.translation: My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ gāo tā wǔ límǐ.
examples.translation: I'm five centimetres taller than him.

examples.reading: tā zǎo wǒ yì nián jìn gōngsī.
examples.translation: He joined the company a year before me.

examples.reading: mèimei wǎn wǒ liǎng nián shàng dàxué.
examples.translation: My younger sister started university two years after me.

examples.reading: dìdi xiǎo wǒ liǎng suì.
examples.translation: My younger brother is two years younger than me.

examples.text: 这个房间比那个大十平方米。
examples.reading: zhège fángjiān bǐ nàge dà shí píngfāngmǐ.
examples.translation: This room is ten square metres bigger than that one.

lessons.title: 被 / 叫 / 让 + agent + 给 + V: passive sentences with 给
lessons.summary: In a colloquial passive sentence, 给 can stand right before the verb after 被, 叫 or 让 and the agent: 我的自行车让人给偷了; it stresses what happened to the subject.
pattern: subject + 被 / 叫 / 让 + agent + 给 + V + 了 / complement
body: Spoken passive sentences often add 给 just before the verb: 我的自行车让人给偷了, 那个杯子叫弟弟给打碎了, 衣服让雨给淋湿了. The meaning is the same as without 给, but 给 makes it sound more colloquial and stresses the effect on the subject, usually something unwelcome. The verb still needs something after it, such as 了 or a complement (打碎了, 拿走了).
被 can be used with or without an agent, but 叫 and 让 always need one: 杯子让弟弟给打碎了 is fine, 杯子让给打碎了 is not. Use 人 when you do not know who did it: 让人给偷了.
The contrast example uses 把: 他的话把妈妈给气哭了. 给 can also stand before the verb in a 把 sentence. There the subject is the cause or doer and the object after 把 is affected, the reverse of a passive.
A common mistake is to drop the agent after 叫 or 让, or to end with a bare verb: 自行车被人给偷 is unfinished; add 了.

examples.text: 我的自行车让人给偷了。
examples.reading: wǒ de zìxíngchē ràng rén gěi tōu le.
examples.translation: My bike got stolen.

examples.text: 那个杯子叫弟弟给打碎了。
examples.reading: nàge bēizi jiào dìdi gěi dǎsuì le.
examples.translation: That cup got broken by my little brother.

examples.text: 这件事被他给说出去了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì bèi tā gěi shuō chūqu le.
examples.translation: He let this slip to other people.

examples.reading: yīfu ràng yǔ gěi lín shī le.
examples.translation: My clothes got soaked by the rain.

examples.reading: nà běn shū bèi shéi gěi ná zǒu le?
examples.translation: Who took that book away?

examples.text: 他的话把妈妈给气哭了。
examples.reading: tā de huà bǎ māma gěi qì kū le.
examples.translation: What he said made Mum so upset she cried.

lessons.title: ……，便……: and then, straight away (formal 就)
lessons.summary: 便 in the second clause says the next action follows at once or naturally from the first; it is a more written, formal word for 就.
body: 便 (biàn) is an adverb that stands before the verb of the second part and says one thing follows the other directly: 他放下行李，便出去找朋友了, 她说完这句话，便离开了会场. It works like 就 but sounds more written; stories and reports use it often. Like 就, it can close an 一…… frame (一到冬天，这里便很少有人来) or a condition with 只要 (只要你多练习，便能说得流利).
便 is an adverb, so it goes after the subject of the second clause, never before it: 看完信，她便明白了一切, not 便她明白了.
The contrast example uses 然后: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影. 然后 is a linking word for the next step in a plan, often after 先, and it can stand before the subject; 便 stresses that the second action follows at once.
A common mistake is to pair 便 with 只有: 只有……才 is fixed, so 只有你多练习，便能…… is wrong; use 只要 with 便.

examples.text: 他放下行李，便出去找朋友了。
examples.reading: tā fàngxià xíngli, biàn chūqu zhǎo péngyou le.
examples.translation: He put down his bags and went straight out to see his friends.

examples.text: 她说完这句话，便离开了会场。
examples.reading: tā shuō wán zhè jù huà, biàn líkāi le huìchǎng.
examples.translation: Having said this, she left the hall.

examples.text: 一到冬天，这里便很少有人来。
examples.reading: yí dào dōngtiān, zhèlǐ biàn hěn shǎo yǒu rén lái.
examples.translation: Once winter comes, hardly anyone comes here.

examples.text: 只要你多练习，便能说得流利。
examples.reading: zhǐyào nǐ duō liànxí, biàn néng shuō de liúlì.
examples.translation: As long as you practise a lot, you will speak fluently.

examples.text: 看完信，她便明白了一切。
examples.reading: kàn wán xìn, tā biàn míngbai le yíqiè.
examples.translation: After reading the letter, she understood everything.

examples.text: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影。
examples.reading: wǒmen xiān chīfàn, ránhòu qù kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: We'll eat first and then go to the cinema.

lessons.title: 或是……，或是……: either … or … (in statements)
lessons.summary: 或是……，或是…… lists two possible actions or choices in a statement, a more formal version of 或者……，或者……; questions use 还是 instead.
pattern: S + 或是 + V1，或是 + V2
body: 或是 (huòshì) means or, like 或者, with a slightly more formal tone. Repeated at the head of two clauses it says one or the other happens: 周末我或是在家看书，或是去公园散步. It can also join two phrases once: 你可以发邮件或是打电话告诉我. The two choices are equal, so they can usually change places.
或是 belongs to statements. In a question that asks the listener to choose, use 还是: 你到底去还是不去? That is the contrast example: 还是 asks, 或是 states the options.
The two parts of 或是……，或是…… should be parallel, with the same kind of phrase after each 或是 (two verb phrases, or two people: 或是你去办，或是我去办).
A common mistake is to use 或是 in a choice question: 你喝茶或是喝咖啡? is wrong when you ask someone to choose; say 你喝茶还是喝咖啡?

examples.text: 周末我或是在家看书，或是去公园散步。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ huòshì zài jiā kàn shū, huòshì qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.translation: At weekends I either read at home or go for a walk in the park.

examples.text: 遇到不懂的词，可以问老师或是查词典。
examples.reading: yùdào bù dǒng de cí, kěyǐ wèn lǎoshī huòshì chá cídiǎn.
examples.translation: When you meet a word you don't know, you can ask the teacher or look it up in a dictionary.

examples.text: 你可以发邮件或是打电话告诉我。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ fā yóujiàn huòshì dǎ diànhuà gàosu wǒ.
examples.translation: You can let me know by email or by phone.

examples.text: 这件事或是你去办，或是我去办。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì huòshì nǐ qù bàn, huòshì wǒ qù bàn.
examples.translation: Either you deal with this or I do.

examples.reading: nǐ dàodǐ qù háishi bú qù?
examples.translation: So are you going or not?

lessons.title: 一旦……就…… (once …) and 假如……（就）…… (if, supposing)
lessons.summary: 一旦……就…… says that once something happens, a consequence follows; 假如…… sets up a supposition, real or imagined, with 就 or a question in the second clause.
body: 一旦 (yídàn) means once or if ever: it introduces an event that may or may not happen and stresses that, once it does, the result follows and is hard to undo: 一旦做了决定，他就不会改变, 机会一旦错过，就不会再来了. The second clause usually has 就.

假如 (jiǎrú) means if or supposing, a slightly more formal 如果. It can introduce a real possibility (假如明天下雨，运动会就改到下周) or an imagined one (假如你能回到过去，你最想做什么?). 就 is common but can be left out, especially when the second clause is a question or has 会 or 不可能 (假如没有你的帮助，我不可能这么快完成).
The contrast example uses 只要: 只要你有时间，就来参加吧. 只要 states a sufficient condition (as long as), not a supposition or a risk. Like 一旦 and 假如 it pairs with 就; 只有 pairs with 才, so 只有……就 is wrong.
A common mistake is to use 一旦 for something that has already happened: say 因为他做了决定, not 一旦他做了决定 about a past fact.

examples.text: 一旦做了决定，他就不会改变。
examples.reading: yídàn zuò le juédìng, tā jiù bú huì gǎibiàn.
examples.translation: Once he has made a decision, he won't change it.

examples.text: 这种病一旦发现，就要马上治疗。
examples.reading: zhè zhǒng bìng yídàn fāxiàn, jiù yào mǎshàng zhìliáo.
examples.translation: If this illness is found, it must be treated at once.

examples.text: 机会一旦错过，就不会再来了。
examples.reading: jīhuì yídàn cuòguò, jiù bú huì zài lái le.
examples.translation: Once you miss a chance, it won't come again.

examples.text: 假如明天下雨，运动会就改到下周。
examples.reading: jiǎrú míngtiān xià yǔ, yùndònghuì jiù gǎi dào xià zhōu.
examples.translation: If it rains tomorrow, the sports day will be moved to next week.

examples.text: 假如你能回到过去，你最想做什么？
examples.reading: jiǎrú nǐ néng huí dào guòqù, nǐ zuì xiǎng zuò shénme?
examples.translation: If you could go back in time, what would you most want to do?

examples.text: 假如没有你的帮助，我不可能这么快完成。
examples.reading: jiǎrú méiyǒu nǐ de bāngzhù, wǒ bù kěnéng zhème kuài wánchéng.
examples.translation: Without your help, I could never have finished so quickly.

examples.text: 只要你有时间，就来参加吧。
examples.reading: zhǐyào nǐ yǒu shíjiān, jiù lái cānjiā ba.
examples.translation: As long as you have time, do come along.

lessons.title: 万一 (in case) and 要不然 / 不然 (otherwise)
lessons.summary: 万一…… raises an unlikely, usually unwelcome possibility (in case …); ……，要不然/不然…… says what will or would happen otherwise.
pattern: clause，要不然 / 不然 + (S) + (就) + result
body: 万一 (wànyī, literally one in ten thousand) introduces a possibility that is unlikely and usually unwelcome: 万一下雨，我们就在家看电影. It is common in advice and in questions about what to do: 多带点儿钱吧，万一不够怎么办? The second clause often has 就.

要不然 and its shorter form 不然 mean otherwise, or else. The first clause says what to do or what happened; the second, after 要不然 or 不然, says the result if that were not so: 快走吧，要不然就赶不上火车了, 你最好穿件外套，不然会感冒的. After a past fact it means otherwise … would have: 幸亏你提醒我，要不然我就忘了.
The contrast example uses 既然: 既然你已经决定了，就去做吧. 既然 (since, now that) starts from a fact both people accept, while 万一 imagines something that has not happened and probably will not.
A common mistake is to use 然后 for otherwise: 快走吧，然后就赶不上火车了 says the opposite of what you mean.

examples.text: 万一下雨，我们就在家看电影。
examples.reading: wànyī xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù zài jiā kàn diànyǐng.
examples.translation: If it happens to rain, we'll stay home and watch a film.

examples.text: 多带点儿钱吧，万一不够怎么办？
examples.reading: duō dài diǎnr qián ba, wànyī bú gòu zěnme bàn?
examples.translation: Take some extra money; what if it isn't enough?

examples.text: 万一有什么问题，你就给我打电话。
examples.reading: wànyī yǒu shénme wèntí, nǐ jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: If anything goes wrong, give me a call.

examples.text: 快走吧，要不然就赶不上火车了。
examples.reading: kuài zǒu ba, yàobùrán jiù gǎn bu shàng huǒchē le.
examples.translation: Let's hurry, or we'll miss the train.

examples.text: 你最好穿件外套，不然会感冒的。
examples.reading: nǐ zuìhǎo chuān jiàn wàitào, bùrán huì gǎnmào de.
examples.translation: You'd better put on a coat, or you'll catch a cold.

examples.text: 幸亏你提醒我，要不然我就忘了。
examples.reading: xìngkuī nǐ tíxǐng wǒ, yàobùrán wǒ jiù wàng le.
examples.translation: Luckily you reminded me, otherwise I'd have forgotten.

examples.text: 既然你已经决定了，就去做吧。
examples.reading: jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, jiù qù zuò ba.
examples.translation: Since you've made up your mind, go ahead and do it.

lessons.title: ……，因而…… (and so) and ……，可见…… (which shows that)
lessons.summary: 因而 opens the second clause with a result that follows from the first, in a formal style; 可见 opens a conclusion drawn from the facts in the first clause.
body: 因而 (yīn'ér) means therefore, and so. It stands at the start of the second clause and introduces the result of the cause in the first: 他每天坚持锻炼，因而身体一直很好. It is more formal than 所以 and, unlike 所以, it is not paired with 因为 at the start of the sentence.

可见 (kějiàn) means which shows that, so clearly. The first clause states a fact; the second, after 可见, is the speaker's conclusion from it: 大家都来参加了，可见这个活动很受欢迎. The direction is fact, then conclusion, not cause, then result.
The contrast example uses 因为……所以……: 因为路上堵车，所以他迟到了. 因为 opens the cause clause at the front; 因而 and 可见 only open the second clause, so 因而路上堵车 is wrong.
A common mistake is to put the reason after 可见: 他没来，可见他生病了 is a conclusion; if you know he is ill, say 他生病了，所以没来.

examples.text: 他每天坚持锻炼，因而身体一直很好。
examples.reading: tā měi tiān jiānchí duànliàn, yīn'ér shēntǐ yìzhí hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He exercises every day, so he has always been healthy.

examples.text: 这里交通方便，因而房价比较高。
examples.reading: zhèlǐ jiāotōng fāngbiàn, yīn'ér fángjià bǐjiào gāo.
examples.translation: Transport here is convenient, so house prices are fairly high.

examples.text: 他的发音很标准，因而大家都以为他是中国人。
examples.reading: tā de fāyīn hěn biāozhǔn, yīn'ér dàjiā dōu yǐwéi tā shì Zhōngguórén.
examples.translation: His pronunciation is so standard that everyone takes him for Chinese.

examples.text: 这么简单的题他都做错了，可见他没认真看。
examples.reading: zhème jiǎndān de tí tā dōu zuò cuò le, kějiàn tā méi rènzhēn kàn.
examples.translation: He got even such an easy question wrong, so clearly he didn't read it carefully.

examples.text: 大家都来参加了，可见这个活动很受欢迎。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu lái cānjiā le, kějiàn zhège huódòng hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.translation: Everybody came, which shows how popular the event is.

examples.text: 因为路上堵车，所以他迟到了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lù shang dǔchē, suǒyǐ tā chídào le.
examples.translation: He was late because of the traffic jam.

lessons.title: 哪怕……，也……: even if …, still …
lessons.summary: 哪怕 introduces an extreme or unlikely supposition, and 也 in the second clause says the result does not change: 哪怕下大雨，他也会去跑步.
pattern: 哪怕 + extreme supposition，S + 也 + V
body: 哪怕 (nǎpà) means even if. It sets up a supposition, often an extreme one, and the second clause says the outcome stays the same; 也 stands before its verb: 哪怕只有一点儿希望，我们也不能放弃. It is close to 即使 and 就算 but more colloquial and more emphatic. 再 + adjective often follows it: 哪怕再忙.
The subject can come before 哪怕 when both clauses share it: 我哪怕不睡觉，也要把这本书看完. 也 stays after any time word or subject in the second clause: 她每天也要给妈妈打个电话.
The contrast example uses 虽然……但是……: 虽然这家饭馆有点儿贵，但是我们还是常来. 虽然 concedes a real fact (the restaurant really is expensive); 哪怕 imagines a case that may not happen. So 哪怕 does not go with 但是.
A common mistake is to use 就 instead of 也: 哪怕下雨，他就会去 is wrong; even if needs 也 (or 都).

examples.text: 哪怕下大雨，他也会去跑步。
examples.reading: nǎpà xià dà yǔ, tā yě huì qù pǎobù.
examples.translation: Even if it pours with rain, he'll still go running.

examples.text: 哪怕只有一点儿希望，我们也不能放弃。
examples.reading: nǎpà zhǐ yǒu yìdiǎnr xīwàng, wǒmen yě bù néng fàngqì.
examples.translation: Even if there's only a sliver of hope, we can't give up.

examples.text: 哪怕再忙，她每天也要给妈妈打个电话。
examples.reading: nǎpà zài máng, tā měi tiān yě yào gěi māma dǎ ge diànhuà.
examples.translation: However busy she is, she calls her mother every day.

examples.text: 我哪怕不睡觉，也要把这本书看完。
examples.reading: wǒ nǎpà bú shuìjiào, yě yào bǎ zhè běn shū kàn wán.
examples.translation: I'll finish this book even if I have to stay up all night.

examples.text: 哪怕别人都不理解，我也要坚持自己的选择。
examples.reading: nǎpà biérén dōu bù lǐjiě, wǒ yě yào jiānchí zìjǐ de xuǎnzé.
examples.translation: Even if nobody else understands, I'll stick to my choice.

examples.text: 虽然这家饭馆有点儿贵，但是我们还是常来。
examples.reading: suīrán zhè jiā fànguǎn yǒudiǎnr guì, dànshì wǒmen háishi cháng lái.
examples.translation: Although this restaurant is a bit expensive, we still come here often.

lessons.title: 不但不……，反而…… (not only not …, but instead) and 不是只……，还…… (not only … but also)
lessons.summary: 不但不 / 不但没有……，反而…… says that instead of the expected result, the opposite happened; 不是（只）……，还 / 还是…… says that something goes further than the first part claims.
pattern: S + 不但不 / 不但没(有) + V，反而 + opposite
S + 不是 (只) + A，还 / 还是 + B
body: 不但不 (or 不但没有 for a past event) denies the expected result, and 反而 (fǎn'ér, on the contrary) gives the opposite one: 吃了药，他的病不但没有好，反而更重了, 我帮了他，他不但不感谢，反而生气了. 反而 is an adverb, so it goes after any subject in the second clause.

不是……，还…… goes in the other direction: the first part is true but not the whole story, and the second adds more. It is most natural with 只 or 光: 她不是只会唱歌，还会跳舞. When the second part names what the person also is, it takes 还是, that is 还 plus 是 (hái shì, also is): 我爸爸不是只会工作，还是个很好的厨师.

The contrast example uses 不但……而且……: 他不但会做饭，而且做得很好吃. 而且 adds something in the same direction; 反而 is used only when the second part goes against what the first led you to expect, and only after a negative 不但不 / 不但没.
A common mistake is to use 反而 after a positive 不但: 他不但会做饭，反而做得很好吃 is wrong; use 而且.

examples.text: 吃了药，他的病不但没有好，反而更重了。
examples.reading: chī le yào, tā de bìng búdàn méiyǒu hǎo, fǎn'ér gèng zhòng le.
examples.translation: After taking the medicine, his illness didn't get better; it got worse.

examples.text: 我帮了他，他不但不感谢，反而生气了。
examples.reading: wǒ bāng le tā, tā búdàn bù gǎnxiè, fǎn'ér shēngqì le.
examples.translation: I helped him, and instead of thanking me he got angry.

examples.text: 雨不但没停，反而越下越大了。
examples.reading: yǔ búdàn méi tíng, fǎn'ér yuè xià yuè dà le.
examples.translation: Far from stopping, the rain got heavier and heavier.

examples.text: 她不是只会唱歌，还会跳舞。
examples.reading: tā bú shì zhǐ huì chànggē, hái huì tiàowǔ.
examples.translation: She doesn't only sing; she can dance too.

examples.text: 我爸爸不是只会工作，还是个很好的厨师。
examples.reading: wǒ bàba bú shì zhǐ huì gōngzuò, hái shì ge hěn hǎo de chúshī.
examples.translation: My dad doesn't just know how to work; he's also a really good cook.

examples.text: 他不但会做饭，而且做得很好吃。
examples.reading: tā búdàn huì zuòfàn, érqiě zuò de hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: He can not only cook, but cook really well.

lessons.title: ……，为的是……: the reason is to …, all in order to …
lessons.summary: 为的是 opens the second clause and states the purpose of the action in the first: 我们提前出发，为的是避开早高峰.
body: 为的是 (wèi de shì) means the purpose is, it is in order to. First you say what someone does, then, after a comma, 为的是 gives the goal: 他每天早起，为的是能多学一会儿, 妈妈这么做，为的是让你少走弯路. It puts weight on the purpose, often to explain or justify an action.
为的是 is fixed: the three syllables do not change (not 为得是 or 为了是), and it always opens the second clause, after the action.
The contrast example uses 为了: 为了能早点儿到，我们打了一辆车. 为了 usually comes first and gives the purpose before the action; 为的是 comes second. So 为的是 does not start a sentence.
A common mistake is to use 因为是 for purpose: 因为 gives a reason (a cause), 为的是 a goal.

examples.text: 他每天早起，为的是能多学一会儿。
examples.reading: tā měi tiān zǎo qǐ, wèi de shì néng duō xué yíhuìr.
examples.translation: He gets up early every day so that he can study a bit longer.

examples.text: 我们提前出发，为的是避开早高峰。
examples.reading: wǒmen tíqián chūfā, wèi de shì bìkāi zǎo gāofēng.
examples.translation: We set off early to avoid the morning rush hour.

examples.text: 妈妈这么做，为的是让你少走弯路。
examples.reading: māma zhème zuò, wèi de shì ràng nǐ shǎo zǒu wānlù.
examples.translation: Mum does this to spare you unnecessary trouble.

examples.text: 他拼命工作，为的是给家人更好的生活。
examples.reading: tā pīnmìng gōngzuò, wèi de shì gěi jiārén gèng hǎo de shēnghuó.
examples.translation: He works himself hard to give his family a better life.

examples.text: 他一直在存钱，为的是买一套自己的房子。
examples.reading: tā yìzhí zài cún qián, wèi de shì mǎi yí tào zìjǐ de fángzi.
examples.translation: He has been saving all along so that he can buy a flat of his own.

examples.text: 为了能早点儿到，我们打了一辆车。
examples.reading: wèile néng zǎo diǎnr dào, wǒmen dǎ le yí liàng chē.
examples.translation: We took a taxi so we could get there a bit earlier.

lessons.title: Compressed sentences: 没有……就没有……, 不……不……, 再……也……
lessons.summary: Some two-clause meanings are packed into one short sentence: 没有A就没有B (without A there is no B), 不A不B (unless A, not B), and 再Adj也V (however …, still …).
pattern: 没有 + A + (，) 就没有 + B
不 + V1 + 不 + V2 / 不行
再 + Adj / V + 也 + V
body: A compressed sentence (紧缩复句) is a complex sentence with the comma and most linking words removed. 没有A就没有B says A is the condition for B: 没有大家的帮助，就没有我今天的成功, 没有你就没有这个家.

不A不B is a double negative meaning unless A, not B, or if not A, then not B: 他不做完作业不睡觉 (he won't go to bed until his homework is done). 不V不行 means must: 这个问题不解决不行. The set phrase 不见不散 (see you there, we wait until we meet) is built the same way.

再A也B means however A, still B: 工作再忙也要按时吃饭, 这件衣服再便宜我也不买. 再 here does not mean again; with an adjective it means no matter how. The contrast example uses 就 alone: 你想去就去吧, a compressed condition (if you want to go, go), where 就 joins the two verbs with no 再 or 也.
A common mistake is to replace the second 不 with 没: 他不做完作业没睡觉 is wrong; the frame is 不……不…… .

examples.text: 没有大家的帮助，就没有我今天的成功。
examples.reading: méiyǒu dàjiā de bāngzhù, jiù méiyǒu wǒ jīntiān de chénggōng.
examples.translation: Without everyone's help, I wouldn't be where I am today.

examples.reading: méiyǒu nǐ jiù méiyǒu zhège jiā.
examples.translation: Without you, this family wouldn't exist.

examples.reading: zhège wèntí bù jiějué bù xíng.
examples.translation: This problem has to be solved.

examples.reading: tā bú zuò wán zuòyè bú shuìjiào.
examples.translation: He doesn't go to bed until he's finished his homework.

examples.text: 工作再忙也要按时吃饭。
examples.reading: gōngzuò zài máng yě yào ànshí chīfàn.
examples.translation: However busy work gets, you must eat at regular times.

examples.text: 这件衣服再便宜我也不买。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu zài piányi wǒ yě bù mǎi.
examples.translation: However cheap this piece of clothing is, I won't buy it.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng qù jiù qù ba.
examples.translation: If you want to go, go ahead.

lessons.title: Class prefixes 超- 多- 反- 无- 亚- 准-: building new words from the front
lessons.summary: Six productive prefixes attach to a word to build a new one: 超 beyond, 多 multi-, 反 counter-, 无 without, 亚 sub- and 准 quasi- or to-be.
pattern: 超 / 多 / 反 / 无 / 亚 / 准 + noun or adjective
超高速, 多功能, 反作用, 无条件, 亚健康, 准妈妈
body: A class prefix is a bound piece that goes in front of many different words and gives them all the same extra meaning. 超 (chāo) means beyond or super-: 超高速, 超大型, 超低价. 多 (duō) means multi-: 多功能, 多媒体. 反 (fǎn) means counter- or anti-: 反作用, 反科学. 无 (wú) means without or non-: 无条件, 无线. 亚 (yà) means sub- or second to: 亚健康, 亚热带. 准 (zhǔn) means quasi- or soon-to-be: 准妈妈, 准新娘, 准大学生.
The new word behaves like an ordinary noun or adjective: 一列超高速列车, 处于亚健康状态, 起反作用. The prefix cannot stand alone in this meaning, so it is learned as part of the word.

The contrast example uses the suffix 化 (城市化). A suffix attaches to the back of a word; these six pieces attach to the front. A common mistake is to treat 无 like the verb 没有 and put it before a full phrase: say 无条件 or 没有任何条件, not 无任何的条件 in everyday speech.

examples.reading: zhè shì yí liè chāo gāosù lièchē.
examples.translation: This is an ultra-high-speed train.

examples.reading: zhè kuǎn shǒujī shì duōgōngnéng de.
examples.translation: This phone is multifunctional.

examples.text: 我们无条件支持你的决定。
examples.reading: wǒmen wútiáojiàn zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
examples.translation: We support your decision unconditionally.

examples.text: 太多的批评可能会起反作用。
examples.reading: tài duō de pīpíng kěnéng huì qǐ fǎnzuòyòng.
examples.translation: Too much criticism may have the opposite effect.

examples.text: 很多年轻人处于亚健康状态。
examples.reading: hěn duō niánqīngrén chǔyú yàjiànkāng zhuàngtài.
examples.translation: Many young people are in a state of sub-health.

examples.text: 她是一位准妈妈，下个月就要生孩子了。
examples.reading: tā shì yí wèi zhǔn māma, xià ge yuè jiù yào shēng háizi le.
examples.translation: She is a mother-to-be; her baby is due next month.

examples.text: 这个国家的城市化程度很高。
examples.reading: zhège guójiā de chéngshìhuà chéngdù hěn gāo.
examples.translation: This country is highly urbanised.

lessons.title: Class suffixes -化 -式 -型 -性: -ization, style, type and -ness
lessons.summary: Four productive suffixes attach to the back of a word: 化 turns it into a process, 式 names a style, 型 names a type or model, and 性 names a quality.
pattern: noun / adjective + 化 / 式 / 型 / 性
现代化, 中式, 新型, 代表性
body: 化 (huà) is like -ize or -ization: 现代化, 自动化, 城市化, 国际化. It can end a sentence with 了 for a change of state (越来越现代化了). 式 (shì) means style or form: 中式, 西式, 开放式. 型 (xíng) means type or model: 新型, 大型, 外向型. 性 (xìng) means a quality or property, like -ness or -ity: 代表性, 知识性, 重要性, 可能性.
式 and 型 make words that describe a noun (开放式厨房, 新型汽车); 性 makes an abstract noun that often follows 有 or takes 很强 (很有代表性, 知识性很强).

The contrast example uses the prefix 超 in 超大型: a word can carry a prefix in front and a suffix behind at the same time. A common mistake is to mix up 型 and 性, which sound alike: 重要性 (importance), not 重要型.

examples.text: 这个城市越来越现代化了。
examples.reading: zhège chéngshì yuèláiyuè xiàndàihuà le.
examples.translation: This city is becoming more and more modern.

examples.text: 这家工厂已经实现了自动化。
examples.reading: zhè jiā gōngchǎng yǐjīng shíxiàn le zìdònghuà.
examples.translation: This factory has already become fully automated.

examples.text: 很多人喜欢开放式厨房。
examples.reading: hěn duō rén xǐhuan kāifàngshì chúfáng.
examples.translation: Many people like open-plan kitchens.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le yí liàng xīnxíng qìchē.
examples.translation: He bought a new-model car.

examples.reading: tā shì ge wàixiàngxíng de rén.
examples.translation: She is the outgoing type.

examples.reading: zhège lìzi hěn yǒu dàibiǎoxìng.
examples.translation: This example is very representative.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū de zhīshixìng hěn qiáng.
examples.translation: This book is very informative.

examples.reading: zhè shì yí zuò chāo dàxíng shāngchǎng.
examples.translation: This is a huge shopping mall.

lessons.title: 人家: others, a person already mentioned, or a coy I
lessons.summary: 人家 is a pronoun that can mean other people, a particular person you point to, or, in a coy or complaining voice, the speaker herself.
body: 人家 (rénjia, second syllable light) has three uses. It can mean other people, like 别人: 人家都不怕. It can point to a particular person, usually to hold them up as a model or to defend them; then a name or pronoun often follows it directly: 人家小王, 人家他. In a coy or complaining voice the speaker can call herself 人家: 人家等了你半天.
Only 人家 can stand right before a name or 他 in apposition; 别人小王 or 大家他 are wrong. Read 人家 with stress on rén and a light jia; rénjiā with a full tone is the noun household (那户人家).

The contrast example uses 自己, the reflexive: 你得自己想办法 means you find a way by yourself. 人家 points away to someone else, 自己 points back to the subject. A common mistake is to swap the characters: 家人 means family members, not others.

examples.text: 人家小王每天都来得很早，你呢？
examples.reading: rénjia Xiǎo Wáng měi tiān dōu lái de hěn zǎo, nǐ ne?
examples.translation: Xiao Wang gets here early every day. What about you?

examples.reading: nǐ kàn rénjia háizi, duō dǒngshì!
examples.translation: Look at other people’s kids, so well-behaved!

examples.text: 人家等了你半天，你怎么才来？
examples.reading: rénjia děng le nǐ bàntiān, nǐ zěnme cái lái?
examples.translation: I waited ages for you. Why are you only coming now?

examples.text: 人家他都不着急，你着急什么？
examples.reading: rénjia tā dōu bù zháojí, nǐ zháojí shénme?
examples.translation: He himself is not worried, so what are you worried about?

examples.text: 人家都下班了，你怎么还在加班？
examples.reading: rénjia dōu xiàbān le, nǐ zěnme hái zài jiābān?
examples.translation: Everyone else has gone home. Why are you still working late?

examples.text: 人家李老师六十多岁了，还天天学英语。
examples.reading: rénjia Lǐ lǎoshī liùshí duō suì le, hái tiāntiān xué Yīngyǔ.
examples.translation: Look at Mr Li: he is over sixty and still studies English every day.

examples.text: 这个问题你得自己想办法。
examples.reading: zhège wèntí nǐ děi zìjǐ xiǎng bànfǎ.
examples.translation: You have to sort this problem out yourself.

lessons.title: Specific measure words 串 滴 枝 扇 卷: bunches, drops, stems, doors and rolls
lessons.summary: Some nouns take their own measure word: 串 for bunches and strings, 滴 for drops, 枝 for stems, 扇 for doors and windows, 卷 juǎn for rolls and 卷 juàn for volumes.
pattern: 一 + 串 / 滴 / 枝 / 扇 / 卷 + noun
数词 + 卷 (juàn) for volumes of a book
body: 串 (chuàn) counts things on a string or in a bunch: 一串钥匙, 一串葡萄. 滴 (dī) counts drops: 几滴水, 一滴眼泪. 枝 (zhī) counts flowers on a stem and branches: 一枝玫瑰; 支 is also seen with flowers. 扇 (shàn) counts doors and windows: 一扇门, 那扇窗户.
卷 has two readings. As juǎn it counts things rolled up: 两卷卫生纸, 一卷胶带. As juàn it counts volumes of a long work: 这部小说有三卷, 第一卷.
The contrast example uses 把, the measure word for things you hold by a handle (一把伞). A common mistake is to use 个 or 张 for everything: say 一扇门, not 一张门, and 一串钥匙, not 一个钥匙 for a whole bunch.

examples.reading: tā shǒu li ná zhe yí chuàn yàoshi.
examples.translation: He is holding a bunch of keys.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shang yǒu jǐ dī shuǐ.
examples.translation: There are a few drops of water on the table.

examples.reading: tā sòng gěi tā yì zhī hóng méigui.
examples.translation: He gave her a red rose.

examples.reading: qǐng bǎ nà shàn chuānghu guānshang.
examples.translation: Please close that window.

examples.text: 我去超市买了两卷卫生纸。
examples.reading: wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi le liǎng juǎn wèishēngzhǐ.
examples.translation: I went to the supermarket and bought two rolls of toilet paper.

examples.reading: zhè bù xiǎoshuō yígòng yǒu sān juàn.
examples.translation: This novel has three volumes in all.

examples.reading: wǒ jiè le péngyou yì bǎ sǎn.
examples.translation: I borrowed an umbrella from a friend.

lessons.title: 番: a round of effort, as in 打扫了一番 and 一番努力
lessons.summary: 番 counts a thorough round of an action, usually as 一番 after the verb or before a noun such as 努力 or 话.
pattern: 经过 / 做了 + 一番 + N
body: 番 (fān) is a verbal measure word for one round of an action that takes some effort or time: 打扫了一番, 讨论了一番, 打量了我一番. It nearly always appears as 一番, and it sounds a little formal and thorough. 一番 also goes before abstract nouns: 一番努力, 一番话, 一番心意.
With a pronoun object the order is V + 了 + pronoun + 一番 (打量了我一番); with 把 the object moves forward (把房间打扫了一番).

The contrast example uses 遍, which counts complete run-throughs and takes any number: 读了好几遍, 看了三遍. 番 does not count repetitions like this, so 看了三番 is wrong. A common mistake is to use 番 with a quick one-off action such as 看一番 for a glance; use 看一眼.

examples.text: 他把房间认真打扫了一番。
examples.reading: tā bǎ fángjiān rènzhēn dǎsǎo le yì fān.
examples.translation: He gave the room a thorough clean.

examples.text: 经过一番努力，他终于考上了大学。
examples.reading: jīngguò yì fān nǔlì, tā zhōngyú kǎoshang le dàxué.
examples.translation: After a lot of hard work, he finally got into university.

examples.reading: tā shàngxià dǎliang le wǒ yì fān.
examples.translation: She looked me up and down.

examples.text: 大家坐下来好好讨论了一番。
examples.reading: dàjiā zuò xiàlái hǎohǎo tǎolùn le yì fān.
examples.translation: Everyone sat down and talked it over properly.

examples.reading: lǎoshī bǎ tā biǎoyáng le yì fān.
examples.translation: The teacher gave him a round of praise.

examples.text: 他把这封信读了好几遍。
examples.reading: tā bǎ zhè fēng xìn dú le hǎo jǐ biàn.
examples.translation: He read the letter over several times.

lessons.title: Degree adverbs 特, 异常 and 较为: very, unusually and relatively
lessons.summary: 特 is a casual very, 异常 means unusually or extraordinarily, and 较为 means relatively in formal style.
body: 特 (tè) is a spoken short form of 特别, very: 特好吃, 特高兴. 异常 (yìcháng) means unusually, beyond the normal, and is formal: 异常寒冷, 异常安静. 较为 (jiàowéi) means relatively or fairly and is also formal; it likes two-syllable adjectives: 较为简单, 较为方便.
All three go directly before the adjective and are not combined with another degree word: 较为很简单 is wrong. 异常 can also be an adjective meaning abnormal (情况异常).
The contrast example uses 特地, on purpose, which shares the character 特 but is a manner adverb before a verb: 他特地来机场接我. A common mistake is to write 特地好吃 for very tasty; the degree word is 特.

examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn de jiǎozi tè hǎochī.
examples.translation: This shop's dumplings are really tasty.

examples.reading: jīnnián dōngtiān yìcháng hánlěng.
examples.translation: This winter is unusually cold.

examples.reading: zhège fāngfǎ jiàowéi jiǎndān.
examples.translation: This method is relatively simple.

examples.reading: kǎochǎng li yìcháng ānjìng.
examples.translation: The exam hall is extraordinarily quiet.

examples.reading: tā érzi tè cōngming.
examples.translation: His son is really clever.

examples.text: 这一带的交通较为方便。
examples.reading: zhè yídài de jiāotōng jiàowéi fāngbiàn.
examples.translation: Transport in this area is fairly convenient.

examples.reading: tā tèdì lái jīchǎng jiē wǒ.
examples.translation: He came to the airport specially to pick me up.

lessons.title: Scope adverbs 净, 一同 and 大都: nothing but, together and mostly
lessons.summary: 净 means nothing but or all, often with a critical tone; 一同 means together; 大都 means mostly, for the most part.
pattern: plural subject + 大都 + V / Adj
body: 净 (jìng) is spoken and says that everything is of one kind, often something the speaker dislikes: 他净说些没用的话, 地上净是树叶. 一同 (yìtóng) means together, a more formal 一起: 我们一同去, 他和朋友一同参加了比赛. 大都 (dàdōu) means mostly or for the most part: 来的大都是年轻人, 这里的房子大都很旧.
大都 needs a plural or collective subject, since it talks about most members of a group. 一同 needs two or more people doing the same thing.

The contrast example uses 只, which limits an amount (只有十块钱). 净 does not limit an amount; it says the whole scene is filled with X. A common mistake is to read 大都 as dàdū, the noun for a big city; the adverb is dàdōu.

examples.reading: tā jìng shuō xiē méiyòng de huà.
examples.translation: He talks nothing but nonsense.

examples.reading: dì shang jìng shì shùyè.
examples.translation: The ground is covered in nothing but leaves.

examples.text: 我们一同去机场接他吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen yìtóng qù jīchǎng jiē tā ba.
examples.translation: Let's go to the airport together to meet him.

examples.text: 李老师带着学生一同参观了博物馆。
examples.reading: Lǐ lǎoshī dài zhe xuésheng yìtóng cānguān le bówùguǎn.
examples.translation: Mr Li took the students round the museum with him.

examples.text: 来参加会议的大都是年轻人。
examples.reading: lái cānjiā huìyì de dàdōu shì niánqīngrén.
examples.translation: Most of the people at the meeting are young.

examples.reading: zhèli de fángzi dàdōu hěn jiù.
examples.translation: Most of the houses here are old.

examples.reading: wǒ shēn shang zhǐ yǒu shí kuài qián.
examples.translation: I only have ten yuan on me.

lessons.title: Time adverbs 一时, 不时, 仍旧, 依旧, 一向: for a moment, now and then, still, always
lessons.summary: 一时 means for the moment, 不时 means from time to time, 仍旧 and 依旧 mean still as before, and 一向 means always, all along.
pattern: 仍旧 / 依旧 / 一向 + V / Adj
body: 一时 (yìshí) means at that moment or for a short while, and often goes with a failure: 一时想不起来, 一时不知道怎么回答. 不时 (bùshí) means every now and then: 不时看看手表. 仍旧 (réngjiù) and 依旧 (yījiù) both mean still, unchanged from before, and are formal synonyms: 这里仍旧没有变化, 他依旧每天跑步.
一向 (yíxiàng) means always, consistently, from the past up to now, and describes habits or character: 他一向很准时. It is not used for one single event.

The contrast example uses 已经, already, which marks that something has happened (会议已经结束了). The adverbs here describe how long or how often, not completion. A common mistake is 他一向去了北京: 一向 cannot go with a one-off completed action; use 已经 or 一直 instead.

examples.text: 他问得太突然，我一时不知道怎么回答。
examples.reading: tā wèn de tài tūrán, wǒ yìshí bù zhīdào zěnme huídá.
examples.translation: He asked so suddenly that for a moment I didn’t know how to answer.

examples.reading: tā bùshí kànkan shǒubiǎo.
examples.translation: She glances at her watch every now and then.

examples.text: 十年过去了，这里仍旧没有什么变化。
examples.reading: shí nián guòqù le, zhèli réngjiù méiyǒu shénme biànhuà.
examples.translation: Ten years have passed, and this place has still hardly changed.

examples.text: 我爷爷八十岁了，依旧每天跑步。
examples.reading: wǒ yéye bāshí suì le, yījiù měi tiān pǎobù.
examples.translation: My grandfather is eighty and still goes running every day.

examples.reading: tā yíxiàng hěn zhǔnshí.
examples.translation: He has always been punctual.

examples.text: 我到的时候，会议已经结束了。
examples.reading: wǒ dào de shíhou, huìyì yǐjīng jiéshù le.
examples.translation: By the time I arrived, the meeting had already ended.

lessons.title: Frequency adverbs 一再 and 再三: again and again
lessons.summary: 一再 and 再三 both mean again and again; 再三 can also follow a verb, as in 考虑再三.
body: 一再 (yízài) and 再三 (zàisān) mean repeatedly, time after time. Before a verb they are often interchangeable: 一再提醒, 再三考虑. 一再 is also common for something unwanted that keeps happening: 他一再迟到.
Only 再三 can come after the verb, mostly after verbs of thinking: 考虑再三, 犹豫再三. 考虑一再 is wrong.

The contrast example uses 又, which says something happened once more in the past (她又穿了那件红裙子). 一再 and 再三 stress many repetitions; 又 marks one more. A common mistake is to use 再 for a past repetition: 他昨天再迟到了 is wrong, it must be 又.

examples.text: 我一再提醒他，他还是忘了。
examples.reading: wǒ yízài tíxǐng tā, tā háishi wàng le.
examples.translation: I reminded him again and again, but he still forgot.

examples.text: 他再三考虑，最后同意了。
examples.reading: tā zàisān kǎolǜ, zuìhòu tóngyì le.
examples.translation: He thought it over many times and finally agreed.

examples.text: 他一再迟到，老板很生气。
examples.reading: tā yízài chídào, lǎobǎn hěn shēngqì.
examples.translation: He keeps turning up late, and the boss is angry.

examples.text: 妈妈再三让我注意安全。
examples.reading: māma zàisān ràng wǒ zhùyì ānquán.
examples.translation: Mum told me again and again to be careful.

examples.text: 我考虑再三，决定不去了。
examples.reading: wǒ kǎolǜ zàisān, juédìng bú qù le.
examples.translation: After thinking it over and over, I decided not to go.

examples.reading: tā yòu chuān le nà jiàn hóng qúnzi.
examples.translation: She is wearing that red dress again.

lessons.title: Manner adverbs 不禁, 赶忙, 特地, 特意, 偷偷: involuntarily, hurriedly, on purpose, secretly
lessons.summary: 不禁 means unable to help doing, 赶忙 means hurriedly, 特地 and 特意 mean specially or on purpose, and 偷偷 means secretly.
pattern: 赶忙 / 特地 / 特意 + V
body: 不禁 (bùjīn) means one cannot help it, for an emotional reaction: 不禁哭了起来, 不禁笑了. 赶忙 (gǎnmáng) means hurriedly, at once, in reaction to something: 赶忙坐好. 特地 (tèdì) and 特意 (tèyì) mean specially, for one purpose, and are interchangeable: 特地赶来, 特意为你准备的. 偷偷 (tōutōu) means secretly, so that nobody sees, often with 地: 偷偷地吃了一块糖.
不禁 and 赶忙 describe past reactions and usually come in the second clause after a cause (听到这个消息, 看到老师进来). 特地 and 特意 need a person with an intention.

The contrast example uses 忽然, suddenly, which describes an event with no intention behind it (天忽然下起了大雨); the sky cannot do something 特地. A common mistake is to use 不禁 for a deliberate action: 他不禁买了一本书 is wrong unless the buying was an urge he could not resist.

examples.text: 看着孩子的照片，她不禁笑了。
examples.reading: kàn zhe háizi de zhàopiàn, tā bùjīn xiào le.
examples.translation: Looking at her child’s photo, she couldn’t help smiling.

examples.text: 看到老师进来，学生们赶忙坐好。
examples.reading: kàndào lǎoshī jìnlái, xuéshengmen gǎnmáng zuòhǎo.
examples.translation: When they saw the teacher come in, the students quickly sat down properly.

examples.text: 他特地赶来参加我的婚礼。
examples.reading: tā tèdì gǎnlái cānjiā wǒ de hūnlǐ.
examples.translation: He made the trip specially to come to my wedding.

examples.text: 这些菜是妈妈特意做的。
examples.reading: zhèxiē cài shì māma tèyì zuò de.
examples.translation: Mum made these dishes specially.

examples.text: 孩子偷偷地吃了一块糖。
examples.reading: háizi tōutōu de chī le yí kuài táng.
examples.translation: The child secretly ate a sweet.

examples.reading: tiān hūrán xià qǐ le dàyǔ.
examples.translation: It suddenly started to pour.

lessons.title: 未必: not necessarily
lessons.summary: 未必 means not necessarily; it softens a negative judgement and goes before the verb, an adjective or 是, 会 and 能.
pattern: 未必 + 是 / 会 / 能 + ...
body: 未必 (wèibì) means not necessarily, may not be: 贵的东西未必都好, 他说的话未必是真的. It is a judgement about likelihood, softer than a flat 不, and it is often used to disagree politely.
未必 goes before the verb or adjective and before modal verbs: 未必会下雨, 未必能找到. It is close to 不一定 in meaning.

The contrast example uses 不必, need not, which talks about necessity, not likelihood: 你不必亲自去. 未必亲自去 would be a guess about what you will do, which does not fit a piece of advice. A common mistake is to confuse the two because both start with a negative: 不必 cannot go before 会 or 能, and 未必 does not give advice.

examples.reading: guì de dōngxi wèibì dōu hǎo.
examples.translation: Expensive things aren't necessarily all good.

examples.reading: tā shuō de huà wèibì shì zhēn de.
examples.translation: What he says is not necessarily true.

examples.reading: zhège bànfǎ wèibì xíng de tōng.
examples.translation: This method may not work.

examples.reading: míngtiān wèibì huì xiàyǔ.
examples.translation: It won't necessarily rain tomorrow.

examples.text: 你去了也未必能找到他。
examples.reading: nǐ qù le yě wèibì néng zhǎodào tā.
examples.translation: Even if you go, you won't necessarily find him.

examples.text: 这点小事，你不必亲自去。
examples.reading: zhè diǎn xiǎoshì, nǐ búbì qīnzì qù.
examples.translation: You needn’t go yourself for such a small matter.

lessons.title: Modal adverbs 恰好, 倒是, 干脆, 明明, 总算: just right, actually, simply, clearly, at last
lessons.summary: 恰好 means just at the right moment, 倒是 concedes or contrasts, 干脆 means simply or just, 明明 means obviously, and 总算 means at long last.
pattern: A + 倒是 + Adj, 就是 / 可是 B
明明 + V, 却 / 可 ...; 干脆 + V
body: 恰好 (qiàhǎo) means by chance, just right; it goes before a verb or after 得: 恰好碰到他, 你来得恰好. 总算 (zǒngsuàn) means at long last, after waiting or trouble: 他总算来了. 干脆 (gāncuì) means simply, just, to cut it short; it often suggests a quick decision: 干脆别去了.

明明 (míngmíng) means obviously, clearly, and is followed by a clause that goes against it: 他明明知道, 却说不知道. 倒是 (dàoshì) concedes one good point before a but (样子倒是不错, 就是太贵了), or says something is easier said than done (你说得倒是容易).

The contrast example uses 果然, as expected (他果然很喜欢). 果然 confirms a prediction; 恰好 is about chance timing and 总算 about relief after waiting. A common mistake is to use 明明 without the contrasting clause: 他明明知道 alone sounds unfinished.

examples.text: 你来得恰好，我正要找你。
examples.reading: nǐ lái de qiàhǎo, wǒ zhèng yào zhǎo nǐ.
examples.translation: You’ve come at just the right time; I was about to look for you.

examples.text: 他明明知道，却说不知道。
examples.reading: tā míngmíng zhīdào, què shuō bù zhīdào.
examples.translation: He clearly knows, but he says he does not.

examples.text: 等了三个小时，他总算来了。
examples.reading: děng le sān ge xiǎoshí, tā zǒngsuàn lái le.
examples.translation: After three hours of waiting, he finally came.

examples.reading: zhème máfan, gāncuì bié qù le.
examples.translation: It's such a hassle, let's just not go.

examples.text: 这件衣服样子倒是不错，就是太贵了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu yàngzi dàoshì búcuò, jiùshì tài guì le.
examples.translation: The style of this jacket is nice enough, but it is too expensive.

examples.text: 你说得倒是容易，你来试试！
examples.reading: nǐ shuō de dàoshì róngyì, nǐ lái shìshi!
examples.translation: That's easy for you to say. You try it!

examples.text: 我猜他会喜欢这个礼物，他果然很喜欢。
examples.reading: wǒ cāi tā huì xǐhuan zhège lǐwù, tā guǒrán hěn xǐhuan.
examples.translation: I guessed he would like the present, and sure enough he loved it.

lessons.title: 于: formal at or in for time and place
lessons.summary: 于 is a formal preposition for time and place, used after verbs such as 生, 位, 建 and 毕业 or before a time word.
pattern: V (生 / 位 / 建 / 毕业) + 于 + time / place
body: 于 (yú) is the written, formal counterpart of 在 for time and place. It often fuses with a one-syllable verb in front of it: 生于上海 (born in), 位于市中心 (located in), 建于上个世纪 (built in), 毕业于北京大学 (graduated from). It can also introduce a time before the verb in notices: 会议将于明天上午九点开始.
The phrase is short and fixed: verb plus 于 plus the time or place, with no 了 between them.

The contrast example uses 从, from, which marks a starting point (我是从北京来的). 于 does not mean from with a verb of coming: 于北京来 is wrong. A common mistake is to use 于 in casual speech, for example 我于家吃饭; in conversation say 我在家吃饭.

examples.text: 我爷爷生于一个小山村。
examples.reading: wǒ yéye shēng yú yí ge xiǎo shāncūn.
examples.translation: My grandfather was born in a small mountain village.

examples.reading: zhè jiā gōngsī wèiyú shì zhōngxīn.
examples.translation: This company is located in the city centre.

examples.text: 会议将于明天上午九点开始。
examples.reading: huìyì jiāng yú míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The meeting will begin at nine tomorrow morning.

examples.reading: zhè zuò qiáo jiàn yú shàng ge shìjì.
examples.translation: This bridge was built in the last century.

examples.reading: tā bìyè yú Běijīng Dàxué.
examples.translation: He graduated from Peking University.

examples.reading: wǒ shì cóng Běijīng lái de.
examples.translation: I come from Beijing.

lessons.title: 至于: as for, turning to a new topic
lessons.summary: 至于 introduces a new, related topic at the start of a clause, meaning as for or as to.
body: 至于 (zhìyú) begins a clause and moves the talk to a second topic connected to the first: 我先去报名, 至于住哪儿, 以后再说. The topic after 至于 can be a noun (至于第二个, 至于小王) or a question phrase (至于住哪儿, 至于钱多钱少). Usually a first topic has already been dealt with, so 至于 rarely opens a conversation.
The verb phrase 不至于 means it will not go so far as, for example 他不至于不来吧. That is the same characters used in a different way.

The contrast example uses 关于, about, which makes a phrase in front of a noun (一个关于环境保护的会). 关于 tells what something is about; 至于 switches topics between clauses, so 一个至于环境保护的会 is wrong. A common mistake is to confuse 至于 with 由于 (because) or 终于 (finally), which look alike.

examples.text: 我先去报名，至于住哪儿，以后再说。
examples.reading: wǒ xiān qù bàomíng, zhìyú zhù nǎr, yǐhòu zài shuō.
examples.translation: I'll sign up first; as for where to stay, we can sort that out later.

examples.text: 第一个问题我同意，至于第二个，我还要想想。
examples.reading: dì-yī ge wèntí wǒ tóngyì, zhìyú dì-èr ge, wǒ hái yào xiǎngxiang.
examples.translation: I agree on the first point; as for the second, I need to think it over.

examples.text: 他只关心工作，至于钱多钱少，他不在乎。
examples.reading: tā zhǐ guānxīn gōngzuò, zhìyú qián duō qián shǎo, tā bú zàihu.
examples.translation: He only cares about the work; as for how much he earns, he does not mind.

examples.text: 大家都同意了，至于小王，我明天再问他。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu tóngyì le, zhìyú Xiǎo Wáng, wǒ míngtiān zài wèn tā.
examples.translation: Everyone has agreed; as for Xiao Wang, I'll ask him tomorrow.

examples.text: 我们开了一个关于环境保护的会。
examples.reading: wǒmen kāi le yí ge guānyú huánjìng bǎohù de huì.
examples.translation: We held a meeting about environmental protection.

lessons.title: 因: formal because of, and 因……而
lessons.summary: 因 is a formal one-syllable preposition meaning because of; it goes before the cause and the verb follows, sometimes with 而.
pattern: A + 因 + B + 而 + V / Adj
body: 因 (yīn) is the written, compact form of 因为 used as a preposition: 比赛因下雨推迟了, 他因病没来上班. The cause right after 因 is often short, a noun or a verb phrase, and the whole sentence has one subject. In formal writing 因 combines with 而: 我们都因你而骄傲 (we are proud because of you).
Typical set phrases are 因病 (because of illness), 因故 (for some reason), 因事 (on business). 因 alone does not start a full clause with its own subject in speech; there 因为 is used.

The contrast example uses 因此, therefore, which comes at the start of the result clause (他身体不好，因此很少出门). 因 goes before the cause; 因此 goes before the result. A common mistake is to pair 因 with 所以 inside one short clause, as in 他因病所以没来.

examples.reading: bǐsài yīn xiàyǔ tuīchí le.
examples.translation: The match was postponed because of rain.

examples.reading: tā yīn bìng méi lái shàngbān.
examples.translation: He didn't come to work because of illness.

examples.text: 这家商店因经营不善关门了。
examples.reading: zhè jiā shāngdiàn yīn jīngyíng búshàn guānmén le.
examples.translation: This shop closed down because it was badly run.

examples.reading: wǒmen dōu yīn nǐ ér jiāo'ào.
examples.translation: We are all proud of you.

examples.text: 小王因工作努力被评为优秀员工。
examples.reading: Xiǎo Wáng yīn gōngzuò nǔlì bèi píngwéi yōuxiù yuángōng.
examples.translation: Xiao Wang was named an outstanding employee for working hard.

examples.text: 他身体不好，因此很少出门。
examples.reading: tā shēntǐ bù hǎo, yīncǐ hěn shǎo chū mén.
examples.translation: His health is poor, so he seldom goes out.

lessons.title: 除……外: formal except for, apart from
lessons.summary: 除 is a formal preposition of exclusion; with 外 or 以外 it means except for (with 都) or apart from (with 还 or 也).
pattern: 除 + N / V + (以) 外, 都 ...
除 + N / V + (以) 外, 还 / 也 ...
body: 除 (chú) is the formal short form of 除了. It usually pairs with 外 or 以外 at the end of the phrase: 除他以外, 除星期一外. With 都 or a negative later in the sentence it excludes: 除他以外, 大家都到了 (everyone except him). With 还 or 也 it adds: 除卖书外, 还卖咖啡 (besides books, coffee too).
The set phrase 除此之外 means apart from this, and it opens a clause. 除 is more formal than 除了, and 除 without 外 or 以外 is rare in speech.
The contrast example uses 除非, unless or only if (除非你去，我才去). 除 leaves something out of a group; 除非 sets a condition. A common mistake is to drop 都 or 还: 除他以外大家到了 sounds incomplete.

examples.reading: chú tā yǐwài, dàjiā dōu dào le.
examples.translation: Everyone is here except him.

examples.text: 除星期一外，每天都有航班。
examples.reading: chú xīngqīyī wài, měi tiān dōu yǒu hángbān.
examples.translation: There are flights every day except Monday.

examples.text: 这家店除卖书外，还卖咖啡。
examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn chú mài shū wài, hái mài kāfēi.
examples.translation: Besides books, this shop also sells coffee.

examples.text: 除此之外，还有一个问题。
examples.reading: chú cǐ zhī wài, hái yǒu yí ge wèntí.
examples.translation: Apart from this, there is one more problem.

examples.text: 除小李外，没有人会说日语。
examples.reading: chú Xiǎo Lǐ wài, méiyǒu rén huì shuō Rìyǔ.
examples.translation: Apart from Xiao Li, nobody speaks Japanese.

examples.reading: chúfēi nǐ qù, wǒ cái qù.
examples.translation: I'll go only if you go.

lessons.title: 不料: unexpectedly, to one’s surprise
lessons.summary: 不料 opens the second clause and says that what happened was not what the speaker expected.
pattern: A (本想 / 以为 ...), 不料 B
body: 不料 (búliào) means unexpectedly, little did one know. It begins the second clause, after a first clause that states a plan or an expectation, often with 本想, 本来, 以为 or 刚: 我本想早点回家, 不料路上堵车了. The subject of the second clause comes after 不料: 不料他笑了.
The surprise is often, but not always, unwelcome. 不料 belongs to written and storytelling style; in speech 没想到 is common.

The contrast example uses 却, but, an adverb that stands after the subject (他却不高兴). 不料 stands at the head of its clause, so 他不料不高兴 is wrong. A common mistake is to use 不料 in the first clause or with no expectation set up before it.

examples.text: 我本想早点回家，不料路上堵车了。
examples.reading: wǒ běn xiǎng zǎo diǎn huí jiā, búliào lù shang dǔchē le.
examples.translation: I meant to get home early, but unexpectedly there was a traffic jam.

examples.text: 他以为考试很容易，不料一道题也不会做。
examples.reading: tā yǐwéi kǎoshì hěn róngyì, búliào yí dào tí yě bú huì zuò.
examples.translation: He thought the exam would be easy, but to his surprise he couldn't answer a single question.

examples.text: 我们刚出门，不料下起了大雨。
examples.reading: wǒmen gāng chū mén, búliào xià qǐ le dàyǔ.
examples.translation: We had just left when, out of nowhere, it started to pour.

examples.text: 本来以为他会生气，不料他笑了。
examples.reading: běnlái yǐwéi tā huì shēngqì, búliào tā xiào le.
examples.translation: I thought he would be angry, but to my surprise he laughed.

examples.text: 我好心提醒他，他却不高兴。
examples.reading: wǒ hǎoxīn tíxǐng tā, tā què bù gāoxìng.
examples.translation: I reminded him out of kindness, but he got annoyed.

lessons.title: 所: 所 + V before a noun, and the passive 为……所
lessons.summary: 所 is a formal particle placed before a verb to mark what is done or known, as in 我所知道的, and in the written passive 为 A 所 V.
pattern: A + 所 + V + 的 (+ N)
B + 为 + A + 所 + V
body: 所 (suǒ) goes between a subject and a transitive verb in a 的 phrase, and points to the thing that the verb acts on: 我所知道的情况 (the situation as I know it), 大家所说的 (what everyone says), 我们所做的一切 (everything we do). The sentence is still correct without 所, but 所 makes it more formal and clear.
In writing, 为 + doer + 所 + verb is a passive: 他的意见为大家所接受 (his view was accepted by everyone), 她为这首歌所感动. The verb here is usually two syllables and has no 了.

The contrast example uses 被, the everyday passive marker (那封信被风吹走了). 被 can take 了 and stands alone; 所 needs 为 in the passive. A common mistake is to put 所 before an adjective or an intransitive verb: 我所高兴的 is wrong.

examples.text: 这就是我所知道的情况。
examples.reading: zhè jiù shì wǒ suǒ zhīdào de qíngkuàng.
examples.translation: This is the situation as far as I know it.

examples.reading: dàjiā suǒ shuō de dōu shì zhēnhuà.
examples.translation: What everyone said is the truth.

examples.text: 他的意见为大家所接受。
examples.reading: tā de yìjiàn wéi dàjiā suǒ jiēshòu.
examples.translation: His opinion was accepted by everyone.

examples.text: 我们所做的一切都是为了孩子。
examples.reading: wǒmen suǒ zuò de yíqiè dōu shì wèile háizi.
examples.translation: Everything we do is for the children.

examples.text: 她深深地为这首歌所感动。
examples.reading: tā shēnshēn de wéi zhè shǒu gē suǒ gǎndòng.
examples.translation: She was deeply moved by this song.

examples.reading: nà fēng xìn bèi fēng chuīzǒu le.
examples.translation: The letter was blown away by the wind.

lessons.title: Modal particles 啦 and 嘛: lively 了 and the obvious or coaxing 嘛
lessons.summary: 啦 is a lively blend of 了 and 啊 at the end of a sentence; 嘛 marks something as obvious or softens a request.
body: 啦 (la) is 了 and 啊 run together. It marks a change or completion with excitement or warmth: 你回来啦, 我们终于到家啦. Use it where 了 would fit at the end of the sentence.
嘛 (ma) has two jobs. After a reason it says this is obvious, so you should accept it: 他还是个孩子嘛, 别生他的气. After a request it coaxes or presses: 有话就说嘛, 你就帮帮我嘛. It is never a question particle.

The contrast example uses 吗, which turns a statement into a yes-no question (你周末有空吗？). 嘛 sounds the same but asks nothing, so 你周末有空嘛？ is wrong as a question. A common mistake is to write 嘛 for 吗 in questions, or to use 啦 where no 了 could stand.

examples.reading: nǐ huílái la!
examples.translation: Oh, you’re back!

examples.reading: wǒmen zhōngyú dào jiā la!
examples.translation: We're finally home!

examples.text: 他还是个孩子嘛，别生他的气。
examples.reading: tā hái shì ge háizi ma, bié shēng tā de qì.
examples.translation: He's only a child, after all; don't be angry with him.

examples.text: 有话就说嘛，别不好意思。
examples.reading: yǒu huà jiù shuō ma, bié bù hǎoyìsi.
examples.translation: If you've got something to say, just say it; don't be shy.

examples.reading: nǐ jiù bāngbang wǒ ma!
examples.translation: Oh, come on, just help me!

examples.reading: nǐ zhōumò yǒu kòng ma?
examples.translation: Are you free at the weekend?

lessons.title: 也好: it is just as well, and A也好，B也好 for whether A or B
lessons.summary: 也好 after a clause means it is just as well; repeated after two items, A也好, B也好, it means whether A or B, followed by 都.
pattern: A 也好, B 也好 (也罢), 都 ...
body: After a clause, 也好 (yě hǎo) accepts a situation as not bad after all: 下雨了，在家休息休息也好 (it is raining, so a rest at home is no bad thing). It often follows a less welcome event and looks on the bright side.
Repeated after two items, 也好 lists the cases and the next clause, usually with 都, says the result is the same in every case: 你去也好，不去也好，都告诉我一声. The second one can be 也罢: 大人也好，孩子也罢.

The contrast example uses the plain adverb 也, also (我妹妹也是老师), which goes before a verb. 也好 comes after a word or clause and closes it. A common mistake is to leave out 都 after the pair, as in 春天也好，秋天也好，这里很美, which sounds unfinished.

examples.text: 下雨了，在家休息休息也好。
examples.reading: xiàyǔ le, zài jiā xiūxi xiūxi yě hǎo.
examples.translation: It's raining, so a rest at home is no bad thing.

examples.text: 让他吃点苦也好，下次就记住了。
examples.reading: ràng tā chī diǎn kǔ yě hǎo, xià cì jiù jìzhù le.
examples.translation: It's just as well he suffers a bit; next time he'll remember.

examples.text: 大人也好，孩子也罢，都喜欢这部电影。
examples.reading: dàrén yě hǎo, háizi yě bà, dōu xǐhuan zhè bù diànyǐng.
examples.translation: Adults and children alike love this film.

examples.text: 你去也好，不去也好，都告诉我一声。
examples.reading: nǐ qù yě hǎo, bú qù yě hǎo, dōu gàosu wǒ yì shēng.
examples.translation: Whether you go or not, let me know either way.

examples.text: 春天也好，秋天也好，这里都很美。
examples.reading: chūntiān yě hǎo, qiūtiān yě hǎo, zhèli dōu hěn měi.
examples.translation: Spring or autumn, it is beautiful here.

examples.reading: wǒ mèimei yě shì lǎoshī.
examples.translation: My younger sister is a teacher too.

lessons.title: Four-character frames A这A那 and 左A右B: this and that, over and over
lessons.summary: A这A那 means doing A to all sorts of things, and 左A右B means doing the same action again and again from every side.
pattern: 左 + V1 + 右 + V2 (V1, V2 same or similar)
body: In A这A那 one verb is repeated with 这 and then 那: 买这买那 (buy this and that), 怕这怕那 (worry about everything), 问这问那 (ask about everything). It often carries a note of impatience. 这 always comes first.
In 左A右B the two verbs are the same or close in meaning, and the frame says the action was repeated many times, often without success: 左想右想 (think it over and over), 左看右看, 左挑右选. 左 always comes first.
The contrast example uses 左右 after a number, meaning about (三十岁左右). That 左右 is one word for an estimate, not a frame around a verb. A common mistake is to reverse the order: 买那买这 and 右看左看 are wrong.

examples.text: 她一进商场就买这买那。
examples.reading: tā yí jìn shāngchǎng jiù mǎi zhè mǎi nà.
examples.translation: As soon as she walks into a mall she buys this and that.

examples.reading: tā zuò shì zǒngshì pà zhè pà nà.
examples.translation: Whatever he does, he worries about everything.

examples.text: 别问这问那了，快去做饭吧！
examples.reading: bié wèn zhè wèn nà le, kuài qù zuò fàn ba!
examples.translation: Stop asking about everything and go and cook!

examples.text: 我左想右想，还是不明白。
examples.reading: wǒ zuǒ xiǎng yòu xiǎng, háishi bù míngbai.
examples.translation: I thought it over and over and still did not understand.

examples.text: 他左看右看，也没找到钥匙。
examples.reading: tā zuǒ kàn yòu kàn, yě méi zhǎodào yàoshi.
examples.translation: He looked everywhere but still could not find the keys.

examples.text: 她左挑右选，最后买了一件红的。
examples.reading: tā zuǒ tiāo yòu xuǎn, zuìhòu mǎi le yí jiàn hóng de.
examples.translation: She picked and chose for ages and in the end bought a red one.

examples.reading: tā kàn shàngqu sānshí suì zuǒyòu.
examples.translation: He looks about thirty.

lessons.title: Fixed phrases 好(不)容易, 那倒(也)是, 算了 and 得了
lessons.summary: 好容易 and 好不容易 both mean with great difficulty; 那倒(也)是 concedes a point; 算了 means forget it; 得了 means that is enough.
pattern: 好 (不) 容易 + 才 + V
body: 好容易 and 好不容易 (hǎo bù róngyì) mean the same thing, with great difficulty, even though one has 不. They come before the verb and usually take 才: 我好不容易才买到这张票, 他好容易才找到一份工作.

那倒是 and 那倒也是 (nà dào yě shì) concede the other person’s point: that is true, I suppose. 算了 (suàn le) drops a matter: forget it, let it go; at the end of a clause, 就算了 means then never mind. 得了 (dé le) stops someone: that will do, enough.

The contrast example uses 不过, but, which adds a reservation after a statement (菜不错，不过服务一般). The fixed phrases here react to a whole situation; 不过 links two clauses. A common mistake is to read 好容易 as very easy in this frame; with 才 it always means it was hard.

examples.text: 我好不容易才买到这张票。
examples.reading: wǒ hǎo bù róngyì cái mǎidào zhè zhāng piào.
examples.translation: I had a really hard time getting this ticket.

examples.text: 他好容易才找到一份工作。
examples.reading: tā hǎo róngyì cái zhǎodào yí fèn gōngzuò.
examples.translation: He finally found a job after a lot of trouble.

examples.text: 那倒也是，这么晚了，我们打车吧。
examples.reading: nà dào yě shì, zhème wǎn le, wǒmen dǎchē ba.
examples.translation: That's true; it's so late, let's take a taxi.

examples.text: 那倒是，他确实比我有经验。
examples.reading: nà dào shì, tā quèshí bǐ wǒ yǒu jīngyàn.
examples.translation: That's true, he really is more experienced than me.

examples.reading: suàn le, bié gēn tā chǎo le.
examples.translation: Forget it, don't argue with him.

examples.reading: dé le, nǐ jiù bié zài shuō le.
examples.translation: That's enough, stop talking.

examples.reading: nǐ yàoshi bù xiǎng qù, jiù suàn le.
examples.translation: If you don't want to go, never mind.

examples.text: 这家饭馆的菜不错，不过服务一般。
examples.reading: zhè jiā fànguǎn de cài búcuò, búguò fúwù yìbān.
examples.translation: The food in this restaurant is good, but the service is so-so.

lessons.title: Scattered here and there: A一+measure, B一+measure and 东一A，西一A
lessons.summary: Two place or time words each followed by 一 and a measure word describe things scattered about or constantly changing; 东一A，西一A is the fixed form with east and west.
pattern: A + 一 + measure, B + 一 + measure
东 + 一 + measure / V, 西 + 一 + measure / V
body: In A一+measure, B一+measure, A and B are places or times, and each is followed by one item: 这儿一棵，那儿一棵 (a tree here, a tree there), 桌上一张，地上一张. The frame paints things lying around without order, or, with times, ideas that keep changing: 今天一个主意，明天一个主意.
东一A，西一A is the fixed version with 东 and 西. It means here and there, bits and pieces, with no plan: 东一句，西一句 (a remark here, a remark there), 东一件，西一件, 东一下，西一下. 东 always comes first.

The contrast example uses 到处, everywhere (教室里到处都是书). 到处 simply says the whole place is full; the frames here paint the scattered pieces one by one. A common mistake is to reverse 东 and 西, as in 西一句，东一句.

examples.text: 他东一句，西一句，说得我都糊涂了。
examples.reading: tā dōng yí jù, xī yí jù, shuō de wǒ dōu hútu le.
examples.translation: He kept jumping from one thing to another until I was totally confused.

examples.text: 房间里东一件，西一件，到处是衣服。
examples.reading: fángjiān li dōng yí jiàn, xī yí jiàn, dàochù shì yīfu.
examples.translation: Clothes are lying all over the room, one here, one there.

examples.text: 他做事总是东一下，西一下，没有计划。
examples.reading: tā zuò shì zǒngshì dōng yí xià, xī yí xià, méiyǒu jìhuà.
examples.translation: He always does things in bits and pieces, with no plan.

examples.text: 院子里这儿一棵，那儿一棵，种了不少果树。
examples.reading: yuànzi li zhèr yì kē, nàr yì kē, zhòng le bù shǎo guǒshù.
examples.translation: Fruit trees are dotted all over the yard, one here, one there.

examples.text: 他今天一个主意，明天一个主意，谁也不知道他想干什么。
examples.reading: tā jīntiān yí ge zhǔyi, míngtiān yí ge zhǔyi, shéi yě bù zhīdào tā xiǎng gàn shénme.
examples.translation: He has one idea today and another tomorrow; nobody knows what he wants.

examples.text: 桌上一张，地上一张，全是他画的画。
examples.reading: zhuō shang yì zhāng, dì shang yì zhāng, quán shì tā huà de huà.
examples.translation: One on the desk, one on the floor: all of them are his drawings.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li dàochù dōu shì shū.
examples.translation: There are books everywhere in the classroom.

lessons.title: Time and turning points: 到……为止, 早不X晚不X and 不X不……，一X……
lessons.summary: 到……为止 marks an end point; 早(也)不X，晚(也)不X complains that something happened at the worst moment; 不X不……，一X…… says you only find out once you try.
pattern: 早 (也) 不 V, 晚 (也) 不 V, 偏偏 ...
不 V 不知道, 一 V + result
body: 到……为止 (dào ... wéizhǐ) means up to, until, as an end point: 到目前为止 (so far), 今天就到这儿为止 (that is all for today).
早(也)不X，晚(也)不X says it did not happen earlier and did not happen later, but at this very bad moment, and it is usually followed by 偏偏: 早不来，晚不来，他偏偏这时候来了. 也 may be added: 早也不坏，晚也不坏.

不X不知道，一X…… says you do not know until you try, and once you do, there is a surprise: 不看不知道，一看吓一跳. The contrast example uses 从……起, from a starting point (从下个月起). 为止 marks where something ends, 起 where it starts, so 从下个月为止 is wrong. A common mistake is to drop 偏偏 or the second half of these frames, which leaves them hanging.

examples.text: 到目前为止，报名的已经有五十人了。
examples.reading: dào mùqián wéizhǐ, bàomíng de yǐjīng yǒu wǔshí rén le.
examples.translation: So far, fifty people have signed up.

examples.text: 今天的课就到这儿为止吧。
examples.reading: jīntiān de kè jiù dào zhèr wéizhǐ ba.
examples.translation: Let's end today's class here.

examples.text: 早不来，晚不来，他偏偏这时候来了。
examples.reading: zǎo bù lái, wǎn bù lái, tā piānpiān zhè shíhou lái le.
examples.translation: Of all times, he had to turn up right now.

examples.text: 电脑早也不坏，晚也不坏，偏偏考试前坏了。
examples.reading: diànnǎo zǎo yě bú huài, wǎn yě bú huài, piānpiān kǎoshì qián huài le.
examples.translation: Of all times, the computer had to break down right before the exam.

examples.text: 不看不知道，一看吓一跳。
examples.reading: bú kàn bù zhīdào, yí kàn xià yí tiào.
examples.translation: You'd never guess until you look, and then it gives you a shock.

examples.text: 这道菜不吃不知道，一吃就忘不了。
examples.reading: zhè dào cài bù chī bù zhīdào, yì chī jiù wàng bu liǎo.
examples.translation: You can't imagine this dish until you try it, and then you never forget it.

examples.text: 从下个月起，每周只工作四天。
examples.reading: cóng xià ge yuè qǐ, měi zhōu zhǐ gōngzuò sì tiān.
examples.translation: Starting next month, we will only work four days a week.

lessons.title: Exclamations about people: 好你个X, 看把他X得, 瞧你X的 and X到Y头上来了
lessons.summary: These spoken frames react to a person: 好你个X scolds or teases, 看把他X得 and 瞧你X的 exclaim over how someone looks or feels, and X到Y头上来了 protests that a wrong has reached even Y.
pattern: 看 / 瞧 + 把 + person + Adj / V + 得
看 / 瞧 + 你 / 他 + Adj + 的; V + 到 + Y + 头上来了
